CMO:0000000.name: clinical measurement
CMO:0000000.def: A quantitative or qualitative value which is the result of an act of assessing a morphological or physiological state or property in a single individual or sample or a group of individuals or samples, based on direct observation or experimental manipulation.

CMO:0000001.name: cardiovascular measurement
CMO:0000001.def: Any value resulting from the quantification of a morphological or physiological parameter pertaining to the heart and/or blood vessels.

CMO:0000002.name: heart rate
CMO:0000002.def: The number of contractions of the cardiac ventricles per unit of time.

CMO:0000003.name: blood pressure measurement
CMO:0000003.def: Measurement of the pressure, or force per area, exerted by circulating blood against the walls of the blood vessels. The pressure is dependent on the energy of the heart action, elasticity of the vessel walls and volume and viscosity of the blood.

CMO:0000004.name: systolic blood pressure
CMO:0000004.def: The maximum arterial pressure within the cardiac cycle, i.e. at the point at which the heart is in its maximal state of contraction. This is the time when the blood is forced from the ventricles of the heart into the pulmonary artery and the aorta.

CMO:0000005.name: diastolic blood pressure
CMO:0000005.def: The minimum arterial pressure within the cardiac cycle, usually at the point at which the heart is in a state of relaxation and expansion. This is the time when the ventricles fill with blood.

CMO:0000006.name: left ventricular diastolic blood pressure
CMO:0000006.def: The minimum pressure in the heart left ventricle, usually at the point at which the heart is in a state of relaxation and expansion and the ventricles fill with blood.

CMO:0000007.name: left ventricular systolic blood pressure
CMO:0000007.def: Measurement of the pressure within the heart left ventricle at the point of maximal contraction, when the blood is forced from the left ventricle into the aorta.

CMO:0000008.name: calculated blood pressure
CMO:0000008.def: A blood pressure measurement which has been normalized or adjusted by a mathematical process or computation. Blood pressure is the pressure, or force per area, exerted by circulating blood against the walls of the blood vessels. The pressure is dependent on the energy of the heart action, elasticity of the vessel walls and volume and viscosity of the blood.

CMO:0000009.name: mean arterial blood pressure
CMO:0000009.def: The average blood pressure within an artery over a specified period of time. It is often calculated using the formula of one third systolic pressure plus two thirds diastolic pressure, or alternatively, using the formula diastolic pressure plus 1/3 of the difference between systolic pressure and  diastolic pressure (i.e. 1/3 pulse pressure).

CMO:0000010.name: developed blood pressure
CMO:0000010.def: A calculated value for the difference between the systolic blood pressure and the diastolic blood pressure at a given point in time when measured in an isolated organ or vessel under conditions where perfusion pressure or flow can be controlled.

CMO:0000011.name: whole body morphological measurement
CMO:0000011.def: Morphological measurement involving the entire body of an organism.

CMO:0000012.name: body weight
CMO:0000012.def: The heaviness or degree to which an entire organism's body is drawn to the earth by gravity.

CMO:0000013.name: body length
CMO:0000013.def: A measurement of the longest dimension of a body, typically between two distinct ends of the body.

CMO:0000014.name: hip circumference
CMO:0000014.def: Total distance around the body at the region of the body lateral to and including the hip joint or coxa.

CMO:0000015.name: body temperature
CMO:0000015.def: The level of heat in an organism.

CMO:0000016.name: heart morphological measurement
CMO:0000016.def: A measurement of the physical form or structure of the heart, the chambered, muscular organ in vertebrates that pumps blood received from the veins into the arteries, thereby maintaining the flow of blood through the entire circulatory system.

CMO:0000017.name: heart weight
CMO:0000017.def: The heaviness of the heart (the central cardiac muscle which maintains the circulation of the blood) or the degree to which it is drawn to the earth by gravity.

CMO:0000018.name: left ventricular developed pressure
CMO:0000018.def: A calculated measurement of the difference between the systolic pressure and the diastolic pressure in the heart left ventricle at a given point in time in an isolated organ or vessel under conditions where perfusion pressure or flow can be controlled.

CMO:0000019.name: proximal hind limb circumference
CMO:0000019.def: Distance around the upper portion of the hind limb closest to the body, typically taken at the area of maximum girth.

CMO:0000020.name: waist to hip ratio (WHR)
CMO:0000020.def: The circumference of the body at the level of the navel divided by the circumference at the widest point around the buttocks, often used to assess distribution of sub-cutaneous and intra-abdominal adipose tissue.

CMO:0000021.name: body morphological measurement
CMO:0000021.def: Measurement of the structure or forms of the entire body or parts of the body of an organism.

CMO:0000022.name: calculated body morphological measurement
CMO:0000022.def: This is a measurement of the physical form or structure of an organism which has been normalized, adjusted or derived by a mathematical process or computation.

CMO:0000023.name: blood chemistry measurement
CMO:0000023.def: A quantification of a parameter of the chemical composition of blood.

CMO:0000024.name: calculated differential white blood cell count
CMO:0000024.def: A measurement which has been normalized, adjusted or derived by a mathematical process or computation, of one or more of the various, specific types of leukocytes present in a sample of blood for which a total white blood cell count was taken, usually 1 cubic mm of peripheral venous blood.

CMO:0000025.name: red blood cell count
CMO:0000025.def: The number of red blood cells in a specified volume of blood most commonly 1 cubic millimeter (i.e. 1 microliter) of peripheral venous blood.

CMO:0000026.name: blood hemoglobin level
CMO:0000026.def: The amount of hemoglobin, the red oxygen-carrying pigment of erythrocytes, in a specified volume of blood.

CMO:0000027.name: white blood cell count
CMO:0000027.def: The number of white blood cells in a specified volume of blood.

CMO:0000028.name: blood protein measurement
CMO:0000028.def: Any measurement involving the amount, composition or type of protein, the complex organic compounds containing carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, and sulfur consisting of alpha-amino acids joined by peptide linkages, in blood.

CMO:0000029.name: platelet count
CMO:0000029.def: The number of platelets (thrombocytes) in a specified volume of blood, usually expressed as platelets per cubic millimeter of whole blood.

CMO:0000030.name: blood neutrophil count
CMO:0000030.def: The number of granulocytes categorized as neutrophils in a specified volume of blood. A neutrophil is, or is in the process of becoming, a granular leucocyte having a nucleus with three to five lobes connected by threads of chromatin, cytoplasm containing very fine granules, and which is readily stainable with neutral dyes.

CMO:0000031.name: blood lymphocyte count
CMO:0000031.def: The number of lymphocytes in a specified volume of blood.

CMO:0000032.name: blood monocyte count
CMO:0000032.def: The number of monocytes in a specified volume of blood.

CMO:0000033.name: blood eosinophil count
CMO:0000033.def: The number of granulocytes categorized as eosinophils in a specified sample of blood. An eosinophil is a granular leukocyte having a nucleus with two lobes connected by a thread of chromatin, and cytoplasm containing coarse, round granules of uniform size that stain readily with eosin and other acid dyes.

CMO:0000034.name: blood basophil count
CMO:0000034.def: The number of granulocytes categorized as basophils in a specified sample of blood. A basophil is a granular leukocyte with an irregularly shaped, relatively pale-staining nucleus that is partially constricted into two lobes, and with cytoplasm containing coarse granules of variable size that stain bluish-black when exposed to basic dyes.

CMO:0000035.name: blood measurement
CMO:0000035.def: A measurement of the blood, it's contents, cells or other factors contained within the blood.

CMO:0000036.name: complete blood count and differential
CMO:0000036.def: Value resulting from the quantification of the cellular elements of the blood, including morphological parameters of blood cells, i.e. cells native to the circulation, including those of erythroid, lymphoid, myeloid and monocytic lineages. The CBC/differential indicates the differential counts of white blood cells, counts of red blood cells and platelets, the concentration of hemoglobin, and the hematocrit.

CMO:0000037.name: hematocrit
CMO:0000037.def: Percentage of total blood volume that is made up of red blood cells.

CMO:0000038.name: mean corpuscular volume
CMO:0000038.def: A measure of the average volume or size of a single red blood cell. It is derived by dividing the total volume of packed red blood cells by the total red blood cell count.

CMO:0000039.name: blood steroid level
CMO:0000039.def: The level of steroids found in a specific volume of blood.

CMO:0000040.name: blood glucocorticoid level
CMO:0000040.def: The amount of glucocorticoids, steroids produced by the adrenal cortex that regulate carbohydrate, lipid and protein metabolism, found in a specific volume of blood.

CMO:0000041.name: red blood cell distribution width-coefficient of variation
CMO:0000041.def: The red cell distribution width (RDW) is a measurement derived from the red blood cell distribution curves generated on automated hematology analyzers and is an indicator of variation in RBC size within a blood sample. The RDW is used along with the indices (MCV, MCH, MCHC) to describe a population of RBCs. The RDW measures the deviation of the RBC width, not the actual width or size of individual cells. The RDW-CV is a calculation based on both the width of the distribution curve and the mean cell size. It is calculated by dividing the standard deviation of the mean cell size by the MCV of the red cells and multiplying by 100 to convert to a percentage.

CMO:0000042.name: plasma glucose level
CMO:0000042.def: Measurement of the amount of glucose, the monosaccharide sugar, C6H12O6, occurring widely in plant and animal tissues which is one of the three dietary monosaccharides that are absorbed directly into the bloodstream during digestion, is the end product of carbohydrate metabolism, and is the chief source of energy for living organisms, in a specified volume of plasma, the fibrinogen-containing fluid portion of the blood in which the particulate components are suspended.

CMO:0000043.name: plasma aspartate aminotransferase activity level
CMO:0000043.def: The amount of enzymatic activity of glutamic-oxaloacetic transaminase enzyme, commonly known as aspartate transaminase or aspartate aminotransferase (AST), in a specified sample of plasma. AST catalyzes the reversible transfer of an amine group from l-glutamic acid to oxaloacetic acid, forming alpha-ketoglutaric acid and l-aspartic acid. Plasma AST level is used as an enzymatic marker for liver disease or damage.

CMO:0000044.name: plasma alanine aminotransferase activity level
CMO:0000044.def: The amount of ezymatic activity of glutamic-pyruvate transaminase enzyme, commonly known as alanine transaminase or alanine aminotransferase (ALT), enzyme in a specified sample of plasma. ALT catalyzes the reversible transamination between alanine and 2-oxoglutarate to generate pyruvate and glutamate. Plasma ALT activity level is used as an enzymatic marker for  liver disease or damage.

CMO:0000045.name: plasma alkaline phosphatase activity level
CMO:0000045.def: Quantitation of the catalytic effect exerted by alkaline phosphatase (AP) in a specified sample of plasma, the fibrinogen-containing fluid portion of the blood in which the particulate components are suspended. AP is an enzyme that catalyzes the cleavage of orthophosphate from orthophosphoric monoesters under alkaline conditions.

CMO:0000046.name: blood glucose level
CMO:0000046.def: Measurement of the amount of glucose, the monosaccharide sugar, C6H12O6, occurring widely in plant and animal tissues which is one of the three dietary monosaccharides that are absorbed directly into the bloodstream during digestion, is the end product of carbohydrate metabolism, and is the chief source of energy for living organisms, in a specified volume of blood, the fluid that circulates through the heart, arteries, capillaries and veins carrying nutrients and oxygen to the body tissues and metabolites away from them.

CMO:0000047.name: plasma indirect bilirubin level
CMO:0000047.def: The amount of indirect or unconjugated bilirubin in a specified sample of blood plasma. Indirect bilirubin is the lipid-soluble form of bilirubin that circulates in loose association with the plasma proteins. It can be calculated by subtracting direct bilirubin level from the total bilirubin level.

CMO:0000048.name: plasma direct bilirubin level
CMO:0000048.def: The level of direct bilirubin in a specified sample of blood plasma. Direct bilirubin is produced when the unconjugated form is carried to the liver where it is conjugated to form the water-soluble bilirubin diglucuronide.

CMO:0000049.name: blood urea nitrogen level
CMO:0000049.def: The level of urea in the blood in terms of nitrogen content; converted to urea concentration by multiplying by 60/28 or 2.14. Urea is the chief nitrogenous end product of protein metabolism in whole blood. Urea is formed in the liver from amino acids and from ammonia compounds and can be found in urine, blood, and lymph.

CMO:0000050.name: blood lipid measurement
CMO:0000050.def: Any value resulting from the quantification of a morphological or physiological parameter of a blood-derived lipid, any of a structurally diverse group of organic compounds found in blood that are insoluble in water but soluble innonpolar solvents that, among other biological functions, serve as a source of fuel and are an important constituent of cell structure.

CMO:0000051.name: blood total cholesterol level
CMO:0000051.def: Measurement of the entire amount of cholesterol, a eukaryotic sterol that in higher animals is the precursor of bile acids and steroid hormones and a key constituent of cell membranes, without taking into account any association with other molecules such as lipoproteins, in a specified volume of blood, the fluid that circulates through the heart, arteries, capillaries and veins carrying nutrients and oxygen to the body tissues and metabolites away from them.

CMO:0000052.name: blood high density lipoprotein cholesterol level
CMO:0000052.def: Measurement of the amount of cholesterol, a eukaryotic sterol that in higher animals is the precursor of bile acids and steroid hormones and a key constituent of cell membranes, carried in high-density lipoprotein (HDL) molecules in a specified volume of blood, the fluid that circulates through the heart, arteries, capillaries and veins carrying nutrients and oxygen to the body tissues and metabolites away from them. HDL is the smallest of the major lipoprotein particles, complex molecules that consist of a protein membrane surrounding a core of lipids. The HDL class of lipoproteins, specifically the subtypes of HDL2 and HDL3, have densities between 1.063 and 1.210 g/ml.
synonyms: free cholesterol in large HDL measurement

CMO:0000053.name: blood low density lipoprotein cholesterol level
CMO:0000053.def: Measurement of the amount of cholesterol, a eukaryotic sterol that in higher animals is the precursor of bile acids and steroid hormones and a key constituent of cell membranes, carried in low-density lipoprotein (LDL) molecules in a specified volume of blood, the fluid that circulates through the heart, arteries, capillaries and veins carrying nutrients and oxygen to the body tissues and metabolites away from them. LDL constitute a class of relatively large, heterogeneous lipoprotein particles, complex molecules that consist of a protein membrane surrounding a core of lipids. The LDL class of lipoproteins has a density between 1.019 and 1.063 g/ml. In some animal species, such as canine and rodents, this may overlap with the HDL1 class and be designated LDL/HDL1.

CMO:0000054.name: plasma total protein level
CMO:0000054.def: Measurement of the total amount of all proteins, the complex organic compounds containing carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, and sulfur consisting of alpha-amino acids joined by peptide linkages, found in a specific volume of plasma, the fibrinogen-containing fluid portion of the blood in which the particulate components are suspended.

CMO:0000055.name: plasma globulin level
CMO:0000055.def: A measure related to globulin, a protein insoluble in water but soluble in a saline solution, extensively found in plasma.

CMO:0000056.name: plasma albumin level
CMO:0000056.def: The amount of albumin in a specified sample of plasma, the fibrinogen-containing fluid portion of the blood in which the particulate components are suspended.

CMO:0000057.name: serum creatinine level
CMO:0000057.def: The amount of creatinine, a catabolic product of creatine phosphate used in skeletal muscle contraction, found in a specified volume of serum.

CMO:0000058.name: plasma phosphate level
CMO:0000058.def: The amount of phosphorus, measured as inorganic phosphate, in a specified sample of plasma.

CMO:0000059.name: plasma chloride level
CMO:0000059.def: The amount of chloride ions found in a specific volume of plasma.

CMO:0000060.name: plasma sodium level
CMO:0000060.def: The amount of sodium ions found in a specific volume of plasma.

CMO:0000061.name: plasma potassium level
CMO:0000061.def: The amount of potassium ions found in a specific volume of plasma.

CMO:0000062.name: plasma bicarbonate level
CMO:0000062.def: The amount of carbonic acid dissolved in carbon dioxide and bicarbonate ion found in a specific volume of plasma.

CMO:0000063.name: blood electrolyte measurement
CMO:0000063.def: A quantification of one or more mineral salts found in the blood in the form of electrically charged ions.

CMO:0000064.name: blood enzyme activity level
CMO:0000064.def: Any quantitation of the catalytic effect exerted by an enzyme in a specified sample of blood. An enzyme is a protein that catalyzes chemical reactions of other substances without itself being destroyed or altered upon completion of the reaction(s).

CMO:0000065.name: plasma calcium level
CMO:0000065.def: The amount of calcium found in a specific volume of plasma.

CMO:0000066.name: plasma anion gap
CMO:0000066.def: The plasma anion gap is a measurement of the difference-or gap-between the negatively charged and positively charged electrolytes in plasma, i.e. blood from which cells and cellular components have been removed. If the anion gap is either too high or too low, it may be a sign of a disorder in the lungs, kidneys, or other organ systems.

CMO:0000067.name: anion gap
CMO:0000067.def: This is a measurement of the difference-or gap-between the negatively charged and positively charged electrolytes in blood. If the anion gap is either too high or too low, it may be a sign of a disorder in the lungs, kidneys, or other organ systems.

CMO:0000068.name: organ morphological measurement
CMO:0000068.def: A measurement of the physical form and structure of an organ.

CMO:0000069.name: heart wet weight
CMO:0000069.def: The weight of the heart after removal from the body but without desiccation.

CMO:0000070.name: heart dry weight
CMO:0000070.def: The weight of the heart after desiccation.

CMO:0000071.name: heart left ventricle wet weight
CMO:0000071.def: The weight of the lower left chamber of the heart, which pumps oxygenated blood through the aorta into the systemic arteries, after removal from the body and separation from the rest of the heart but without desiccation.

CMO:0000072.name: heart right ventricle wet weight
CMO:0000072.def: The weight of the lower right chamber of the heart, which pumps venous blood through the pulmonary trunk and arteries to the capillaries of the lung, after removal from the body and separation from the rest of the heart but without desiccation.

CMO:0000073.name: calculated heart weight
CMO:0000073.def: This is a measurement which has been normalized, adjusted or derived by a mathematical process or computation, of the weight of the heart, that is, its heaviness or the degree to which it is drawn toward the earth by gravity.

CMO:0000074.name: heart weight to body weight ratio
CMO:0000074.def: A calculated value in which the weight of the heart, the chambered, muscular organ in vertebrates that pumps blood received from the veins into the arteries, thereby maintaining the flow of blood through the entire circulatory system, is divided by the total weight of the body, and the result presented as a ratio, fraction, quotient or percentage, thus normalizing it to body weight and, by extension, to the size of the organism.
synonyms: heart weight as percentage of body weight

CMO:0000075.name: heart weight as percentage of body weight
CMO:0000075.def: A calculated value in which the weight of the heart, the chambered, muscular organ in vertebrates that pumps blood received from the veins into the arteries, thereby maintaining the flow of blood through the entire circulatory system, is presented as percentage of the total weight of the body, thus normalizing it to body weight.

CMO:0000076.name: aorta weight
CMO:0000076.def: The weight of the aorta, the main trunk from which the arterial system proceeds. Weight is the heaviness or degree to which a body is drawn to the earth by gravity.

CMO:0000077.name: blood vessel measurement
CMO:0000077.def: Any quantification of a morphological or physiological parameter of one or more blood vessels, the network of muscular tubes that carry blood through the body.

CMO:0000078.name: body length, nose to tail
CMO:0000078.def: The distance between the tip of the nose and the very end of the appendage extending from the end of the trunk of an organism.

CMO:0000079.name: body length, nose to rump
CMO:0000079.def: The distance between the tip of the nose and the back end of an organism.

CMO:0000080.name: renal/urinary measurement
CMO:0000080.def: This is any measurement, morphological or physiological, involving the kidney or any of the organs involved in the production or excretion of urine.

CMO:0000081.name: kidney weight
CMO:0000081.def: The weight of one or both kidneys, the organ which functions to maintain proper water and electrolyte balance, regulate acid-base concentration, and filter the blood of metabolic wastes.

CMO:0000082.name: right kidney wet weight
CMO:0000082.def: The weight of the right kidney, the organ which lies on the right side of the body from the perspective of the subject and functions to maintain proper water and electrolyte balance, regulate acid-base concentration, and filter the blood of metabolic wastes, after removal from the body but without desiccation.

CMO:0000083.name: left kidney wet weight
CMO:0000083.def: The weight of the left kidney, the organ which lies on the left side of the body from the perspective of the subject and functions to maintain proper water and electrolyte balance, regulate acid-base concentration, and filter the blood of metabolic wastes, after removal from the body but without desiccation.

CMO:0000084.name: single kidney wet weight
CMO:0000084.def: The weight of a single kidney, the organ which functions to maintain proper water and electrolyte balance, regulate acid-base concentration, and filter the blood of metabolic wastes, after removal from the body but without desiccation.

CMO:0000085.name: both kidneys wet weight
CMO:0000085.def: The weight of both kidneys, the organ which functions to maintain proper water and electrolyte balance, regulate acid-base concentration, and filter the blood of metabolic wastes, after removal from the body but without desiccation.

CMO:0000086.name: liver/biliary measurement
CMO:0000086.def: This is any measurement, morphological or physiological, involving the liver, the gall bladder, or the bile ducts.

CMO:0000087.name: kidney morphological measurement
CMO:0000087.def: Measurement of the physical form or structure of one or both kidneys, the organ which functions to maintain proper water and electrolyte balance, regulate acid-base concentration, and filter the blood of metabolic wastes.

CMO:0000088.name: abdominal fat pad weight
CMO:0000088.def: Weight of the encapsulated adipose tissue in the body region between the thorax and pelvis.

CMO:0000089.name: body fat morphological measurement
CMO:0000089.def: Measurement of adipose tissue in entire body or region of body of an organism.

CMO:0000092.name: liver weight
CMO:0000092.def: Measurement of the weight or heaviness of the liver, that is, the degree to which it is drawn toward the earth by gravity. The liver is the large abdominal organ/gland which functions in the storage and filtration of blood, secretion of bile, detoxification of noxious substances, synthesis and storage of glycogen, synthesis and breakdown of fats and temporary storage of fatty acids, and synthesis of serum proteins.

CMO:0000093.name: liver morphological measurement
CMO:0000093.def: Measurement of the physical form or structure of the liver, the large abdominal organ/gland which functions in the storage and filtration of blood, secretion of bile, detoxification of noxious substances, synthesis and storage of glycogen, synthesis and breakdown of fats and temporary storage of fatty acids, and synthesis of serum proteins.

CMO:0000094.name: respiratory system measurement
CMO:0000094.def: A measurement to assess the morphological or physiological state of the respiratory system or portion of the respiratory system.

CMO:0000095.name: abdominal fat pad weight to body weight ratio
CMO:0000095.def: The weight of the encapsulated adipose tissue found in the abdomen compared to the weight of the entire body, usually expressed as a percentage.

CMO:0000096.name: lung weight
CMO:0000096.def: The weight of the lung, the organ component of the respiratory system responsible for the exchange of gases between the environment and the blood. Weight is the heaviness or degree to which a body (or a part of the body such as an organ) is drawn toward the earth by gravity.

CMO:0000097.name: lung wet weight
CMO:0000097.def: The weight, after removal from the body but without desiccation, of one or both lungs, the organ component of the respiratory system responsible for the exchange of gases between the environment and the blood.

CMO:0000098.name: lung dry weight
CMO:0000098.def: The weight, after desiccation, of one or both lungs, the organ component of the respiratory system responsible for the exchange of gases between the environment and the blood.

CMO:0000099.name: right lung wet weight
CMO:0000099.def: The weight, after removal from the body but without desiccation, of the single lung located on the right side of the body. The lung is the organ component of the respiratory system responsible for the exchange of gases between the environment and the blood.

CMO:0000100.name: left lung wet weight
CMO:0000100.def: The weight, after removal from the body but without desiccation, of the single lung located on the left side of the body. The lung is the organ component of the respiratory system responsible for the exchange of gases between the environment and the blood.

CMO:0000101.name: calculated lung weight
CMO:0000101.def: A measurement which has been normalized, adjusted or derived by a mathematical process or computation, of the weight of the lung, the organ component of the respiratory system responsible for the exchange of gases between the environment and the blood. Weight is the heaviness or degree to which a body (or a part of the body such as an organ) is drawn toward the earth by gravity.

CMO:0000102.name: lung dry weight to body weight ratio
CMO:0000102.def: A calculated measurement in which the weight after dessication of one or both lungs, the organ component of the respiratory system responsible for the exchange of gases between the environment and the blood, is divided by the total weight of the body and presented as a ratio, fraction, quotient or percentage.

CMO:0000103.name: right lung weight to left lung weight ratio
CMO:0000103.def: A calculated measurement in which the weight of the right lung (the lung on the side of the body to the south when the organism is facing east) is divided by the weight of the left lung of the same individual and presented as a ratio, fraction, quotient or percentage. The lungs are the organ component of the respiratory system responsible for the exchange of gases between the environment and the blood. Weight is the heaviness or degree to which a body (or a part of the body such as an organ) is drawn toward the earth by gravity.
synonyms: right lung weight/left lung weight ratio

CMO:0000104.name: single lung dry weight
CMO:0000104.def: The weight, after desiccation, of one individual lung, the organ component of the respiratory system responsible for the exchange of gases between the environment and the blood.

CMO:0000105.name: body mass index (BMI)
CMO:0000105.def: A measurement relating body weight to height in an organism; typically calculated as the weight of an individual divided by the height of that individual squared. For quadrupeds, the square of body height is often replaced by the square of body length.

CMO:0000106.name: body height
CMO:0000106.def: The vertical measurement of a body.

CMO:0000107.name: tissue composition measurement
CMO:0000107.def: A measurement that indicates the compositional nature of a tissue or set of tissues.

CMO:0000108.name: heart right ventricle weight to left ventricle weight ratio
CMO:0000108.def: A calculated value which compares the weight of the right ventricle, the lower chamber of the right side of the heart, which pumps venous blood through the pulmonary trunk and arteries to the capillaries of the lung, with the weight of the left ventricle, the lower chamber of the left side of the heart, which pumps oxygenated blood out through the aorta to all the tissues of the body, and presents it as a ratio.

CMO:0000109.name: blood B lymphocyte count
CMO:0000109.def: The number of B lymphocytes in a specified volume of blood.

CMO:0000110.name: blood T lymphocyte count
CMO:0000110.def: The number of T lymphocytes in a specified volume of blood.

CMO:0000111.name: blood granulocyte count
CMO:0000111.def: The number of granulocytes (polymorphonuclear leukocytes) in a specified volume of blood, usually 1 cubic millimeter.

CMO:0000112.name: plasma angiotensin I converting enzyme activity level
CMO:0000112.def: Quantitation of the catalytic effect exerted by angiotensin converting enzyme (ACE) in a specified sample of plasma, the fibrinogen-containing fluid portion of the blood in which the particulate components are suspended.

CMO:0000113.name: blood direct renin activity level
CMO:0000113.def: Measurement of the amount of renin activity in a specified sample of blood via the direct immunologic detection of the renin protein in the sample and subsequent conversion of the protein level to an activity level.

CMO:0000114.name: ventilation measurement
CMO:0000114.def: This is any measurable or observable characteristic related to the total volume of gas inspired or expired. Ventilation rate is expressed as the volume of gas entering or leaving the lungs in a given amount of time and can be calculated by multiplying the volume of gas, either inhaled or exhaled, during a breath (the tidal volume) by the breathing rate.

CMO:0000115.name: blood renin activity level
CMO:0000115.def: The amount of ezymatic activity of renin, an enzyme which catalyzes cleavage of the leucine-leucine bond in angiotensinogen to generate angiotensin I, in a specified volume of blood.

CMO:0000116.name: plasma renin activity level
CMO:0000116.def: An estimation of the amount of renin in a specific volume of plasma calculated from the rate of formation of angiotensin I or II.

CMO:0000117.name: blood free fatty acids level
CMO:0000117.def: The amount of free fatty acids found in a specific volume of blood.

CMO:0000118.name: blood triglyceride level
CMO:0000118.def: The amount of triglycerides in a specific volume of blood, the fluid that circulates through the heart, arteries, capillaries and veins carrying nutrients and oxygen to the body tissues and metabolites away from them. Triglycerides are any of a group of lipids that are esters formed from one molecule of glycerol and three molecules of one or more fatty acids, are widespread in adipose tissue, and commonly circulate in the blood in the form of lipoproteins.

CMO:0000119.name: blood lipoprotein level
CMO:0000119.def: The amount of lipoproteins, any of a group of conjugated proteins that have at least one lipid component, in a specific volume of blood.

CMO:0000120.name: plasma apolipoprotein level
CMO:0000120.def: The amount of proteins that bind to lipids found in a specific volume of plasma.

CMO:0000121.name: blood angiotensin II level
CMO:0000121.def: The amount of angiotensin II in a specific sample of blood. Angiotensin II (AngII) is the octapeptide, Asp-Arg-Val-Tyr-Ile-His-Pro-Phe, that is derived from angiotensinogen and acts as a powerful vasopressor and stimulator of aldosterone secretion.

CMO:0000122.name: mean corpuscular hemoglobin level
CMO:0000122.def: The average amount of hemoglobin per red blood cell as a caculated value by dividing the total mass of hemoglobin by the number of red blood cells in a volume of blood, often expressed as picograms per cell.

CMO:0000123.name: blood bilirubin level
CMO:0000123.def: The amount of bilirubin found in a specific volume of blood.

CMO:0000124.name: blood sex steroid level
CMO:0000124.def: The amount of sex steroids, hormones which interact with vertebrate androgen or estrogen receptors, found in a specific volume of blood.

CMO:0000125.name: urine creatinine level
CMO:0000125.def: Measurement of the amount of creatinine in a specified sample of urine, the fluid waste product excreted by the kidneys. Creatinine is a nitrogenous compound formed in muscle as the end product of creatine metabolism. Blood and urine tests for creatinine are used as diagnostic indicators of kidney function and muscle mass.

CMO:0000126.name: bioimpedance
CMO:0000126.def: The impedance, or opposition, of a section of tissue to passage of electric current.

CMO:0000127.name: muscle morphological measurement
CMO:0000127.def: Any measurement of the physical form or structure of the skeletal, smooth and/or heart muscles of the body.

CMO:0000128.name: urine potassium level
CMO:0000128.def: The amount of potassium ions in a specified volume of urine.

CMO:0000129.name: urine sodium level
CMO:0000129.def: The amount of sodium ions in a specified volume of urine.

CMO:0000130.name: urine albumin level
CMO:0000130.def: The amount of albumin in a specified volume of urine.  Urine albumin levels which are above normal but not detectable with routine protein testing are referred to as microalbuminuria.

CMO:0000131.name: muscle weight
CMO:0000131.def: Weight of muscle, an organ which contracts to produce movement.

CMO:0000132.name: minute ventilation
CMO:0000132.def: Total volume of gas inhaled and exhaled from the lungs per one minute.

CMO:0000133.name: end-tidal partial pressure of carbon dioxide (PETCO2)
CMO:0000133.def: The amount of carbon dioxide present in air exhaled from the lungs.

CMO:0000134.name: maximal carbon dioxide production (VCO2)
CMO:0000134.def: The rate of elimination of carbon dioxide from the lungs.

CMO:0000135.name: maximal oxygen consumption
CMO:0000135.def: VO2 max (maximal oxygen consumption), refers to the maximum amount of oxygen that an individual can utilize during intense or maximal exercise. The more oxygen a person can use during high level exercise, the more energy a person can produce. This test is the gold standard for determining cardiorespiratory fitness because the muscles need oxygen for prolonged aerobic exercise, and the heart must pump adequate amounts of blood through the circulation to meet the demands of aerobic exercise.

CMO:0000136.name: brain morphological measurement
CMO:0000136.def: Measurement of the physical form or structure of the brain, the component of the central nervous system enclosed within the cranium which is the primary center for the regulation and control of bodily activities.
synonyms: left superior temporal gyrus thickness measurement
superior frontal gyrus grey matter volume measurement

CMO:0000137.name: brain weight
CMO:0000137.def: The weight of the brain, that is, its heaviness or the degree to which it is drawn toward the earth by gravity. The brain is the portion of the central nervous system enclosed within the cranium. It is composed of gray matter and white matter and is the primary center for the regulation and control of bodily activities, receiving and interpreting sensory impulses, and transmitting information to the muscles and body organs.

CMO:0000138.name: calculated brain weight
CMO:0000138.def: A measurement which has been normalized, adjusted or derived by a mathematical process or computation, of the weight of the brain, that is, its heaviness or the degree to which it is drawn toward the earth by gravity.

CMO:0000139.name: brain weight to body weight ratio
CMO:0000139.def: A calculated measurement in which the weight of the brain is divided by the total weight of the body of the organism, and the result presented as a ratio, fraction, quotient or percentage thus normalizing it to body weight and, by extension, to the size of the organism.
synonyms: brain weight as percentage of body weight

CMO:0000140.name: both kidneys wet weight as percentage of body weight
CMO:0000140.def: A calculated measurement in which the weight after removal from the body but without desiccation of both kidneys, the paired organ which functions to maintain proper water and electrolyte balance, regulate acid-base concentration, and filter the blood of metabolic wastes, is divided by the total weight of the body and presented as a percentage, thus normalizing it to body weight.

CMO:0000141.name: liver weight as percentage of body weight
CMO:0000141.def: Weight of the liver in comparison to whole body weight expressed as percentage.

CMO:0000142.name: adrenal gland morphological measurement
CMO:0000142.def: Measurement of the physical form or structure of one or both of the adrenal glands, the complex endocrine glands located just above the kidneys which  release hormones in response to stress through the synthesis of corticosteroids such as cortisol and catecholamines such as adrenaline (epinephrine) and noradrenaline, as well as producing androgens in the innermost cortical layer.

CMO:0000143.name: adrenal gland weight
CMO:0000143.def: The weight of one or both of the adrenal glands, that is, their heaviness or the degree to which they are drawn toward the earth by gravity.

CMO:0000144.name: calculated adrenal gland weight
CMO:0000144.def: A measurement which has been normalized, adjusted or derived by a mathematical process or computation, of the weight of one or both adrenal glands.

CMO:0000145.name: single adrenal gland weight to body weight ratio
CMO:0000145.def: A calculated measurement in which the weight of one individual adrenal gland is divided by the total weight of the body and the result presented as a ratio, fraction, quotient or percentage, thus normalizing it to body weight and, by extension, to the size of the organism.
synonyms: ratio of the weight of a single adrenal gland to the weight of the body
single adrenal gland weight as percentage of body weight
single suprarenal gland weight to body weight ratio

CMO:0000146.name: spleen morphological measurement
CMO:0000146.def: Measurement of the physical form or structure of the spleen, the highly vascular lymphoid organ which serves to store blood, disintegrate old blood cells, filter foreign substances from the blood, and to produce lymphocytes.

CMO:0000147.name: spleen weight
CMO:0000147.def: The weight of the spleen, that is, its heaviness or degree to which it is drawn toward the earth by gravity. The spleen is the highly vascular lymphoid organ which serves to store blood, disintegrate old blood cells, filter foreign substances from the blood, and to produce lymphocytes.

CMO:0000148.name: calculated spleen weight
CMO:0000148.def: A measurement which has been normalized, adjusted or derived by a mathematical process or computation, of the weight of the spleen, that is, its heaviness or the degree to which it is drawn toward the earth by gravity.

CMO:0000149.name: spleen weight to body weight ratio
CMO:0000149.def: A calculated measurement in which the weight of the spleen is divided by the total weight of the body, and the result presented as a ratio, fraction, quotient or percentage, thus normalizing it to body weight and, by extension, to the size of the organism.
synonyms: spleen weight as percentage of body weight

CMO:0000150.name: male reproductive organ morphological measurement
CMO:0000150.def: Measurement of the form or structure of any organ which is part of the complex of male gonads, associated ducts, and external genitalia concerned with sexual reproduction.

CMO:0000151.name: testis weight
CMO:0000151.def: The weight of one or both of the paired egg-shaped glands normally situated in the scrotum, in which the spermatozoa develop.

CMO:0000152.name: calculated testis weight
CMO:0000152.def: The weight of one or both of the testes, the paired egg-shaped glands normally situated in the scrotum, in which the spermatozoa develop, which has been normalized or adjusted by a mathmatical process or computation.

CMO:0000153.name: testis weight to body weight ratio
CMO:0000153.def: A calculated measurement in which the weight of one or both testes, the paired egg-shaped glands normally situated in the scrotum, in which the spermatozoa develop, is divided by the total body weight of the organism and the result presented as a ratio, fraction, quotient or percentage thus normalizing it to body weight and, by extension, to the size of the organism.
synonyms: testis weight as percentage of body weight

CMO:0000154.name: brain dry weight
CMO:0000154.def: Weight of the brain after desiccation of the excised organ.

CMO:0000155.name: brain wet weight
CMO:0000155.def: The weight of the brain after removal from the body but without desiccation.

CMO:0000156.name: lung weight to body weight ratio
CMO:0000156.def: A calculated measurement in which the weight of one or both lungs is divided by the total weight of the body, and the result presented as a ratio, fraction, quotient or percentage, thus normalizing it to body weight and, by extension, to the size of the organism.
synonyms: lung weight as percentage of body weight

CMO:0000157.name: calculated liver weight
CMO:0000157.def: A measurement which has been normalized, adjusted or derived by a mathematical process or computation, of the weight or heaviness of the liver, that is, the degree to which it is drawn toward the earth by gravity.

CMO:0000158.name: liver wet weight
CMO:0000158.def: The weight after removal from the body but without desiccation of the liver, the large abdominal organ/gland which functions in the storage and filtration of blood, secretion of bile, detoxification of noxious substances, synthesis and storage of glycogen, synthesis and breakdown of fats and temporary storage of fatty acids, and synthesis of serum proteins.

CMO:0000159.name: liver dry weight
CMO:0000159.def: The weight after desiccation of the liver, the large abdominal organ/gland which functions in the storage and filtration of blood, secretion of bile, detoxification of noxious substances, synthesis and storage of glycogen, synthesis and breakdown of fats and temporary storage of fatty acids, and synthesis of serum proteins.

CMO:0000160.name: calculated kidney weight
CMO:0000160.def: Any measurement that has been normalized, adjusted or derived by a mathematical process or computation, of the weight of one or both kidneys, the paired organ which functions to maintain proper water and electrolyte balance, regulate acid-base concentration, and filter the blood of metabolic wastes.

CMO:0000161.name: left adrenal gland wet weight
CMO:0000161.def: The weight of an individual left adrenal gland, that is the gland located on the left side of the body when viewed from the organism's perspective, after removal from the body but without desiccation.

CMO:0000162.name: right adrenal gland wet weight
CMO:0000162.def: The weight of an individual right adrenal gland, that is the gland located on the right side of the body when viewed from the organism's perspective, after removal from the body but without desiccation.

CMO:0000163.name: single adrenal gland wet weight
CMO:0000163.def: Weight of one individual adrenal gland after removal from the body but without desiccation.

CMO:0000164.name: both adrenal glands wet weight
CMO:0000164.def: The total weight of both adrenal glands together after removal from the body but without desiccation.

CMO:0000165.name: both lungs wet weight
CMO:0000165.def: The weight together, after removal from the body but without desiccation, of both lungs, the organ component of the respiratory system responsible for the exchange of gases between the environment and the blood.

CMO:0000167.name: adrenal gland wet weight
CMO:0000167.def: Weight of one or both adrenal glands after removal from the body but without desiccation.

CMO:0000168.name: adrenal gland dry weight
CMO:0000168.def: Weight of one or both adrenal glands after desiccation of the excised organ(s).

CMO:0000169.name: kidney wet weight
CMO:0000169.def: The weight of one or both kidneys, the organ which functions to maintain proper water and electrolyte balance, regulate acid-base concentration, and filter the blood of metabolic wastes, after removal from the body but without desiccation.

CMO:0000170.name: kidney dry weight
CMO:0000170.def: The weight after desiccation of one or both kidneys, the organ which functions to maintain proper water and electrolyte balance, regulate acid-base concentration, and filter the blood of metabolic wastes.

CMO:0000171.name: spleen wet weight
CMO:0000171.def: The weight of the spleen after removal from the body but without desiccation. The spleen is the highly vascular lymphoid organ which serves to store blood, disintegrate old blood cells, filter foreign substances from the blood, and to produce lymphocytes.

CMO:0000172.name: spleen dry weight
CMO:0000172.def: The weight of the spleen after desiccation. The spleen is the highly vascular lymphoid organ which serves to store blood, disintegrate old blood cells, filter foreign substances from the blood, and to produce lymphocytes.

CMO:0000173.name: testis wet weight
CMO:0000173.def: The weight after removal from the body but without desiccation of one or both of the testicles, the paired egg-shaped glands normally situated in the scrotum, in which the spermatozoa develop.

CMO:0000174.name: single testis dry weight
CMO:0000174.def: This is the weight of one testis after desiccation. Testes are the paired, egg-shaped glands normally situated in the scrotum, in which the spermatozoa develop

CMO:0000175.name: both testes wet weight
CMO:0000175.def: The weight after removal from the body but without desiccation both of the testicles, the paired egg-shaped glands normally situated in the scrotum, in which the spermatozoa develop.

CMO:0000176.name: single testis wet weight
CMO:0000176.def: The weight after removal from the body but without desiccation of a single testicle, one of the paired egg-shaped glands normally situated in the scrotum, in which the spermatozoa develop.

CMO:0000177.name: right testis wet weight
CMO:0000177.def: The weight after removal from the body but without desiccation of the right testicle, one of the paired egg-shaped glands normally situated in the scrotum, in which the spermatozoa develop.  The right testicle is the one of the pair located closer to the right side of the body from the perspective of the subject.

CMO:0000178.name: left testis wet weight
CMO:0000178.def: The weight after removal from the body but without desiccation of the left testicle, one of the paired egg-shaped glands normally situated in the scrotum, in which the spermatozoa develop.  The left testicle is the one of the pair located closer to the left side of the body from the perspective of the subject.

CMO:0000179.name: blood vessel diameter
CMO:0000179.def: The length of a line which crosses a transverse view of a blood vessel, passing through its center and ending on either side at either the inner surface or outer surface of the blood vessel wall.

CMO:0000180.name: ejection fraction
CMO:0000180.def: Percentage of blood pumped out of the left ventricle with each heart beat.

CMO:0000181.name: end-systolic volume
CMO:0000181.def: Volume of blood in left ventricle at end of contraction.

CMO:0000182.name: head morphological measurement
CMO:0000182.def: Morphological measurement of the top most or forward most division of an organism's body usually containing the brain and sense organs.

CMO:0000183.name: head circumference
CMO:0000183.def: Total distance around the head of an organism.

CMO:0000184.name: skull volume
CMO:0000184.def: Total volume or capacity of the bony or cartilaginous framework of the head.

CMO:0000185.name: limb morphological measurement
CMO:0000185.def: Morphological measurement of one of paired appendages used for locomotion or grasping.

CMO:0000186.name: distal hind limb circumference
CMO:0000186.def: The linear distance around the lower portion of the hind limb, i.e. the segment of the hind limb farthest from the body.

CMO:0000187.name: distal forelimb circumference
CMO:0000187.def: This is the distance around one of the paired front or upper limbs of a quadruped in the segment farthest from the body.

CMO:0000188.name: forelimb length
CMO:0000188.def: This is a measurement of the linear extent from end to end of an anterior appendage such as a foreleg or an arm. Typically this means the sum of the length of the humerus plus the length of the radius.

CMO:0000189.name: hind limb length
CMO:0000189.def: This is a measurement of the linear extent from end to end of a posterior appendage such as a leg. Typically this means the sum of the length of the femur plus the length of the tibia.

CMO:0000190.name: tail morphological measurement
CMO:0000190.def: Any morphological measurement of the flexible appendage extending outward from the trunk or main part of the body.

CMO:0000191.name: tail length
CMO:0000191.def: The distance from the tip of the extended, flexible appendage at the rear of a vertebrate to the point of contact with the trunk or main body.

CMO:0000192.name: blood viscosity measurement
CMO:0000192.def: Measurement of the resistance of blood to flow caused by friction of its component molecules as they slide past one another.

CMO:0000193.name: intramuscular fat weight
CMO:0000193.def: A measurement of the amount, by weight, of the small deposits of fat located within a specified amount of skeletal muscle.

CMO:0000194.name: blood viscoelasticity
CMO:0000194.def: A measurement to describe the combined properties of viscosity, related to the energy dissipated during flow, and elasticity, related to the energy stored during flow, of blood.

CMO:0000195.name: circulation measurement
CMO:0000195.def: Any measurement of the movement of blood through the heart and blood vessels.

CMO:0000196.name: blood flow rate
CMO:0000196.def: The volume of blood flowing through a vessel or organ per unit of time.

CMO:0000197.name: cardiac output
CMO:0000197.def: The volume of blood pumped from the right or left ventricle per minute, also used to calculate - stroke volume X heart rate.

CMO:0000198.name: arterial blood flow rate
CMO:0000198.def: The volume of blood flowing through an artery per unit time.

CMO:0000199.name: venous blood flow rate
CMO:0000199.def: The volume of blood passing through a vein per unit time.

CMO:0000200.name: intramuscular fat weight as percent of body weight
CMO:0000200.def: A calculated measurement in which the weight of the small deposits of fat located within and throughout skeletal muscle is presented as a percentage of the total weight of the body thus normalizing it to body weight.
synonyms: intramuscular adipose weight as percent of body weight

CMO:0000201.name: vessel shear stress measurement
CMO:0000201.def: This is a measurement of the tangential force of the flowing blood on the endothelial surface of the blood vessel. The value is defined by the Hagen-Poiseuille equation (τ = 4μQ/πR3, where τ is the shear stress, μ is the blood viscosity, Q is the volumetric flow rate, and R is the lumen radius).

CMO:0000202.name: in vitro vessel shear stress
CMO:0000202.def: This is a measurement of the tangential force of flowing blood on the endothelial surface of an in vitro blood vessel or other experimental support. The experimental set-up may use steady, nonpulsatile laminar shear stress, pulsatile laminar shear stress, or nonlaminar oscillatory shear stress.
synonyms: in vitro blood vessel shear stress

CMO:0000203.name: in vivo vessel shear stress
CMO:0000203.def: This is a measurement of shear stress in a model organism by the experimental creation of an arteriovenous fistula, ligation of vessels, or transposition of a vein graft into the arterial circulation.
synonyms: in vivo blood vessel shear stress

CMO:0000204.name: blood coagulation measurement
CMO:0000204.def: Measurement to assess the sequential process through which multiple factors of the blood interact to form an insoluble fibrin clot.

CMO:0000205.name: in vivo coagulation measurement
CMO:0000205.def: Measurement of the coagulation properties of blood within a living organism or as it leaves the living organism.

CMO:0000206.name: in vitro coagulation measurement
CMO:0000206.def: Measurement of coagulation and factors affecting coagulation in blood after removal from the living organism.

CMO:0000207.name: bleeding time (BT)
CMO:0000207.def: The time interval between the appearance of the first drop of blood and the removal of the last drop after puncture. In humans, the puncture is often made in the ear lobe or finger.

CMO:0000208.name: intramuscular fat morphological measurement
CMO:0000208.def: Measurement of the physical form or structure of the small deposits of fat located within and throughout skeletal muscle.

CMO:0000209.name: blood fibrinogen level
CMO:0000209.def: Measurement of the amount of fibrinogen in blood, the fluid that circulates through the heart, arteries, capillaries and veins carrying nutrients and oxygen to the body tissues and metabolites away from them. Fibrinogen is a glycoprotein comprised of three pairs of nonidentical polypeptide chains; cleavage products of fibrinogen have a major role in blood clotting as well as roles in cell adhesion and spreading, display vasoconstrictor activity, and can function as chemotactic and mitogenic agents for several cell types.

CMO:0000210.name: activated partial thromboplastin time
CMO:0000210.def: The time needed for plasma to form a fibrin clot after the addition of calcium and a phospholipid reagent. It is used to evaluate the intrinsic clotting system.

CMO:0000211.name: prothrombin time
CMO:0000211.def: Measurement of the clotting ability of fibrinogen, prothrombin, proaccelerin, proconvertin and Stuart factor, usually given in seconds to formation of clot after the addition of a tissue factor or thromboplastin.

CMO:0000212.name: thrombin time
CMO:0000212.def: The time needed for a fibrin clot to form after the addition of thrombin to citrated plasma.

CMO:0000213.name: intramuscular fat cell count to skeletal muscle volume ratio
CMO:0000213.def: A calculated measurement of the number of intramuscular fat cells, that is, adipocytes which make up the small deposits of fat located within and throughout skeletal muscle, divided by the volume of skeletal muscle in the sample, presented as a ratio, fraction or quotient, thus normalizing it to the size of the muscle sample.
synonyms: intramuscular adipocyte count to skeletal muscle volume ratio
number of adipocytes per cubic centimeter of muscle
number of fat cells per cubic cm of muscle

CMO:0000214.name: intramuscular fat area as percentage of skeletal muscle area
CMO:0000214.def: A calculated value in which the area of  intramuscular fat divided by a specified area of skeletal muscle and presented as a percentage, thus normalizing it to the total area of the muscle.
synonyms: intramuscular adipose area as percentage of muscle area
intramuscular adipose area as percentage of skeletal muscle area

CMO:0000216.name: lumen diameter at maximum dilation expressed as percent of baseline

CMO:0000217.name: plasma magnesium level
CMO:0000217.def: The amount of magnesium ions in a specified volume of plasma.

CMO:0000219.name: lumen diameter at maximum constriction expressed as percent of baseline

CMO:0000220.name: systemic vascular resistance
CMO:0000220.def: Resistance to blood flow by blood vessels throughout the body, the degree to which the blood vessels impede the flow of blood, often calculated as SVR equal to the difference between mean arterial blood pressure (MAP) and central venous pressure (CVP) divided by cardiac output (CO) (SVR=MAP − CVP/CO).

CMO:0000221.name: end-diastolic volume
CMO:0000221.def: Volume of blood in left ventricle immediately before a contraction.

CMO:0000222.name: tidal volume
CMO:0000222.def: Volume of gas inhaled and exhaled during one respiratory cycle.

CMO:0000223.name: stroke volume
CMO:0000223.def: Volume of blood pumped from one ventricle of the heart with each beat, calculated by subtracting the volume of blood in the ventricle at the end of a beat (end-systolic volume) from the volume of blood just prior to the beat (end-diastolic volume).

CMO:0000224.name: body region fat morphological measurement
CMO:0000224.def: A measurement on the adipose tissue in a portion of the body.

CMO:0000225.name: arterial blood gas measurement
CMO:0000225.def: Any measurement of a gas or gases dissolved in arterial blood, that is, blood which has absorbed oxygen in the lungs, including oxygen, nitrogen carbon dioxide and/or hydrogen.

CMO:0000226.name: body fat percentage, Lukaski equation
CMO:0000226.def: Total body fat as a percentage of total body mass calculated based on Total Body Water equal to 0.372 times height in centimeters squared divided by resistance plus 3.05 times sex (male-1, female-2) plus 0.142 times weight minus 0.69 times age.

CMO:0000227.name: cell measurement
CMO:0000227.def: Any quantification of a morphological or physiological parameter of one or more cells.  A cell is a membrane-enclosed protoplasmic mass constituting the smallest structural unit of an organism that is capable of independent functioning.

CMO:0000228.name: cardiomyocyte count
CMO:0000228.def: Number of cells of muscular tissue in the heart in a specified sample size.

CMO:0000229.name: blood vessel endothelial cell count
CMO:0000229.def: The enumeration, i.e. measurement of the total number, of the specialized liner cells that form an interface between the circulating blood and the rest of the vessel wall in a specified sample of blood vessel, any one of the network of muscular tubes that carry blood through the body.

CMO:0000230.name: heart electrical conduction measurement
CMO:0000230.def: Any measurement of components of the electrical conduction system of the heart.The electrical conduction system of the heart transmits signals generated usually by the sinoatrial node to cause contraction of the heart muscle.

CMO:0000231.name: cell membrane potential
CMO:0000231.def: Difference in electrical polarization or charge between two sides of a cell membrane or cell wall.

CMO:0000232.name: RR interval
CMO:0000232.def: Interval between an R wave and the next R wave of successive heart beats, inverse of the heart rate.

CMO:0000233.name: PR interval
CMO:0000233.def: Time between the beginning of the P wave to the beginning of the QRS complex, reflects the time the electrical impulse takes to travel from the sinus node through the AV node and entering the ventricles, used as an estimate of AV node function.

CMO:0000234.name: ST interval
CMO:0000234.def: The time between the J point ( the point at which the QRS complex finishes and the ST segment begins) to the end of the T wave.

CMO:0000235.name: QT interval
CMO:0000235.def: An interval measured from the onset of the QRS wave complex to the offset of the T wave.

CMO:0000237.name: aorta wall thickness
CMO:0000237.def: The depth of the wall of the aorta, the main trunk from which the arterial system proceeds.

CMO:0000238.name: heart posterior wall thickness
CMO:0000238.def: The thickness or depth of the dorsal/posterior wall of the heart. The dorsal wall is the portion of the heart muscle which is closest to the spine and farthest from the chest wall of the organism.

CMO:0000239.name: heart left ventricle posterior wall thickness
CMO:0000239.def: The thickness or depth (i.e. the measurement of the two-dimensional extent of the distance between the inner and outer surfaces) of the dorsal/posterior wall of the left ventricle of the heart. The dorsal wall is the portion of the muscle enclosing the ventricle which is closest to the spine and farthest from the chest wall of the organism. The left ventricle is the lower chamber of the left side of the heart, which pumps oxygenated blood out through the aorta to all the tissues of the body.
synonyms: heart left ventricle dorsal wall thickness

CMO:0000240.name: heart right ventricle posterior wall thickness
CMO:0000240.def: The thickness or depth of the dorsal/posterior wall of the right ventricle of the heart. The dorsal wall is the portion of the muscle enclosing the ventricle which is closest to the spine and farthest from the chest wall of the organism.
synonyms: heart right ventricle dorsal wall thickness

CMO:0000241.name: forced expiratory volume to forced vital capacity ratio
CMO:0000241.def: The comparison of forced expiratory volume to forced vital capacity expressed as ratio or percentage.

CMO:0000242.name: waist circumference
CMO:0000242.def: Distance completely around the body in the area between the thorax and hips. In humans, this is commonly at the umbilicus.

CMO:0000243.name: total abdominal fat area
CMO:0000243.def: Total area of adipose tissue in the abdominal area including subcutaneous and visceral adipose tissue.

CMO:0000244.name: abdominal visceral fat area
CMO:0000244.def: Area of adipose tissue within the muscle wall surrounding the abdominal cavity.

CMO:0000245.name: abdominal subcutaneous fat area
CMO:0000245.def: Area of adipose tissue found beneath the skin in the abdominal region. Sometimes calculated as total fat area minus abdominal visceral fat area.

CMO:0000246.name: skin fold thickness
CMO:0000246.def: This measurement is made on the layer of skin and subcutaneous fat raised by pinching the skin and letting the underlying muscle fall back to the bone. It is often used to estimate percentage of body fat.

CMO:0000247.name: skin fold thickness, bicep
CMO:0000247.def: Measurement made on the layer of skin and subcutaneous fat raised by pinching the skin and letting the underlying muscle fall back to the bone in the region of the biceps muscle, commonly the upper arm in humans.

CMO:0000248.name: skin fold thickness, tricep
CMO:0000248.def: Measurement of a fold of skin and subcutaneous fat taken at a point running parallel to the length of the upper limb over the triceps muscle midway between the acromion and olecranon.

CMO:0000249.name: skin fold thickness, subscapular
CMO:0000249.def: Measurement made on the layer of skin and subcutaneous fat raised by pinching the skin and letting the underlying muscle fall back to the bone in the region just below the scapula.

CMO:0000250.name: skin fold thickness, suprailiac
CMO:0000250.def: Measurement is made on the layer of skin and subcutaneous fat raised by pinching the skin and letting the underlying muscle fall back to the bone in the area at the midaxillary line directly above the iliac crest.

CMO:0000251.name: forced vital capacity (FVC)
CMO:0000251.def: The volume of air that can be forcibly expelled from a maximally inflated lung.

CMO:0000253.name: maximum mid-expiratory flow (MMEF)
CMO:0000253.def: Maximal rate of air flow through the pulmonary tree during forced expiration.

CMO:0000254.name: forced expiratory volume
CMO:0000254.def: Fraction of forced vital capacity that is exhaled in a specific number of seconds.

CMO:0000255.name: maximal volume ventilation
CMO:0000255.def: Maximum volume of air that an organism can breathe in and out during a specified period of time, often 1 minute.

CMO:0000256.name: urine measurement
CMO:0000256.def: Any measurement of urine, the fluid waste product excreted by the kidneys, or its components.

CMO:0000257.name: urine specific gravity
CMO:0000257.def: This calculated measurement is the ratio of the density of urine to the density of water at a given temperature and pressure.

CMO:0000258.name: urine pH
CMO:0000258.def: Urine pH is a measure of its acidity and is determined by the negative logarithm of the hydrogen ion concentration in a specified sample of urine.

CMO:0000260.name: timed urine volume
CMO:0000260.def: The amount of urine voided over a specified period of time.

CMO:0000261.name: urination frequency
CMO:0000261.def: The number of times an organism voids urine over a specified period of time.

CMO:0000262.name: urine catecholamine level
CMO:0000262.def: Measurement of the amount of one or more catecholamines, any of a group of amines composed of a pyrocatechol molecule and the aliphatic portion of an amine that have important physiological effects as neurotransmitters and hormones, in a specified sample of urine, the fluid waste product excreted by the kidneys.

CMO:0000263.name: P wave amplitude
CMO:0000263.def: The magnitude of the P wave, the initial deflection of the cardiac cycle representing excitation of the atria as presented in an electrocardiogram.

CMO:0000264.name: P wave duration
CMO:0000264.def: The time from start to finish of the P wave , in the electrocardiograph illustrating the initial deflection of the cardiac cycle, representing the excitation of the atria.

CMO:0000265.name: Q wave depth
CMO:0000265.def: The distance to the lowest part of the Q wave which shows the initial downward deflection related to the initial phase of depolarization of the ventricular myocardium and the depolarization of the interventricular septum as measured by electrocardiograph.

CMO:0000266.name: Q wave duration
CMO:0000266.def: The time from start to finish of the Q wave which illustrates the initial downward deflection related to the initial phase of depolarization of the ventricular myocardium and the depolarization of the interventricular septum as measured by an electrocardiograph.

CMO:0000267.name: QRS duration
CMO:0000267.def: The time from start to finish of the QRS interval as calculated from a set of measurements taken from the beginning of the QRS complex to the end of the QRS complex representing the time it takes for ventricles to depolarize.

CMO:0000268.name: QRS amplitude
CMO:0000268.def: The magnitude of the portion of the electrocardiograph comprising the Q, R, and S waves which together represent ventricular depolarization.

CMO:0000269.name: QTC interval
CMO:0000269.def: QT interval corrected for heart rate calculated by the QT interval divided by the square root of the interval from one QRS complex to the onset of the next QRS complex measured in seconds.

CMO:0000270.name: R wave amplitude
CMO:0000270.def: The magnitude of the R wave, which is the initial upward deflection of the QRS complex following the Q wave representing early depolarization of the ventricles as illustrated by an electrocardiograph.

CMO:0000271.name: R wave duration
CMO:0000271.def: The time from start to finish of the R wave, the initial upward deflection of the QRS complex following the Q wave which represents early depolarization of the ventricles as illustrated in and electrocardiograph.

CMO:0000272.name: S wave amplitude
CMO:0000272.def: The magnitude of the S wave, the downward deflection of the QRS complex following the R wave representing late depolarization of the ventricles as illustrated in an electrocardiograph.

CMO:0000273.name: S wave duration
CMO:0000273.def: The time from start to finish of the S wave which is the downward deflection of the QRS complex following the R wave representing late depolarization as illustrated by an electrocardiograph.

CMO:0000277.name: T wave amplitude
CMO:0000277.def: The magnitude of the T wave, the deflection following the QRS complex representing repolarization of the ventricles as illustrated by and electrocardiograph.

CMO:0000278.name: PP interval
CMO:0000278.def: An interval measured from the onset of the P wave in one PQRST wave complex to the onset of the P wave in the following PQRST wave complex.

CMO:0000280.name: urine amylase level
CMO:0000280.def: The amount of amylase, an enzyme that catalyzes the hydrolysis of starch and glycogen, in a specified volume of urine.

CMO:0000281.name: urine calcium level
CMO:0000281.def: The amount of calcium in a specified volume of urine. Usually determined from a 24 hour volume of urine, expressed in mg of urine per kg of calcium per day or mg per 24 hours.

CMO:0000282.name: urine cortisol level
CMO:0000282.def: The amount of cortisol, a glucocorticoid hormone produced by the adrenal cortex, in a specified volume of urine.

CMO:0000283.name: partial pressure of blood carbon dioxide (Pco2)
CMO:0000283.def: The force per unit area attributable to the carbon dioxide, a colorless, odorless, incombustible gas formed during respiration and composed of one atom of carbon and two atoms of oxygen, dissolved in a specified volume of blood, defined as the force per unit area exerted by carbon dioxide in a mixture of gases in equilibrium with such a sample of blood at the same temperature.

CMO:0000284.name: serum carboxyhemoglobin level
CMO:0000284.def: A measure of the amount of carboxyhemoglobin formed by the combination of carbon monoxide and hemoglobin in a specified volume of serum, the clear liquid that separates from blood after it has clotted completely, i.e. blood plasma from which fibrinogen has been removed.

CMO:0000285.name: activated clotting time (ACT)
CMO:0000285.def: Time for whole blood to clot after the addition of particulate activators.

CMO:0000286.name: blood peptide hormone level
CMO:0000286.def: Measurement of the amount in blood of a molecular chain compound composed of two or more amino acids joined by peptide bonds that is produced in one part or organ of the body and initiates or regulates the activity of an organ or a group of cells in another part of the body.

CMO:0000288.name: percent change in ventilation
CMO:0000288.def: Change in the amount of air breathed in and out between two points in time or two conditions expressed as a percentage.

CMO:0000289.name: respiration rate
CMO:0000289.def: The number of breaths taken by an organism per unit of time.

CMO:0000290.name: mean corpuscular hemoglobin
CMO:0000290.def: The average amount of hemoglobin per red blood cell caculated by dividing the total mass of hemoglobin by the number of red blood cells in a volume of blood.

CMO:0000291.name: mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration
CMO:0000291.def: This is a measure of the concentration of hemoglobin in a given volume of packed red blood cells.

CMO:0000292.name: pulse pressure
CMO:0000292.def: The difference between systolic and diastolic blood pressures, i.e. the difference between the maximal arterial pressure and minimal arterial pressure during the cardiac cycle.

CMO:0000293.name: elbow breadth
CMO:0000293.def: In humans this measurement is commonly performed with the individual's arm extended perpendicular to the body and bent with the fingers pointing up so the angle at the elbow is 90 degrees. The greatest distance across the elbow joint is used for the measurement.

CMO:0000294.name: pulse
CMO:0000294.def: The count of the rhythmic contractions and expansions of an artery due to the surge of blood from the beat of the heart.

CMO:0000295.name: upright sagittal abdominal diameter
CMO:0000295.def: The measured distance from an individual's back to upper abdomen from midway between the top of the pelvis and the bottom of the ribs, commonly measured while the individual is upright.

CMO:0000297.name: supine abdominal height
CMO:0000297.def: Measured distance between back and upper abdomen of an individual, midway between the top of the pelvis and bottom of the ribs while individual is in the supine position.

CMO:0000298.name: absolute change in partial pressure of blood carbon dioxide
CMO:0000298.def: The difference between partial pressure of blood carbon dioxide between two points in time or two conditions.

CMO:0000299.name: absolute change in partial pressure of blood oxygen
CMO:0000299.def: Difference in partial pressure of blood oxygen between two points in time or two conditions.

CMO:0000300.name: absolute change in blood pH
CMO:0000300.def: The difference in blood pH between two different points in time or between two different conditions.

CMO:0000301.name: body density
CMO:0000301.def: The measure of mass per unit of volume often used to determine body fat composition. Techniques often used include comparison of body weight inside and outside of water or a ratio of body volume and weight. Common formulas include body density equal to body weight divided by body volume minus residual lung volume or body density equal to body weight divided by the dividend of body weight minus water weight divided by the density of water minus residual lung volume.

CMO:0000303.name: body fat percentage, Siri equation
CMO:0000303.def: Total body fat expressed as a percentage of body mass using the formula percent body fat equals 495 divided by body density minus 450. Often used for Caucasian men.

CMO:0000304.name: fat mass index (FMI)
CMO:0000304.def: The total amount of body fat calculated as fat mass index equal to fat weight divided by height squared.

CMO:0000306.name: fat free mass index (FFMI)
CMO:0000306.def: Portion of the body not comprised of lipids often calculated as fat free mass equal to fat free mass divided by height squared.

CMO:0000307.name: residual lung volume
CMO:0000307.def: The amount of gas remaining in the lung at the end of a maximal exhalation.

CMO:0000308.name: body fat percentage, Lohman equation
CMO:0000308.def: Fat as a percentage of body weight using the formula percent body fat equal to 503.3 divided by body density minus 459.2.

CMO:0000309.name: body fat percentage, Schutte equation
CMO:0000309.def: Total body fat expressed as percentage of body weight using the formula percent fat equal to 437.4 divided by body density minus 392.8. Often used for African and African-American men.

CMO:0000310.name: body fat percentage, Ortiz equation
CMO:0000310.def: Total body fat expressed as a percentage of body mass using the equation percent fat equal to 483.2 divided by body density minus 436.9.  Often used for African or African-American women.

CMO:0000311.name: abdominal fat morphological measurement
CMO:0000311.def: A measurement of the physical form or structure of the adipose tissue in the body region between the thorax and pelvis.

CMO:0000312.name: calculated body fat morphological measurement
CMO:0000312.def: This is a measurement of body adipose tissue which has been normalized, adjusted or derived by a mathematical process or computation.

CMO:0000313.name: abdominal fat weight
CMO:0000313.def: The weight of any or all of the adipose tissue types in the abdominal region.

CMO:0000315.name: arm span
CMO:0000315.def: Distance between the tips of the longest fingers with the arms maximally outstretched laterally.

CMO:0000316.name: chest circumference
CMO:0000316.def: Distance around the upper trunk of an organism, typically taken at the maximum breadth.

CMO:0000317.name: proximal forelimb circumference
CMO:0000317.def: This is the distance around one of the paired front or upper limbs of a quadruped in the segment closest to the body.

CMO:0000318.name: hepatocyte count
CMO:0000318.def: The number of hepatic cells, polyhedral epithelial cells that constitute the substance of a liver acinus, in a specified sample size.

CMO:0000319.name: pancreatic beta cell count
CMO:0000319.def: The number of islet cells which secrete insulin and make up the islets of Langerhans in the pancreas in a specified sample size.

CMO:0000320.name: retina cell count
CMO:0000320.def: Number of cells in a specified sample of the innermost coat lining of the interior of the eyeball.

CMO:0000321.name: bronchial epithelial cell count
CMO:0000321.def: Number of cells in a specified sample of the internal lining of a bronchus.

CMO:0000322.name: osteoblast cell count
CMO:0000322.def: The number of osteoblasts, cells which arise from a fibroblast and are associated with the production of bone, in a specified sample size.

CMO:0000323.name: osteoclast cell count
CMO:0000323.def: The number of osteoclasts, multinuclear cells associated with the absorption and removal of bone, in a specified sample size.

CMO:0000324.name: Purkinje cell count
CMO:0000324.def: The number of Purkinje cells, neurons in the cerebellar cortex, in a specified tissue sample.

CMO:0000325.name: Schwann cell count
CMO:0000325.def: The number of Schwann cells, large nucleated cells whose membranes spirally wrap axons of myelinated peripheral neurons, in a specified sample volume.

CMO:0000326.name: oocyte count
CMO:0000326.def: Number of oocytes, immature female reproductive cells in a specified sample size.

CMO:0000327.name: sperm count
CMO:0000327.def: The number of mature male germ cells, sperm, in a specified volume of semen.

CMO:0000328.name: neuron count
CMO:0000328.def: The number of neurons, conducting cells of the nervous system, in a specified sample.

CMO:0000329.name: intestine morphological measurement
CMO:0000329.def: Measurement of the physical form or structure of the intestine, the portion of the alimentary canal extending from the pyloric opening of the stomach to the anus.

CMO:0000330.name: intestine length
CMO:0000330.def: Distance from end to end of the portion of the alimentary canal extending from the pyloric valve of the stomach to the anus.

CMO:0000332.name: pancreas morphological measurement
CMO:0000332.def: Measurement of the physical form or structure of the pancreas, the compound endocrine/exocrine gland located behind the stomach in vertebrates which secretes hormones (insulin, glucagon, and somatostatin) into the bloodstream and digestive enzymes and ions such as sodium bicarbonate into the small intestine.

CMO:0000333.name: pancreas weight
