CMO:0000333.def: The weight of the pancreas, the compound endocrine/exocrine gland located behind the stomach in vertebrates which secretes hormones (insulin, glucagon, and somatostatin) into the bloodstream and digestive enzymes and ions such as sodium bicarbonate into the small intestine.

CMO:0000334.name: heart atrium morphological measurement
CMO:0000334.def: Measurement of the physical form or structure of either the right or the left upper chamber of the heart that receives blood from the veins and forces it into a ventricle.

CMO:0000335.name: left atrium weight
CMO:0000335.def: The weight of the left atrium of the heart, the upper chamber on the left which empties into the lower chamber. Weight is the heaviness or degree to which a body is drawn toward the earth by gravity.

CMO:0000336.name: right atrium weight
CMO:0000336.def: The weight of the right atrium, the upper right chamber of the heart which empties into the lower right chamber, i.e. the right ventricle. Weight is the heaviness or degree to which a body is drawn to the earth by gravity.

CMO:0000337.name: left atrium volume
CMO:0000337.def: A measure of the capacity of the left heart atrium, the upper left chamber which empties into the lower heart chamber.

CMO:0000338.name: right atrium volume
CMO:0000338.def: A measure of the three dimensional capacity of the right atrium of the heart, the upper right chamber which empties into the lower right chamber, i.e. the right ventricle.

CMO:0000339.name: heart ventricle morphological measurement
CMO:0000339.def: Any measurement of the physical form or structure of one or both ventricles of the heart, that is, the lower chambers of the heart that pump blood away from the heart either to the lungs to be oxygenated or, once oxygenated, to the rest of the body.

CMO:0000340.name: both kidneys wet weight to body weight ratio
CMO:0000340.def: A calculated measurement in which the weight after removal from the body but without desiccation of both kidneys, the paired organ which functions to maintain proper water and electrolyte balance, regulate acid-base concentration, and filter the blood of metabolic wastes, is divided by the total weight of the body and presented as a ratio, percentage, fraction or quotient, thus normalizing it to body weight.
synonyms: both kidneys wet weight as percentage of body weight

CMO:0000341.name: tumor measurement
CMO:0000341.def: Measurement of an abnormal growth of tissue resulting from uncontrolled, progressive multiplication of cells and serving no physiological function.

CMO:0000342.name: plasma insulin level
CMO:0000342.def: The amount of insulin, the fuel-regulating peptide hormone which is formed from proinsulin in the beta cells of the pancreatic islets and which promotes the storage of glucose and the uptake of amino acids, increases protein and lipid synthesis, and inhibits lipolysis and gluconeogenesis, in a specified sample of plasma, the fibrinogen-containing fluid portion of the blood in which the particulate components are suspended.

CMO:0000343.name: mammary tumor number
CMO:0000343.def: The number of tumors found within the mammary gland.

CMO:0000344.name: mammary tumor growth rate
CMO:0000344.def: The change is size between two points in time for a tumor found within the mammary gland.

CMO:0000345.name: post-insult time to mammary tumor formation
CMO:0000345.def: The amount of time to the first discernible appearance of tumor in the mammary gland following the administration of a tumor causing agent.

CMO:0000346.name: mammary tumor diameter
CMO:0000346.def: The length of a transverse line moving from side to side through the center of a tumor located in the mammary gland.

CMO:0000347.name: mammary tumor measurement
CMO:0000347.def: Measurement of an abnormal growth of tissue in the mammary gland resulting from uncontrolled, progressive multiplication of cells and serving no physiological function.

CMO:0000348.name: mammary tumor weight
CMO:0000348.def: The weight of a tumor found within a mammary gland.

CMO:0000349.name: blood insulin level
CMO:0000349.def: The amount of insulin, the fuel-regulating peptide hormone which is formed from proinsulin in the beta cells of the pancreatic islets and which promotes the storage of glucose and the uptake of amino acids, increases protein and lipid synthesis, and inhibits lipolysis and gluconeogenesis, in a specified sample of blood, the fluid that circulates through the heart, arteries, capillaries and veins carrying nutrients and oxygen to the body tissues and metabolites away from them.

CMO:0000350.name: blood glucose level area under curve (AUC)
CMO:0000350.def: A calculated value in which a series of measurements of the amount of glucose, the monosaccharide sugar, C6H12O6, occurring widely in plant and animal tissues which is one of the three dietary monosaccharides that are absorbed directly into the bloodstream during digestion, is the end product of carbohydrate metabolism, and is the chief source of energy for living organisms, in a specified volume of blood is plotted against time for a single individual and the extent of the two dimensional region bounded by the curve and the axes of the graph is determined.

CMO:0000351.name: blood insulin level area under curve (AUC)
CMO:0000351.def: A calculated value in which a series of measurements of the amount of insulin in a specified volume of blood is plotted against time for a single individual and the extent of the two dimensional region bounded by the curve and the axes of the graph is determined. Insulin is the fuel-regulating peptide hormone which is formed from proinsulin in the beta cells of the pancreatic islets and which promotes the storage of glucose and the uptake of amino acids, increases protein and lipid synthesis, and inhibits lipolysis and gluconeogenesis.

CMO:0000352.name: calculated blood glucose level
CMO:0000352.def: A measurement which has been normalized, adjusted or derived by a mathematical process or computation of the amount of glucose, the monosaccharide sugar, C6H12O6, occurring widely in plant and animal tissues which is one of the three dietary monosaccharides that are absorbed directly into the bloodstream during digestion, is the end product of carbohydrate metabolism, and is the chief source of energy for living organisms, in a specified volume of blood, the fluid that circulates through the heart, arteries, capillaries and veins carrying nutrients and oxygen to the body tissues and metabolites away from them.

CMO:0000353.name: calculated blood insulin level
CMO:0000353.def: A measurement which has been normalized, adjusted or derived by a mathematical process or computation, of the amount of insulin, the fuel-regulating peptide hormone which is formed from proinsulin in the beta cells of the pancreatic islets and which promotes the storage of glucose and the uptake of amino acids, increases protein and lipid synthesis, and inhibits lipolysis and gluconeogenesis, in a specified sample of blood, the fluid that circulates through the heart, arteries, capillaries and veins carrying nutrients and oxygen to the body tissues and metabolites away from them.

CMO:0000355.name: mesenteric fat pad weight
CMO:0000355.def: Weight of the encapsulated adipose tissue attached to the membranous fold or mesentery of the abdomen.

CMO:0000356.name: retroperitoneal fat pad weight
CMO:0000356.def: Weight of the encapsulated adipose tissue found posterior to the peritoneum.

CMO:0000357.name: epididymal fat pad weight
CMO:0000357.def: Weight of the encapsulated adipose tissue surrounding the epididymis, the structure along the posterior body of the testis.

CMO:0000358.name: serum insulin level
CMO:0000358.def: The amount of insulin, the fuel-regulating peptide hormone which is formed from proinsulin in the beta cells of the pancreatic islets and which promotes the storage of glucose and the uptake of amino acids, increases protein and lipid synthesis, and inhibits lipolysis and gluconeogenesis, in a specified sample of serum, the clear liquid that separates from blood after it has clotted completely, i.e. blood plasma from which fibrinogen has been removed.

CMO:0000359.name: calculated serum insulin level
CMO:0000359.def: A measurement which has been normalized, adjusted or derived by a mathematical process or computation, of the amount of insulin, the fuel-regulating peptide hormone which is formed from proinsulin in the beta cells of the pancreatic islets and which promotes the storage of glucose and the uptake of amino acids, increases protein and lipid synthesis, and inhibits lipolysis and gluconeogenesis, in a specified sample of serum, the clear liquid that separates from blood after it has clotted completely, i.e. blood plasma from which fibrinogen has been removed.

CMO:0000360.name: serum triglyceride level
CMO:0000360.def: The amount of triglycerides in a specified volume of serum, the clear liquid that separates from blood after it has clotted completely, i.e. blood plasma from which fibrinogen has been removed. Triglycerides are any of a group of lipids that are esters formed from one molecule of glycerol and three molecules of one or more fatty acids, are widespread in adipose tissue, and commonly circulate in the blood in the form of lipoproteins.

CMO:0000361.name: serum high density lipoprotein cholesterol level
CMO:0000361.def: Measurement of the amount of cholesterol, a eukaryotic sterol that in higher animals is the precursor of bile acids and steroid hormones and a key constituent of cell membranes, carried in high-density lipoprotein (HDL) molecules in a specified volume of serum, the clear liquid that separates from blood after it has clotted completely, i.e. blood plasma from which fibrinogen has been removed. HDL is the smallest of the major lipoprotein particles, complex molecules that consist of a protein membrane surrounding a core of lipids. The HDL class of lipoproteins, specifically the subtypes of HDL2 and HDL3, have densities between 1.063 and 1.210 g/ml.

CMO:0000362.name: serum low density lipoprotein cholesterol level
CMO:0000362.def: Measurement of the amount of cholesterol, a eukaryotic sterol that in higher animals is the precursor of bile acids and steroid hormones and a key constituent of cell membranes, carried in low-density lipoprotein (LDL) molecules in a specified volume of serum, the clear liquid that separates from blood after it has clotted completely, i.e. blood plasma from which fibrinogen has been removed. LDL constitute a class of relatively large, heterogeneous lipoprotein particles, complex molecules that consist of a protein membrane surrounding a core of lipids. The LDL class of lipoproteins has a density between 1.019 and 1.063 g/ml. In some animal species, such as canine and rodents, this may overlap with the HDL1 class and be designated LDL/HDL1.

CMO:0000363.name: serum total cholesterol level
CMO:0000363.def: Measurement of the entire amount of cholesterol, a eukaryotic sterol that in higher animals is the precursor of bile acids and steroid hormones and a key constituent of cell membranes, without taking into account any association with other molecules such as lipoproteins, in a specified volume of serum, the clear liquid that separates from blood after it has clotted completely, i.e. blood plasma from which fibrinogen has been removed.

CMO:0000364.name: complete blood cell count
CMO:0000364.def: The calculation of the cellular elements of the blood, usually including cell counts for white and red blood cells and platelets.

CMO:0000365.name: total white blood cell count
CMO:0000365.def: The total number of leukocytes in a designated volume of blood.

CMO:0000366.name: blood differential white blood cell count
CMO:0000366.def: The number of each type of leukocyte present in a specific volume of blood, usually 1 cubic millimeter.

CMO:0000367.name: blood granulocyte count to total leukocyte count ratio
CMO:0000367.def: A calculated measurement in which the number of all granulocytes (regardless of type) in a specified sample of blood is divided by the total number of white blood cells in the sample, and the result presented as a ratio, fraction, quotient or percentage.
synonyms: granulocyte count as percentage of total white blood cells
granulocyte count to total WBC count ratio
granulocyte count to total white blood cell count ratio

CMO:0000368.name: blood basophil count to total leukocyte count ratio
CMO:0000368.def: A calculated measurement in which the number of basophil granulocytes is divided by the number of all white blood cells in a specified sample of peripheral venous blood, and the result presented as a ratio, fraction, quotient or percentage. A basophil is a granular leukocyte with an irregularly shaped, relatively pale-staining nucleus that is partially constricted into two lobes, and with cytoplasm containing coarse granules of variable size that stain bluish-black when exposed to basic dyes.
synonyms: basophil count as percentage of total white blood cells
basophil count to total WBC count ratio
basophil count to total white blood cell count ratio

CMO:0000369.name: blood eosinophil count to total leukocyte count ratio
CMO:0000369.def: A calculated measurement in which the number of eosinophil granulocytes is divided by the number of all white blood cells in a specified sample of peripheral venous blood, and the result presented as a ratio, fraction, quotient or percentage. An eosinophil is a granular leukocyte having a nucleus with two lobes connected by a thread of chromatin, and cytoplasm containing coarse, round granules of uniform size that stain readily with eosin and other acid dyes.
synonyms: eosinophil count as percentage of total white blood cells
eosinophil count to total WBC count ratio

CMO:0000370.name: blood neutrophil count to total leukocyte count ratio
CMO:0000370.def: A calculated measurement in which the number of neutrophil granulocytes is divided by the number of all white blood cells in a specified sample of peripheral venous blood, and the result presented as a ratio, fraction, quotient or percentage. A neutrophil is, or is in the process of becoming, a granular leucocyte having a nucleus with three to five lobes connected by threads of chromatin, cytoplasm containing very fine granules, and which is readily stainable with neutral dyes.
synonyms: neutrophil count as percentage of total white blood cells
neutrophil count to total WBC count ratio

CMO:0000371.name: blood lymphocyte count to total leukocyte count ratio
CMO:0000371.def: A calculated measurement in which the number of lymphocytes in a specified sample of blood is divided by the total number of white blood cells in the sample, and the result presented as a ratio, fraction, quotient or percentage.
synonyms: lymphocyte count as percentage of total white blood cells
lymphocyte count to total WBC count ratio

CMO:0000372.name: blood B lymphocyte count to total leukocyte count ratio
CMO:0000372.def: A calculated measurement in which the number of B lymphocytes in a specified sample of blood is divided by the total number of white blood cells in the sample, and the result presented as a ratio, fraction, quotient or percentage.
synonyms: B lymphocyte count as percentage of total white blood cells
B lymphocyte count to total WBC count ratio

CMO:0000373.name: blood T lymphocyte count to total leukocyte count ratio
CMO:0000373.def: A calculated measurement in which the number of T lymphocytes in a specified sample of blood is divided by the total number of white blood cells in the sample, and the result presented as a ratio, fraction, quotient or percentage.
synonyms: T lymphocyte count as percentage of total white blood cells
T lymphocyte count to total WBC count ratio

CMO:0000374.name: blood monocyte count to total leukocyte count ratio
CMO:0000374.def: A calculated measurement in which the number of monocytes in a specified sample of blood is divided by the total number of white blood cells in the sample, and the result presented as a ratio, fraction, quotient or percentage.
synonyms: monocyte count as percentage of total white blood cells
monocyte count to total WBC count ratio

CMO:0000375.name: calculated white blood cell measurement
CMO:0000375.def: Any measurement which has been normalized, adjusted or derived by a mathematical process or computation, of one or more white blood cells, any of various blood cells that have a nucleus and cytoplasm, separate into a thin white layer when whole blood is centrifuged, and help protect the body from infection and disease.

CMO:0000376.name: serum total bilirubin level
CMO:0000376.def: The complete or entire amount of bilirubin in a specified volume of serum, the clear liquid that separates from blood after it has clotted completely, i.e. blood plasma from which fibrinogen has been removed. Bilirubin is the bile pigment produced by breakdown of heme and reduction of biliverdin.

CMO:0000377.name: plasma ionized calcium level
CMO:0000377.def: The level of calcium ions in a specified volume of plasma.

CMO:0000378.name: total plasma calcium level
CMO:0000378.def: The amount of calcium ions and protein bound calcium in a specified volume of plasma.

CMO:0000379.name: blood pH
CMO:0000379.def: Blood pH is a measure of its acidity and is determined by the negative logarithm of the hydrogen ion concentration in a specified sample of blood.

CMO:0000380.name: total lung capacity
CMO:0000380.def: Total volume to which lungs can be expanded with greatest inspiratory effort.

CMO:0000381.name: partial pressure of blood oxygen
CMO:0000381.def: The force per unit area attributable to the oxygen, the chemical element with atomic number 8 which is the essential agent in the respiration of plants and animals, dissolved in a specified volume of blood.

CMO:0000382.name: urine chloride level
CMO:0000382.def: The amount of chloride ions in a specific volume of urine.

CMO:0000383.name: urine glucose level
CMO:0000383.def: The amount of glucose in a specified volume of urine.

CMO:0000384.name: urine albumin level to urine creatinine level ratio
CMO:0000384.def: A calculated measurement in which the amount of microalbumin, that is, a level of albumin in the urine which is above normal but not detectable with routine protein testing, is divided by the amount of creatinine in a specified volume of urine. Often expressed as microalbumin concentration divided by creatinine concentration times 1000 mg per gram.

CMO:0000385.name: urine osmolality
CMO:0000385.def: The number of dissolved particles in a specified volume of urine.

CMO:0000386.name: urine color
CMO:0000386.def: The color of urine voided from the body.

CMO:0000387.name: forelimb morphological measurement
CMO:0000387.def: Measurement of the physical form or structure of an anterior appendage such as a leg or the homologous structure in other animals. In quadrupeds, the appendage(s) closest to the head of the animal.

CMO:0000388.name: hind limb morphological measurement
CMO:0000388.def: Measurement of the physical form or structure of a posterior appendage such as a leg or the homologous structure in other animals. In quadrupeds, the appendage(s) farthest from the head of the animal.

CMO:0000390.name: maternal age at first egg production
CMO:0000390.def: The age, that is, the duration of the life of a female bird at the point in time when her initial egg is laid; the earliest or youngest age at which a specific individual has produced an egg.

CMO:0000391.name: maternal age at birth of last offspring
CMO:0000391.def: The age, that is, the duration of the life of the mother at the point in time when her final offspring is born; the latest or oldest age at which a specific individual has given birth.

CMO:0000395.name: egg yolk weight, fowl
CMO:0000395.def: Weight of the yellow portion of the egg of a bird.

CMO:0000396.name: egg production rate, fowl
CMO:0000396.def: Number of eggs laid by a bird divided by the number of days over which the eggs are produced.

CMO:0000399.name: ejaculation duration
CMO:0000399.def: The length of time required from start to finish for the expulsion of semen from the male urethra.

CMO:0000401.name: cleaved embryo number following in vitro fertilization
CMO:0000401.def: The quantity determined by count of the number of embryos which have undergone cell division in a group of embryos produced by in vitro fertilization, the union of male and female germ cells outside the body, in an artificial environment such as in a laboratory medium.
synonyms: cleaved embryo number, post IVF treatment
post IVF treatment cleaved embryo number

CMO:0000402.name: egg measurement, fowl
CMO:0000402.def: Any measurement of all or part of an ovum in combination with its nutrient stores and protective outer coverings, of a bird.

CMO:0000403.name: egg yolk height to diameter ratio, fowl
CMO:0000403.def: The height of the egg yolk of a bird divided by the diameter of the yolk.

CMO:0000404.name: female reproductive organ morphological measurement
CMO:0000404.def: Measurement of the physical form or structure of any organ which is part of the complex of female gonads, associated ducts, and external genitalia concerned with sexual reproduction.

CMO:0000406.name: single ovary weight
CMO:0000406.def: The weight of only one of the pair of female sexual glands in which the oocytes are formed.

CMO:0000407.name: both ovaries weight
CMO:0000407.def: The total weight of both of the female sexual glands in which the oocytes are formed.

CMO:0000408.name: uterine horn length
CMO:0000408.def: Distance between the two ends of one of the tubular extensions from the uterine body to which the uterine tube is connected.

CMO:0000414.name: mammary gland morphological measurement
CMO:0000414.def: Measurement of the physical form or structure of any part of the structure of the mammary gland, the specialized gland of the skin of female mammals, which secretes milk for nourishment of the young.

CMO:0000415.name: udder height
CMO:0000415.def: Distance from the floor of the udder, the mammary organ or cattle and certain other mammals, to the point at the top where it joins the body wall. The udder is a large bag like envelope containing two or more glands, each having a teat.

CMO:0000417.name: udder width
CMO:0000417.def: Distance from side to side of the udder, the mammary organ of cattle and certain other mammals, at the top of the rear attachment to the body.

CMO:0000418.name: growth measurement
CMO:0000418.def: Measure of increase in size of an organism over a specified period of time.

CMO:0000419.name: average daily body weight gain
CMO:0000419.def: Average increase in weight per day as calculated from total weight gain over a specified period of time.

CMO:0000420.name: body weight gain
CMO:0000420.def: Increase in an organism's body weight over a specified period of time.

CMO:0000421.name: carcass morphological measurement
CMO:0000421.def: Measure of the body of an organism after slaughter, with particular parts removed, often the head, hide or skin and internal organs.

CMO:0000422.name: carcass length
CMO:0000422.def: Distance from end to end of animal after slaughter and removal of the head.

CMO:0000423.name: copulation duration
CMO:0000423.def: Length of time a female and male pair are in position for sexual union.

CMO:0000425.name: wing weight
CMO:0000425.def: The weight of one of the paired anterior appendages of birds usually consisting of the humerus, radius, ulna, and metacarpus and all associated muscle and skin.

CMO:0000426.name: consumption measurement
CMO:0000426.def: The quantification of any morphological or physiological parameter related to intake or ingestion, especially of food or drink, or a value resulting from such a quantification.

CMO:0000427.name: food intake rate
CMO:0000427.def: Amount of food consumed over a specified period of time.

CMO:0000428.name: back fat morphological measurement
CMO:0000428.def: Measurement of the physical form or structure of the adipose tissue in the posterior part of the trunk, usually from the neck to the pelvis.

CMO:0000429.name: back fat weight
CMO:0000429.def: Total weight of all adipose tissue located in the posterior region of the trunk, usually from the neck to the pelvis.

CMO:0000430.name: calculated back fat morphological measurement
CMO:0000430.def: A measurement which has been normalized, adjusted or derived by a mathematical process or computation, of the physical form or structure of the adipose tissue in the posterior part of the trunk, usually from the neck to the pelvis.

CMO:0000431.name: back fat percentage
CMO:0000431.def: Weight of subcutaneous fat along the back expressed as a percentage of total body or carcass weight.

CMO:0000432.name: back fat thickness
CMO:0000432.def: Depth of adipose tissue located in the area posterior part of the trunk.

CMO:0000433.name: back fat thickness, 10th rib
CMO:0000433.def: Depth of adipose tissue in the posterior trunk area at the location of the 10th rib.

CMO:0000434.name: back fat thickness, midpoint
CMO:0000434.def: Depth of adipose tissue in the posterior area of the trunk, at the midpoint of the body length.

CMO:0000435.name: back fat thickness, 3rd lumbar vertebra
CMO:0000435.def: Depth of the adipose tissue in the posterior trunk area located at the region of the third lumbar vertebra.

CMO:0000436.name: back fat thickness, 1st rib
CMO:0000436.def: Depth of adipose tissue in the posterior trunk area located in the region of the 1st rib.

CMO:0000437.name: skeleton morphological measurement
CMO:0000437.def: Measurement of the physical form or structure of the bony framework of the body or a portion of this framework.

CMO:0000438.name: vertebrae number
CMO:0000438.def: Number of bones of the spinal column.

CMO:0000439.name: spinal column length
CMO:0000439.def: Distance from first vertebra to last vertebra making up the spinal column.

CMO:0000440.name: ulna length
CMO:0000440.def: The distance from one end to the other of the ulna, the major bone of the forelimb.

CMO:0000441.name: tail weight
CMO:0000441.def: Weight of the appendage extending from the posterior end of the trunk.

CMO:0000442.name: femur length
CMO:0000442.def: Distance from one end to the other of the femur, the major bone in the upper portion of the hindlimb of quadrupeds or the lower limb of bipeds.

CMO:0000443.name: bone morphological measurement
CMO:0000443.def: Measure of the physical form or structure of one or more bones the hard, rigid form of connective tissue constituting most of the skeleton of vertebrates and composed chiefly of calcium salts.

CMO:0000444.name: femur weight
CMO:0000444.def: Measurement of the heaviness of the major bone in the upper portion of the hindlimb of quadrupeds or the lower limb of bipeds.

CMO:0000445.name: teat number
CMO:0000445.def: The number of teats, protuberances on the mammary glands, breasts or udders of female mammals through which milk is excreted.

CMO:0000446.name: interteat distance
CMO:0000446.def: Distance between any two teats, protuberances from the breasts, mammary glands or udders of female mammals, which excrete milk.

CMO:0000447.name: teat length
CMO:0000447.def: Distance from top of teat attached to mammary gland, breast or udder to the part of the teat farthest away.

CMO:0000448.name: total muscle weight
CMO:0000448.def: Aggregated weight of all muscle tissue from a single individual.

CMO:0000449.name: thoracic vertebrae number
CMO:0000449.def: The number of vertebrae in the spinal column within the thorax, the middle portion of the spinal column usually extending from the neck to the thoracic diaphragm, encased by the ribs.

CMO:0000450.name: tibia length
CMO:0000450.def: Measurement of the linear distance from one end to the other of the tibia, the medial and larger of the two bones of the lower leg of bipeds or hindlimb of quadrupeds which articulates with the femur, fibula, and talus.

CMO:0000451.name: tibia weight
CMO:0000451.def: The weight of the tibia, the major bone of the lower portion of the hindlimb, which articulates with the femur, fibula, and talus.

CMO:0000452.name: food intake duration
CMO:0000452.def: Total amount of time spent consuming food during a specified period of time.

CMO:0000453.name: tibia midshaft width
CMO:0000453.def: Distance across the tibia, the major bone of the lower portion of the hindlimb, taken midway between the two ends of the bone.

CMO:0000454.name: drink intake duration
CMO:0000454.def: Total amount of time spent consuming liquids during a specified period of time.

CMO:0000455.name: drink intake rate
CMO:0000455.def: Amount of drink, that is, a liquid that is brought into the mouth and swallowed to quench thirst, for nourishment, etc., consumed per unit time.

CMO:0000456.name: adipocyte measurement
CMO:0000456.def: A measure of a single or group of fat cells, connective tissue cells specialized for the synthesis and storage of fat; such cells consist of a large cytoplasmic vesicle filled with globules of triglycerides with the nucleus displaced to one side and the cytoplasm seen as a thin line around the fat vesicle.

CMO:0000457.name: carcass circumference, butt
CMO:0000457.def: Distance around a carcass taken in a parallel plane just above the anal opening.

CMO:0000458.name: carcass weight
CMO:0000458.def: The weight of an animal's body after slaughter with particular parts removed, often the head, internal organs and skin or hide.

CMO:0000459.name: cervical vertebra length
CMO:0000459.def: The distance from end to end of a single cervical vertebra, that is, the distance between the two surfaces in one vertebra that connect to the corresponding surfaces of adjacent vertebrae. A cervical vertebra is any of the individual bones forming the neck region of the spinal column, the protective bony corridor through which the spinal cord passes.

CMO:0000460.name: cervical vertebral column length
CMO:0000460.def: Distance from end to end of the expanse of the spinal column made up of cervical vertebrae, which constitutes the neck skeletal frame.

CMO:0000461.name: total skeletal weight
CMO:0000461.def: Aggregated weight of all the bones making up the skeleton or hard framework of an individual organism's body.

CMO:0000462.name: carcass skeletal weight
CMO:0000462.def: Aggregated weight of bones constituting the carcass of an animal after slaughter usually with portions removed such as the head.

CMO:0000463.name: carcass width
CMO:0000463.def: Distance from side to side of an organism's body after slaughter often with parts removed such as the head, skin or hide and internal organs.

CMO:0000464.name: diaphragm weight
CMO:0000464.def: Weight of the diaphragm, the muscle separating the thoracic and abdominal cavities.

CMO:0000465.name: single feeding food intake volume
CMO:0000465.def: Volume of food consumed in a single feeding episode.

CMO:0000466.name: single feeding food intake weight
CMO:0000466.def: Weight of food consumed in a single feeding episode.

CMO:0000467.name: gestation period length
CMO:0000467.def: Duration of pregnancy from time of fertilization of the oocyte until birth.

CMO:0000468.name: horn number
CMO:0000468.def: Number of horns, pointed projections often found in pairs, on the head of an individual animal.

CMO:0000469.name: humerus length
CMO:0000469.def: Distance from end to end of the humerus, the bone in the upper portion of the forelimb.

CMO:0000470.name: small intestine weight
CMO:0000470.def: Weight of the proximal end of the intestine extending from the pyloric valve to the cecum.

CMO:0000471.name: large intestine weight
CMO:0000471.def: Weight of t the distal portion of the intestine extending from its junction with the small intestine to the anus.

CMO:0000472.name: teat number, left
CMO:0000472.def: Number of teats located on the left side of an animal.

CMO:0000473.name: teat number, right
CMO:0000473.def: Number of teats located on the right side of an animal.

CMO:0000474.name: carcass length, first cervical vertebra to pelvis
CMO:0000474.def: The distance from first cervical vertebra to pelvis on an animal after slaughter.

CMO:0000475.name: carcass length, first rib to pelvis
CMO:0000475.def: The distance from the first rib to pelvis on an animal after slaughter.

CMO:0000476.name: adipocyte count
CMO:0000476.def: The number of fat cells in a specified sample of adipose tissue. A fat cell is a connective tissue cell specialized for the synthesis and storage of fat; such cells consist of a large cytoplasmic vesicle filled with globules of triglycerides with the nucleus displaced to one side and the cytoplasm seen as a thin line around the fat vesicle.

CMO:0000477.name: plasma immunoglobulin measurement
CMO:0000477.def: Any measurement related to immunoglobulin, any of several classes of proteins produced by plasma cells and lymphocytes which play essential roles in the immune system, for example, attaching to foreign substances in an effort to destroy them, in plasma, the fibrinogen-containing fluid portion of the blood in which the particulate components are suspended.

CMO:0000478.name: plasma antibody level
CMO:0000478.def: A measurement of the amount of an immunoglobulin molecule possessing a specific amino acid sequence that binds to a specific antigen, a substance introduced into an organism which initiates an immune response including the production of the very antibodies which bind to it in an effort to destroy it, in a specified sample of plasma, the fibrinogen-containing fluid portion of the blood in which the particulate components are suspended.

CMO:0000479.name: plasma E. coli specific antibody level
CMO:0000479.def: The amount of immunoglobulin molecule with an amino acid sequence that binds with Escherichia coli, a Gram negative rod-shaped bacterium, in a specific volume of plasma, the fibrinogen-containing fluid portion of the blood in which the particulate components are suspended.
synonyms: plasma Escherichia coli specific antibody level

CMO:0000480.name: plasma E. coli specific antibody level, post challenge
CMO:0000480.def: The amount of immunoglobulin molecule with a sequence that binds to Escherichia coli, a Gram negative rod-shaped bacteria, in a specific volume of plasma taken at a determined time point following a directed exposure to E. coli.
synonyms: plasma Escherichia coli specific antibody level, post challenge

CMO:0000481.name: plasma E. coli specific antibody level, post vaccination
CMO:0000481.def: The amount of an immunoglobulin with a sequence that binds to Escherichia coli, a Gram negative rod-shaped bacteria, in a specific volume of plasma taken at a determined time point following vaccination for E. coli.
synonyms: plasma Escherichia coli specific antibody level, post vaccination

CMO:0000482.name: plasma E. coli specific antibody level change, post vaccination
CMO:0000482.def: The difference in the amount of immunoglobulin molecule with sequence that binds to Escherichia coli, a Gram negative rod-shaped bacteria, in specified volumes of plasma taken before vaccination and at a determined time point after vaccination.
synonyms: change in plasma E. coli specific antibody level after vaccination
plasma Escherichia coli specific antibody level change, post vaccination

CMO:0000483.name: plasma E. coli specific antibody level change, post challenge
CMO:0000483.def: The difference in the amount of immunoglobulin molecule with sequence that binds to Eschericia coli, a Gram negative rod-shaped bacteria in specified volumes of plasma taken before a directed E. coli exposure and at a determined time point after E. coli challenge.
synonyms: change in plasma E. coli specific antibody level after challenge
plasma Escherichia coli specific antibody level change, post challenge

CMO:0000485.name: blood adiponectin level
CMO:0000485.def: Amount of adiponectin, a hormone that modulates glucose regulation and fatty acid catabolism, in a specified volume of blood.

CMO:0000486.name: adipose tissue adiponectin level
CMO:0000486.def: The amount of adiponectin, a hormone that modulates glucose regulation and fatty acid catabolism, in a specified sample of adipose tissue.

CMO:0000487.name: serum aldosterone level
CMO:0000487.def: The amount of aldosterone, a hormone produced by the adrenal cortex which acts as a mineralocorticoid, found in a specified volume of serum.

CMO:0000488.name: serum bicarbonate level
CMO:0000488.def: The amount of carbonic acid dissolved in carbon dioxide and carbonate ion found in a specified volume of serum.

CMO:0000489.name: serum chloride level
CMO:0000489.def: The amount of chloride ions found in a specified volume of serum.

CMO:0000490.name: glomerular filtration rate
CMO:0000490.def: Glomerular filtration rate describes the flow rate of filtered fluid through the kidney. It is calculated by comparative measurements of substances (ex. creatinine or inulin) in the blood and urine over a designated period of time.

CMO:0000491.name: blood glomerular filtration rate, Diet in Renal Disease Formula (MDRD)

CMO:0000492.name: blood glomerular filtration rate, Chronic Kidney Disease Epidemiology Collaboration formula (CKE-EPI)
CMO:0000492.def: A calculated measurement which estimates the glomerular filtration rate (GFR), that is, the volume of fluid filtered from the renal capillaries per unit time, based on the serum creatinine level and adjusted for gender.

CMO:0000493.name: blood glomerular filtration rate, May Quadratic formula

CMO:0000494.name: blood glomerular filtration rate, Schwartz formula

CMO:0000495.name: serum potassium level
CMO:0000495.def: Amount of potassium ions in a specified volume of serum.

CMO:0000496.name: blood potassium level
CMO:0000496.def: The amount of potassium ions in a specified volume of blood.

CMO:0000497.name: blood chloride level
CMO:0000497.def: The amount of chloride ions in a specified volume of blood.

CMO:0000499.name: blood sodium level
CMO:0000499.def: The amount of sodium ions in a specified volume of blood.

CMO:0000500.name: serum sodium level
CMO:0000500.def: The amount of sodium ions in a specified volume of serum.

CMO:0000501.name: blood uric acid level
CMO:0000501.def: The amount of uric acid, a heterocyclic compound of carbon, nitrogen, oxygen, and hydrogen,the end product of purine catabolism, in a specified sample of blood, the fluid that circulates through the heart, arteries, capillaries and veins carrying nutrients and oxygen to the body tissues and metabolites away from them.

CMO:0000502.name: blood calcium level
CMO:0000502.def: The amount of calcium ions in a specified volume of blood.

CMO:0000503.name: serum calcium level
CMO:0000503.def: The amount of calcium ions in a specified volume of serum.

CMO:0000504.name: blood phosphate level
CMO:0000504.def: The amount of phosphorus, measured as inorganic phosphate, in a specified sample of blood.

CMO:0000506.name: hemoglobin concentration
CMO:0000506.def: The amount of hemoglobin, the red oxygen-carrying pigment of erythrocytes, in a specified volume of blood, as calculated from the optical density of a solution of lysed red cells in which hemoglobin has been converted to cyanomethemoglobin and measured with a spectrophotometer.

CMO:0000507.name: hemoglobin absorbance
CMO:0000507.def: The optical density as calculated from the intensity of light at a specified wavelength as it passes through a solution of lysed red blood cells.

CMO:0000508.name: hemoglobin measurement
CMO:0000508.def: A measure of the oxygen carrying pigment of erythrocytes.

CMO:0000509.name: blood androstenedione level
CMO:0000509.def: The amount of androstenedione, an androgenic steroid produced by the testis, adrenal cortex and ovary, in a specified volume of blood.

CMO:0000515.name: blood cortisol level
CMO:0000515.def: The amount of cortisol, the major natural glucocorticoid synthesized in the adrenal cortex and which affects the metabolism of glucose, protein and fats, in a specific volume of blood.

CMO:0000516.name: serum cortisol level
CMO:0000516.def: The amount of cortisol, a glucocorticoid which affects the metabolism of glucose, protein and fats, in a specified volume of serum.

CMO:0000517.name: blood aldosterone level
CMO:0000517.def: The amount of aldosterone, a hormone produced by the adrenal cortex, which acts as a mineralcorticoid, found in a specified volume of blood.

CMO:0000518.name: blood apolipoprotein level
CMO:0000518.def: The amount of apolipoprotein, any or all of the protein constituents of lipoproteins found in a specified volume of blood, the fluid that circulates through the heart, arteries, capillaries and veins carrying nutrients and oxygen to the body tissues and metabolites away from them.

CMO:0000519.name: blood apolipoprotein A level
CMO:0000519.def: The amount of apolipoprotein A, a class of apolipoproteins that occur primarily in high density lipoproteins, in a specified volume of blood.

CMO:0000524.name: blood apolipoprotein AI to apolipoprotein B ratio

CMO:0000525.name: blood low density lipoprotein specific apolipoprotein B level

CMO:0000526.name: blood very low density lipoprotein specific apolipoprotein B level

CMO:0000527.name: blood chylomicron level
CMO:0000527.def: Measurement of the amount of chylomicrons, a class of lipoproteins (approximate density range <0.95 g/ml) that transport exogenous triglycerides and cholesterol from the small intestine to other tissues, found in a specified volume of blood, the fluid that circulates through the heart, arteries, capillaries and veins carrying nutrients and oxygen to the body tissues and metabolites away from them.

CMO:0000528.name: pulmonary arterial diastolic blood pressure
CMO:0000528.def: Blood pressure measured in the pulmonary artery during diastole, that is, during dilation or relaxation of the heart ventricles.

CMO:0000529.name: pulmonary arterial systolic blood pressure
CMO:0000529.def: Blood pressure measured in the pulmonary artery during systole, that is, during contraction of the heart ventricles.

CMO:0000530.name: heart left ventricle weight to body weight ratio
CMO:0000530.def: A calculated value in which the weight of the left ventricle, the lower chamber of the left side of the heart, which pumps oxygenated blood out through the aorta to all the tissues of the body, is divided by the total weight of the body and the result presented as a ratio, fraction, quotient or percentage, thus normalizing it to body weight and by extension to the size of the organism.
synonyms: heart left ventricle weight as a percentage of body weight

CMO:0000531.name: percent change in respiration rate
CMO:0000531.def: Difference in respiratory rate between two points in time or two conditions expressed as a percentage.

CMO:0000532.name: percent change in tidal volume
CMO:0000532.def: Difference in tidal volume between two points in time or two conditions expressed as a percentage.

CMO:0000533.name: absolute change in mean arterial blood pressure
CMO:0000533.def: The difference in mean arterial blood pressure between two points in time or two conditions expressed as the result of the subtraction in and of itself without comparison by ratio with another quantity.

CMO:0000534.name: absolute change in heart rate
CMO:0000534.def: Absolute difference in heart rate between two points in time or two conditions.

CMO:0000535.name: blood ethanol level
CMO:0000535.def: The amount of ethanol, the colorless, volatile, flammable liquid, CH3CH2OH, produced by yeast fermentation of carbohydrates or synthesized by hydration of ethylene, found in a specified volume of blood, the fluid that circulates through the heart, arteries, capillaries and veins carrying nutrients and oxygen to the body tissues and metabolites away from them.

CMO:0000536.name: kidney glomerulus count
CMO:0000536.def: The number of glomeruli in all or part of a kidney. Glomeruli are the tufts of capillaries each situated within a Bowman's capsule at the end of a renal tubule in the vertebrate kidney that filter waste products from the blood and thus initiate urine formation.

CMO:0000537.name: plasma creatinine level
CMO:0000537.def: The amount of creatinine, a catabolic product of creatine phosphate used in skeletal muscle contraction, found in a specified volume of plasma.

CMO:0000540.name: heart left ventricle weight as a percentage of body weight
CMO:0000540.def: A calculated value in which the weight of the left ventricle, the lower chamber of the left side of the heart, which pumps oxygenated blood out through the aorta to all the tissues of the body, is presented as percentage of the total weight of the body thus normalizing it to body weight.

CMO:0000542.name: serum phosphate level
CMO:0000542.def: The amount of phosphorus, measured as inorganic phosphate, in a specified sample of serum.

CMO:0000543.name: serum glucose level
CMO:0000543.def: Measurement of the amount of glucose, the monosaccharide sugar, C6H12O6, occurring widely in plant and animal tissues which is one of the three dietary monosaccharides that are absorbed directly into the bloodstream during digestion, is the end product of carbohydrate metabolism, and is the chief source of energy for living organisms, in a specified volume of serum, the clear liquid that separates from blood after it has clotted completely, i.e. blood plasma from which fibrinogen has been removed.

CMO:0000546.name: plasma free fatty acids level
CMO:0000546.def: The amount of free fatty acids found in a specific volume of plasma, the fibrinogen-containing fluid portion of the blood in which the particulate components are suspended.

CMO:0000547.name: serum free fatty acids level
CMO:0000547.def: The amount of free fatty acids found in a specific volume of serum, the clear liquid that separates from blood after it has clotted completely, i.e. blood plasma from which fibrinogen has been removed.

CMO:0000548.name: plasma triglyceride level
CMO:0000548.def: The amount of triglycerides in a specified volume of plasma, the fibrinogen-containing fluid portion of the blood in which the particulate components are suspended. Triglycerides are any of a group of lipids that are esters formed from one molecule of glycerol and three molecules of one or more fatty acids, are widespread in adipose tissue, and commonly circulate in the blood in the form of lipoproteins.

CMO:0000549.name: blood albumin level
CMO:0000549.def: The amount of albumin in a specified sample of blood. Albumin is the major plasma protein, responsible for much of the plasma colloidal osmotic pressure and serving as a transport protein for large organic anions (e.g., fatty acids, bilirubin, some drugs) and for some hormones when their specific binding globulins are saturated.

CMO:0000550.name: serum albumin level
CMO:0000550.def: The amount of albumin in a specified sample of serum, the clear liquid that separates from blood after it has clotted completely, i.e. blood plasma from which fibrinogen has been removed.

CMO:0000569.name: serum anion gap
CMO:0000569.def: The serum anion gap is a measurement of the difference-or gap-between the negatively charged and positively charged electrolytes in serum, i.e. blood plasma from which clotting factors have been removed. If the anion gap is either too high or too low, it may be a sign of a disorder in the lungs, kidneys, or other organ systems.

CMO:0000570.name: plasma ethanol level
CMO:0000570.def: The amount of ethanol, the colorless, volatile, flammable liquid, CH3CH2OH, produced by yeast fermentation of carbohydrates or synthesized by hydration of ethylene, found in a specified volume of plasma, the fibrinogen-containing fluid portion of the blood in which the particulate components are suspended.

CMO:0000571.name: serum ethanol level
CMO:0000571.def: The amount of ethanol, the colorless, volatile, flammable liquid, CH3CH2OH, produced by yeast fermentation of carbohydrates or synthesized by hydration of ethylene, found in a specified volume of serum, the clear liquid that separates from blood after it has clotted completely, i.e. blood plasma from which fibrinogen has been removed.

CMO:0000572.name: plasma angiotensin II level
CMO:0000572.def: The amount of angiotensin II in a specified sample of plasma, the fibrinogen-containing fluid portion of the blood in which the particulate components are suspended.

CMO:0000573.name: serum angiotensin II level
CMO:0000573.def: The amount of angiotensin II in a specified sample of serum, the clear liquid that separates from blood after it has clotted completely, i.e. blood plasma from which fibrinogen has been removed.

CMO:0000574.name: blood alanine aminotransferase activity level
CMO:0000574.def: The amount of enzymatic activity of glutamic-pyruvate transaminase enzyme, commonly known as alanine transaminase or alanine aminotransferase (ALT), enzyme in a specified sample of blood. ALT catalyzes the reversible transamination between alanine and 2-oxoglutarate to generate pyruvate and glutamate. Blood ALT level is used as an enzymatic marker for liver disease or damage.

CMO:0000575.name: serum alanine aminotransferase activity level
CMO:0000575.def: The amount of ezymatic activity of glutamic-pyruvate transaminase enzyme, commonly known as alanine transaminase or alanine aminotransferase (ALT), enzyme in a specified sample of serum. ALT catalyzes the reversible transamination between alanine and 2-oxoglutarate to generate pyruvate and glutamate. Serum ALT level is used as an enzymatic marker for liver disease or damage.

CMO:0000576.name: blood alkaline phosphatase activity level
CMO:0000576.def: Quantitation of the catalytic effect exerted by alkaline phosphatase (AP) in a specified sample of blood. AP is an enzyme that catalyzes the cleavage of orthophosphate from orthophosphoric monoesters under alkaline conditions.

CMO:0000577.name: serum alkaline phosphatase activity level
CMO:0000577.def: Quantitation of the catalytic effect exerted by alkaline phosphatase (AP) in a specified sample of serum, the clear liquid that separates from blood after it has clotted completely, i.e. blood plasma from which fibrinogen has been removed. AP is an enzyme that catalyzes the cleavage of orthophosphate from orthophosphoric monoesters under alkaline conditions.

CMO:0000578.name: blood angiotensin I converting enzyme activity level
CMO:0000578.def: Quantitation of the catalytic effect exerted by angiotensin converting enzyme (ACE) in a specified sample of blood. ACE is an enzyme of the hydrolase class that catalyzes cleavage of a dipeptide from the C-terminal end of angiotensin I to form activated angiotensin II.

CMO:0000579.name: serum angiotensin I converting enzyme activity level
CMO:0000579.def: Quantitation of the catalytic effect exerted by angiotensin converting enzyme (ACE) in a specified sample of serum, the clear liquid that separates from blood after it has clotted completely, i.e. blood plasma from which fibrinogen has been removed.

CMO:0000580.name: blood aspartate aminotransferase activity level
CMO:0000580.def: The amount of enzymatic activity of glutamic-oxaloacetic transaminase enzyme, commonly known as aspartate transaminase or aspartate aminotransferase (AST), in a specified sample of blood. AST catalyzes the reversible transfer of an amine group from l-glutamic acid to oxaloacetic acid, forming alpha-ketoglutaric acid and l-aspartic acid. Blood AST level is used as an enzymatic marker for liver disease or damage.

CMO:0000581.name: serum aspartate aminotransferase activity level
CMO:0000581.def: The amount of enzymatic activity of glutamic-oxaloacetic transaminase enzyme, commonly known as aspartate transaminase or aspartate aminotransferase (AST), in a specified sample of serum. AST catalyzes the reversible transfer of an amine group from l-glutamic acid to oxaloacetic acid, forming alpha-ketoglutaric acid and l-aspartic acid. Serum AST level is used as an enzymatic marker for liver disease or damage.

CMO:0000584.name: blood carboxyhemoglobin level
CMO:0000584.def: A measure of the amount of carboxyhemoglobin formed by the combination of carbon monoxide and hemoglobin in a specified volume of whole blood.

CMO:0000585.name: plasma total cholesterol level
CMO:0000585.def: Measurement of the entire amount of cholesterol, a eukaryotic sterol that in higher animals is the precursor of bile acids and steroid hormones and a key constituent of cell membranes, without taking into account any association with other molecules such as lipoproteins, in a specified volume of plasma, the fibrinogen-containing fluid portion of the blood in which the particulate components are suspended.

CMO:0000586.name: plasma urea nitrogen level
CMO:0000586.def: The level of urea in terms of nitrogen content measured in a specific volume of plasma, the fibrinogen-containing fluid portion of the blood in which the particulate components are suspended.The plasma urea nitrogen level is converted to urea concentration by multiplying by 60/28 or 2.14. Urea is the chief nitrogenous end product of protein metabolism in whole blood. Urea is formed in the liver from amino acids and from ammonia compounds and can be found in urine, blood, and lymph.

CMO:0000587.name: serum urea nitrogen level
CMO:0000587.def: The level of urea in terms of nitrogen content found in a specific volume of serum, i.e. blood plasma from which clotting factors have been removed. The urea nitrogen level is converted to urea concentration by multiplying by 60/28 or 2.14. Urea is the chief nitrogenous end product of protein metabolism in whole blood.Urea is formed in the liver from amino acids and from ammonia compounds and is found in urine, blood, and lymph.

CMO:0000588.name: plasma hemoglobin level
CMO:0000588.def: The amount of hemoglobin, the oxygen carrying pigment of erythrocytes, found in a specified volume of plasma, the fibrinogen-containing fluid portion of the blood in which the particulate components are suspended.

CMO:0000589.name: plasma carboxyhemoglobin level
CMO:0000589.def: A measure of the amount of carboxyhemoglobin formed by the combination of carbon monoxide and hemoglobin in a specified volume of plasma, the fibrinogen-containing fluid portion of the blood in which the particulate components are suspended.

CMO:0000590.name: serum renin activity level
CMO:0000590.def: An estimation of the amount of renin in a specific volume of serum calculated from the rate of formation of angiotensin I or II.

CMO:0000595.name: absolute change in plasma renin activity level
CMO:0000595.def: The difference in the levels of renin catalytic activity in blood plasma between two points in time or two conditions expressed as the result of the subtraction in and of itself without comparison by ratio with another quantity.

CMO:0000596.name: blood CD4 cell count
CMO:0000596.def: Measurement of the number of lymphocytes expressing the CD4 antigen on their surface in a specified volume of whole blood. CD4 is a membrane glycoprotein found primarily on T lymphocytes, but also can be expressed on B cells, macrophages, and granulocytes. On T cells it is a co-receptor for the T cell receptor (TCR), interacts with MHC class II antigens, and functions to initiate or augment the early phase of T-cell activation.

CMO:0000597.name: blood CD8 cell count
CMO:0000597.def: Measurement of the number of lymphocytes expressing the CD8 antigen on their surface in a specified volume of whole blood. CD8 is a glycoprotein on the surface of killer T lymphocytes that enhances binding with major histocompatibility complex molecules.

CMO:0000598.name: blood CD4 cell count to CD8 cell count ratio
CMO:0000598.def: Calculated measurement of the ratio in whole blood of lymphocytes expressing the CD4 antigen on the surface to lymphocytes expressing the CD8 antigen on the surface.

CMO:0000599.name: blood CD25 cell count
CMO:0000599.def: Measurement of the number of lymphocytes expressing the CD25 antigen on their surface in a specified volume of whole blood.

CMO:0000600.name: blood regulatory T cell count
CMO:0000600.def: Measurement of the number of T lymphocytes (T cell) whose function is control or suppression of the T cell mediated immune response. Regulatory T cells are generally distinguished from other classes of lymphocytes on the basis of the presence and/or absence of a number of specific cell surface marker proteins.

CMO:0000603.name: blood CD25 cell count to CD4 cell count ratio
CMO:0000603.def: A calculated measurement in which number of T lymphocytes in a specified sample of blood expressing the surface CD25 antigen is divided by number of T lymphocytes in the same sample of blood expressing the surface CD4 antigen, and presented as a ratio, fraction, quotient or percentage.
synonyms: CD25(+) cell to CD4(+) cell ratio as percentage
CD25+ cell to CD4+ cell ratio as percentage

CMO:0000604.name: blood CD25 cell count to CD8 cell count ratio
CMO:0000604.def: A calculated measurement in which the number of T lymphocytes in a specified sample of blood expressing surface CD25 antigen is divided by the number of T lymphocytes in the same sample of blood expressing surface CD8 antigen and presented as a ratio, fraction, quotient or percentage.
synonyms: CD25(+) cell count to CD8(+) cell count ratio
CD25+ cell count to CD8+ cell count ratio
CD25 cell to CD8 cell ratio as percentage

CMO:0000605.name: left ventricular end-systolic blood pressure
CMO:0000605.def: Measurement of the pressure within the heart left ventricle at the end of systole, the period of contraction of the heart when the blood is forced from the ventricles into the pulmonary artery (right ventricle) and the aorta (left ventricle).

CMO:0000606.name: left ventricular end-diastolic blood pressure
CMO:0000606.def: The pressure in the heart left ventricle at the end of diastole, the period when the heart is in a state of relaxation and expansion and the ventricles fill with blood.

CMO:0000607.name: absolute change in systolic blood pressure
CMO:0000607.def: Calculated measurement of a difference in the maximum arterial blood pressure, that is the pressure at the point of maximal contraction of the heart, between two points in time or two conditions expressed as a number (positive or negative), not as a ratio or percentage relative to another quantity.

CMO:0000608.name: absolute change in diastolic blood pressure
CMO:0000608.def: Calculated measurement of a difference in diastolic blood pressure between two points or two conditions expressed as a number (positive or negative), not as a ratio or percentage relative to another quantity. The diastolic pressure is the minimum arterial pressure within the cardiac cycle, usually at the point at which the heart is in a state of relaxation and expansion. This is the time when the ventricles fill with blood.

CMO:0000609.name: thymus morphological measurement
CMO:0000609.def: Measurement of the physical form or structure of the thymus, the lymphoid organ which is the site of the proliferation, differentiation and maturation of T lymphocytes, and of the production of hormones such as thymopoietin and thymosin which control these processes.

CMO:0000610.name: thymus weight
CMO:0000610.def: The weight of the thymus, the lymphoid organ which is the site of the proliferation, differentiation and maturation of T lymphocytes, and of the production of hormones such as thymopoietin and thymosin which control these processes.

CMO:0000612.name: thymus weight to body weight ratio

CMO:0000614.name: pituitary gland morphological measurement
CMO:0000614.def: Measurement of the physical form or structure of the pituitary gland, the small, oval endocrine gland attached to the base of the vertebrate brain and consisting of an anterior and posterior lobe, the secretions of which control the other endocrine glands and influence growth, metabolism, and maturation.

CMO:0000615.name: pituitary gland weight
CMO:0000615.def: The weight of the pituitary gland, the small, oval endocrine gland attached to the base of the vertebrate brain and consisting of an anterior and posterior lobe, the secretions of which control the other endocrine glands and influence growth, metabolism, and maturation.

CMO:0000617.name: pituitary gland weight to body weight ratio

CMO:0000618.name: absolute change in pituitary gland weight

CMO:0000619.name: single adrenal gland weight to body weight ratio

CMO:0000620.name: both adrenal glands weight as percentage of body weight

CMO:0000621.name: both adrenal glands weight to body weight ratio
CMO:0000621.def: A calculated measurement in which the total, combined weight of both adrenal glands is divided by the total weight of the body and the result presented as a ratio, fraction, quotient or percentage thus normalizing it to body weight and, by extension, to the size of the organism.
synonyms: both adrenal glands weight as percentage of body weight
both suprarenal glands weight to body weight ratio
ratio of the weight of both adrenal glands to the weight of the body

CMO:0000622.name: single kidney wet weight to body weight ratio
CMO:0000622.def: A calculated measurement in which the weight after removal from the body but without desiccation of a single kidney, one of the paired organs which function to maintain proper water and electrolyte balance, regulate acid-base concentration, and filter the blood of metabolic wastes, is divided by the total weight of the body and presented as a ratio, percentage, fraction or quotient, thus normalizing it to body weight.
synonyms: individual kidney wet weight as percentage of body weight
individual kidney wet weight to body weight ratio
single kidney wet weight as percentage of body weight

CMO:0000623.name: single kidney wet weight as percentage of body weight
CMO:0000623.def: A calculated measurement in which the weight after removal from the body but without desiccation of a single kidney, one of the paired organs which function to maintain proper water and electrolyte balance, regulate acid-base concentration, and filter the blood of metabolic wastes, is divided by the total weight of the body and presented as a percentage, thus normalizing it to body weight.
synonyms: individual kidney wet weight as percentage of body weight

CMO:0000626.name: pancreas wet weight
CMO:0000626.def: The weight of the pancreas after removal from the body but without desiccation. The pancreas is the compound endocrine/exocrine gland located behind the stomach in vertebrates which secretes hormones (insulin, glucagon, and somatostatin) into the bloodstream and digestive enzymes and ions such as sodium bicarbonate into the small intestine.

CMO:0000627.name: pancreas dry weight
CMO:0000627.def: The weight of the pancreas after desiccation. The pancreas is the compound endocrine/exocrine gland located behind the stomach in vertebrates which secretes hormones (insulin, glucagon, and somatostatin) into the bloodstream and digestive enzymes and ions such as sodium bicarbonate into the small intestine.

CMO:0000629.name: pancreas weight as a percentage of body weight

CMO:0000630.name: pancreas weight to body weight ratio

CMO:0000632.name: single lung wet weight
CMO:0000632.def: The weight, after removal from the body but without desiccation, of one individual lung, the organ component of the respiratory system responsible for the exchange of gases between the environment and the blood.

CMO:0000633.name: liver weight to body weight ratio
CMO:0000633.def: A calculated measurement in which the weight of the liver is divided by total weight of the body, and the result presented as a ratio, fraction, quotient or percentage, thus normalizing it to body weight and, by extension, to the size of the organism.
synonyms: liver weight as percentage of body weight

CMO:0000635.name: retroperitoneal fat pad weight to body weight ratio
CMO:0000635.def: A calculated measurement in which the weight of the retroperitoneal fat pad, the mass of closely packed fat cells surrounded by fibrous tissue located behind the peritoneum, is divided by the total body weight of the organism and the result presented as a ratio, fraction, quotient or percentage thus normalizing it to body weight and, by extension, to the size of the organism.
synonyms: retroperitoneal fat pad weight as percentage of body weight

CMO:0000636.name: seminal vesicle weight
CMO:0000636.def: The heaviness, i.e. the degree to which an object is drawn toward the earth by gravity, of one or both of a pair of pouchlike glands situated on each side of the male urinary bladder that secrete seminal fluid and nourish and promote the movement of spermatozoa through the urethra.

CMO:0000637.name: epididymides weight
CMO:0000637.def: The heaviness of the epididymides, i.e., the degree to which one or both of the epididymides is drawn toward the ground.  The epididymis is an elongated cordlike structure along the posterior border of the testis; its coiled duct provides for storage, transit, and maturation of spermatozoa and is continuous with the ductus deferens.

CMO:0000638.name: motile sperm count to total sperm count ratio
CMO:0000638.def: Number of sperm which display autokinesia divided by the total number of sperm  in a sample, expressed as a percentage.

CMO:0000640.name: sperm measurement
CMO:0000640.def: Any measurement of a mature male gamete or germ cell that consists of a cylindrical nucleated cell with a short neck and a thin motile tail, contains genetic information to be transmitted by the male, exhibits autokinesia, and is able to effect zygosis with an ovum.

CMO:0000641.name: litter measurement
CMO:0000641.def: Any measurement of a group of neonates, products of one gestation, provided the average number per gestation is in excess of two.

CMO:0000642.name: litter size
CMO:0000642.def: The number, i.e., the quantity determined by count, of animals in a group of neonates, products of one gestation produced at one birth by a multiparous mammal.

CMO:0000643.name: percent of live offspring per litter
CMO:0000643.def: The quantity determined by count of the number of animals in a group of neonates, products of one gestation produced at one birth by a multiparous mammal, that survive and are alive at birth, divided by the total number of offspring in the litter, expressed as a percent.

CMO:0000644.name: normal sperm count to total sperm count ratio
CMO:0000644.def: Number of sperm which display no defects in form or function divided by the total number of sperm  in a sample, expressed as a percentage.

CMO:0000645.name: daily sperm count
CMO:0000645.def: The total number of sperm, i.e. mature male germ cells, produced by an individual in a 24 hour period.

CMO:0000646.name: plasma high density lipoprotein cholesterol level
CMO:0000646.def: Measurement of the amount of cholesterol, a eukaryotic sterol that in higher animals is the precursor of bile acids and steroid hormones and a key constituent of cell membranes, carried in high-density lipoprotein (HDL) molecules in a specified volume of plasma, the fibrinogen-containing fluid portion of the blood in which the particulate components are suspended. HDL is the smallest of the major lipoprotein particles, complex molecules that consist of a protein membrane surrounding a core of lipids. The HDL class of lipoproteins, specifically the subtypes of HDL2 and HDL3, have densities between 1.063 and 1.210 g/ml.

CMO:0000647.name: plasma low density lipoprotein cholesterol level
CMO:0000647.def: Measurement of the amount of cholesterol, a eukaryotic sterol that in higher animals is the precursor of bile acids and steroid hormones and a key constituent of cell membranes, carried in low-density lipoprotein (LDL) molecules in a specified volume of plasma, the fibrinogen-containing fluid portion of the blood in which the particulate components are suspended. LDL constitute a class of relatively large, heterogeneous lipoprotein particles, complex molecules that consist of a protein membrane surrounding a core of lipids. The LDL class of lipoproteins has a density between 1.019 and 1.063 g/ml. In some animal species, such as canine and rodents, this may overlap with the HDL1 class and be designated LDL/HDL1.

CMO:0000648.name: blood very low density lipoprotein cholesterol level
CMO:0000648.def: Measurement of the amount of cholesterol, a eukaryotic sterol that in higher animals is the precursor of bile acids and steroid hormones and a key constituent of cell membranes, carried in very low-density lipoprotein (VLDL) molecules in a specified volume of blood, the fluid that circulates through the heart, arteries, capillaries and veins carrying nutrients and oxygen to the body tissues and metabolites away from them. VLDL constitute a class of large (e.g. approximately 30-80 nm in diameter) lipoprotein particles, complex molecules that consist of a protein membrane surrounding a core of lipids. The VLDL class of lipoproteins has a density between 0.95 and 1.006 g/ml.
synonyms: very low density lipoprotein cholesterol measurement

CMO:0000649.name: plasma very low density lipoprotein cholesterol level
CMO:0000649.def: Measurement of the amount of cholesterol, a eukaryotic sterol that in higher animals is the precursor of bile acids and steroid hormones and a key constituent of cell membranes, carried in very low-density lipoprotein (VLDL) molecules in a specified volume of plasma, the fibrinogen-containing fluid portion of the blood in which the particulate components are suspended. VLDL constitute a class of large (e.g. approximately 30-80 nm in diameter) lipoprotein particles, complex molecules that consist of a protein membrane surrounding a core of lipids. The VLDL class of lipoproteins has a density between 0.95 and 1.006 g/ml.

CMO:0000650.name: serum very low density lipoprotein cholesterol level
CMO:0000650.def: Measurement of the amount of cholesterol, a eukaryotic sterol that in higher animals is the precursor of bile acids and steroid hormones and a key constituent of cell membranes, carried in very low-density lipoprotein (VLDL) molecules in a specified volume of serum, the clear liquid that separates from blood after it has clotted completely, i.e. blood plasma from which fibrinogen has been removed. VLDL constitute a class of large (e.g. approximately 30-80 nm in diameter) lipoprotein particles, complex molecules that consist of a protein membrane surrounding a core of lipids. The VLDL class of lipoproteins has a density between 0.95 and 1.006 g/ml.

CMO:0000651.name: prostate gland morphological measurement
CMO:0000651.def: Measurement of the physical form or structure of the prostate gland, the gland surrounding the male urethra just below the base of the bladder which secretes a fluid that constitutes a major portion of the semen.

CMO:0000652.name: prostate gland wet weight
CMO:0000652.def: The weight, after removal from the body but without desiccation, of the prostate gland. The prostate is the gland surrounding the male urethra just below the base of the bladder which secretes a fluid that constitutes a major portion of the semen.

CMO:0000654.name: mesenteric fat pad weight to body weight ratio
CMO:0000654.def: A calculated measurement in which the weight of the mesenteric fat pad, after removal from the body, is measured, divided by the total weight of the body, and presented as a ratio, percentage, fraction or quotient, thus normalizing it to body weight.
synonyms: mesenteric fat pad weight as a percentage of body weight

CMO:0000657.name: epididymal fat pad morphological measurement
CMO:0000657.def: Measurement of the physical form or structure of the encapsulated adipose tissue surrounding the epididymis, the structure along the posterior body of the testis.

CMO:0000658.name: epididymal fat pad weight to body weight ratio
CMO:0000658.def: A calculated measurement in which the weight of the epididymal fat pad is divided by the total weight of the body and the result presented as a ratio, fraction, quotient or percentage.
synonyms: epididymal fat pad weight as percentage of body weight

CMO:0000659.name: blood globulin measurement
CMO:0000659.def: Any measurement related to one or more globulins, a class of proteins defined as being insoluble in water but soluble in a saline solution which includes carrier proteins, acute phase reactants, coagulation factors, complement components, and immunoglobulins, in a specified sample of blood.

CMO:0000661.name: serum total protein level
CMO:0000661.def: Measurement of the total amount of all proteins, the complex organic compounds containing carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, and sulfur consisting of alpha-amino acids joined by peptide linkages, found in a specific volume of serum, the clear liquid that separates from blood after it has clotted completely, i.e. blood plasma from which fibrinogen has been removed.

CMO:0000662.name: heart contraction measurement
CMO:0000662.def: Any measurement of components of the periodic tightening and loosening of the heart muscle.

CMO:0000663.name: time to onset of heart contraction
CMO:0000663.def: Measure of the time from the relaxation of the heart muscle to the beginning of the tightening of the heart muscle during contraction.

CMO:0000664.name: time to peak heart contraction
CMO:0000664.def: Measurement of the time from the beginning of heart muscle contraction to the maximum contracted state.

CMO:0000665.name: heart contraction pressure
CMO:0000665.def: Pressure exerted by the heart muscle in its maximally contracted state.

CMO:0000666.name: blood lactate dehydrogenase activity level
CMO:0000666.def: The amount of ezymatic activity of lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) in a specified volume of blood. LDH is the enzyme which catalyses the reaction S)-lactate + NAD(+) <=> pyruvate + NADH. Blood LDH level can be used as a marker for tissue damage.

CMO:0000667.name: plasma lactate dehydrogenase activity level
CMO:0000667.def: The amount of ezymatic activity of lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) in a specified volume of plasma. LDH is the enzyme which catalyses the reaction S)-lactate + NAD(+) <=> pyruvate + NADH. Plasma LDH level can be used as a marker for tissue damage.

CMO:0000668.name: serum lactate dehydrogenase activity level
CMO:0000668.def: The amount of ezymatic activity of lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) in a specified volume of serum. LDH is the enzyme which catalyses the reaction S)-lactate + NAD(+) <=> pyruvate + NADH. Serum LDH level can be used as a marker for tissue damage.

CMO:0000669.name: organ measurement
CMO:0000669.def: Any measurement of a structural part of a system of the body that is composed of tissues and cells that enable it to perform a particular function.

CMO:0000671.name: heart effluent measurement
CMO:0000671.def: A measurement made on a fluid flowing out of the heart.

CMO:0000672.name: heart effluent volume
CMO:0000672.def: The volume of a fluid flowing out of the heart.

CMO:0000673.name: timed heart effluent volume
CMO:0000673.def: The volume of a fluid flowing out of the heart during a specified amount of time.

CMO:0000674.name: organ effluent measurement
CMO:0000674.def: Measurement of a fluid flowing out of an organ, especially one which has been removed from the body for study.

CMO:0000675.name: heart effluent enzyme level
CMO:0000675.def: The amount of an enzyme in a specified volume of fluid flowing out of the heart.

CMO:0000676.name: heart effluent lactate dehydrogenase activity level
CMO:0000676.def: The amount of lactate dehydrogenase activity measured in a specified volume of fluid flowing out of the heart.

CMO:0000677.name: organ lesion measurement
CMO:0000677.def: Measurement of a lesion in an organ. A lesion is a localized pathological change in structure of an organ or tissue due to injury or disease; especially one that is circumscribed and well defined.

CMO:0000678.name: heart lesion measurement
CMO:0000678.def: A measurement of any lesion of the heart. A lesion is a localized pathological change in structure of an organ or tissue due to injury or disease; especially one that is circumscribed and well defined.

CMO:0000679.name: infarction measurement
CMO:0000679.def: Measurement of an area of necrotic tissue resulting from a reduction or obstruction of the oxygen supplied to that tissue.

CMO:0000680.name: heart infarction measurement
CMO:0000680.def: Measurement of an area of necrotic tissue in the heart resulting from a reduction or obstruction of the oxygen supply.

CMO:0000681.name: brain infarction measurement
CMO:0000681.def: Measurement of an area of necrotic tissue in the brain resulting from a reduction or obstruction of the oxygen supply to the brain.

CMO:0000682.name: heart left ventricle infarction measurement
CMO:0000682.def: Measurement of an area of necrotic tissue in the left ventricle of the heart resulting from a reduction or obstruction of the oxygen supply to the heart.

CMO:0000683.name: organ infarction size measurement
CMO:0000683.def: Measurement of the area, volume or weight of necrotic tissue resulting from a reduction or obstruction of the oxygen supplied to that tissue.

CMO:0000684.name: heart infarction size
CMO:0000684.def: Measurement of the area, volume or weight of necrotic tissue in the heart resulting from a reduction or obstruction of the oxygen supply to the heart.

CMO:0000685.name: heart left ventricle infarction size
CMO:0000685.def: Measurement of the area, volume or weight of necrotic tissue in the heart left ventricle resulting from a reduction or obstruction of the oxygen supply to the heart.

CMO:0000686.name: calculated heart left ventricle infarction size

CMO:0000687.name: heart left ventricle infarction size to total heart left ventricle size ratio

CMO:0000688.name: heart ventricle weight
CMO:0000688.def: The heaviness of one or both ventricles of the heart, that is, the lower chambers of the heart that pump blood away from the heart either to the lungs to be oxygenated or, once oxygenated, to the rest of the body, or the degree to which one or both ventricles of the heart are drawn toward the earth by gravity.

CMO:0000693.name: calculated heart left ventricle infarction area

CMO:0000694.name: calculated heart left ventricle infarction weight

CMO:0000695.name: heart left ventricle infarction weight to total heart left ventricle weight ratio

CMO:0000699.name: absolute change in body temperature
CMO:0000699.def: The difference in body temperature between two different points in time or between two different conditions.

CMO:0000700.name: blood vessel resistance measurement
CMO:0000700.def: Measurement of the amount of resistance in a blood vessel to the flow of blood or other fluid through it.

CMO:0000701.name: pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR)
CMO:0000701.def: Resistance to blood flow by blood vessels in the lung.

CMO:0000702.name: calculated pulmonary vascular resistance
CMO:0000702.def: Measurement of vascular resistance in lung blood vessels calculated from other indirect measurements.

CMO:0000703.name: calculated pulmonary vascular resistance normalized to body weight

CMO:0000704.name: blood vessel distensibility
CMO:0000704.def: A measure of a blood vessel's ability to stretch, dilate or expand.

CMO:0000706.name: blood vessel endothelium measurement
CMO:0000706.def: Measurement made on the endothelial tissue or endothelial cells lining a blood vessel.

CMO:0000709.name: methylene blue metabolism-surface area product without auto-oxidation

CMO:0000710.name: methylene blue metabolism-surface area product after auto-oxidation

CMO:0000711.name: methylene blue to FAPGG metabolism-surface area product ratio
CMO:0000711.def: Ratio of the methylene blue metabolism-surface area product without auto-oxidation to the FAPGG metabolism-surface area product.
