CMO:0003648.def: A measurement in which the number of individuals in a study population that display one or more tubulointerstitial lesion(s) of the kidney at a point in time or develop such lesions within a determined period of time are compared to the total number of individuals in the study population. Often expressed as a percentage but could be expressed as a ratio. The lesions may involve tubular atrophy, tubular dilatation, interstitial inflammatory cell infiltrates, interstitial fibrosis or other pathology.

CMO:0003649.name: percentage of study population developing kidney tubulointerstitial damage during a period of time
CMO:0003649.def: A measurement in which the number of individuals in a study population that develop kidney tubulointerstitial damage within a determined period of time, are compared to the total number of individuals in the study population. Usually expressed as a percentage, but could be expressed as a ratio.
synonyms: percentage of study population developing renal tubulointerstitial damage during a period of time

CMO:0003650.name: percentage of study population developing kidney tubulointerstitial damage at a point in  time
CMO:0003650.def: A measurement in which the number of individuals in a study population that develop kidney tubulointerstitial damage at a point in time, are compared to the total number of individuals in the study population. Usually expressed as a percentage, but could be expressed as a ratio.
synonyms: percentage of study population developing renal tubulointerstitial damage at a point in time

CMO:0003651.name: metastatic liver tumor area
CMO:0003651.def: A measurement of the average extent of the two-dimensional surface of, or plane through metastatic liver tumors. A metastatic tumor in the liver is a secondary, abnormal growth of tissue resulting from the spread of cancer cells to the liver from the place where they first formed.

CMO:0003652.name: eye physiological measurement
CMO:0003652.def: Any measurement related to the function of or processes involved in the ophthalmic perception of light.

CMO:0003653.name: electrical activity measurement of retina
CMO:0003653.def: A measurement of electrical signal (amplitude/voltage) generated in the retina after stimulation by flashing or flickering of light.

CMO:0003655.name: a-wave amplitude of ERG waveform
CMO:0003655.def: The a-wave is the first large negative component of the electrical wave generated by the retina in response to light. The amplitude of the a-wave is measured from the baseline to the negative trough of the a-wave. The a-wave reflects the physiological health of the photoreceptors in the outer retina.

CMO:0003656.name: b-wave amplitude of ERG waveform
CMO:0003656.def: The b-wave is positive and usually larger in amplitude than the a-wave of the ERG waveform, generated by the retina in response to light. The amplitude of the b-wave is measured from the trough of the a-wave to the following peak of the b-wave. The b-wave reflects the health of the inner layers of the retina, including the ON bipolar cells and the Muller cells.

CMO:0003657.name: central venous pressure
CMO:0003657.def: CVP (central venous pressure) is the pressure in the thoracic vena cava near the right atrium (therefore, CVP and right atrial pressure are essentially the same). Central venous pressure is an important concept in clinical cardiology because it is a major determinant of the filling pressure and therefore the preload of the right ventricle.

CMO:0003658.name: number of capillaries per cardiomyocyte
CMO:0003658.def: The average number of capillaries associated with and/or surrounding an individual cardiac muscle fiber, a cylindrical multinucleate cell of cardiac muscle tissue containing contracting myofibrils. Capillaries are the minute vessels connecting arterioles and venules, the walls of which act as a semipermeable membrane for interchange of various substances between the blood and tissue fluid.
synonyms: number of capillaries per cardiac muscle fiber

CMO:0003659.name: A23187 response/sensitivity measurement
CMO:0003659.def: Measurement of an organism's, organ's, tissue's or cell's capacity to respond, such as by a change in activity, state or condition, to A23187, an ionophorous, polyether antibiotic from Streptomyces chartreusensis. It binds and transports CALCIUM and other divalent cations across membranes and uncouples oxidative phosphorylation while inhibiting ATPase of rat liver mitochondria.

CMO:0003660.name: A23187-induced blood vessel dilation expressed as percent reduction of the force generated in a pre-constricted blood vessel
CMO:0003660.def: This is a measure of the relaxation caused by the addition of A23187 to a pre-constricted blood vessel. It is the ratio of the amount of dilation compared to a fully dilated blood vessel.
synonyms: calcimycin-induced blood vessel dilation expressed as percent reduction of the force generated in a pre-constricted blood vessel

CMO:0003661.name: blood volume measurement
CMO:0003661.def: A determination of the amount of space occupied by the total amount of blood, as measured in cubic units, in the circulatory system of an individual.

CMO:0003662.name: calculated blood volume
CMO:0003662.def: A measurement which has been normalized, adjusted or derived by a mathematical process or computation, of the size of the three dimensional space occupied by circulating blood.

CMO:0003663.name: volume of blood removed to total prehemorrhagic blood volume ratio
CMO:0003663.def: A calculated measurement in which the size of the three dimensional space occupied by blood removed from an organism is divided by the total size of the three dimensional space occupied by the prehemorrhagic blood of that organism, and the result presented as a ratio, fraction, quotient or percentage.
synonyms: ratio of blood volume removed to total prehemorrhagic blood volume

CMO:0003664.name: phenylephrine-induced blood vessel contractile force expressed as percent of contractile force generated by potassium chloride
CMO:0003664.def: A calculated measurement in which the contractile force of a blood vessel in response to a specified dosage of phenylephrine is divided by the contractile force exerted by that vessel in the presence of potassium chloride and the result expressed as a percentage. Phenylephrine is an adrenergic drug that is a powerful vasoconstrictor.

CMO:0003665.name: dose of irradiation that is fatal to 50% of the total study population
CMO:0003665.def: The amount of x-radiation that is sufficient to kill 50 percent of a population within a certain time frame.
synonyms: dose of x-radiation that is fatal to 50% of the total study population

CMO:0003666.name: dose of whole thorax lung irradiation that causes 50% of the total study population to have lung dysfunction
CMO:0003666.def: The amount of x-radiation that is sufficient to cause 50 percent of a population to have lung dysfunction (measurable as increased breathing rate or other parameter) within a certain time frame.
synonyms: dose of whole thorax lung irradiation at which breathing rate increases for 50% of the total study population
dose of whole thorax lung x-radiation that causes 50% of the total study population to have lung dysfunction

CMO:0003668.name: retinal inner nuclear layer thickness
CMO:0003668.def: The measurement of the thickness of the retinal layer between the inner plexiform layer and the outer plexiform layer that contains closely packed cell bodies of bipolar cells, horizontal cells, and amacrine cells.

CMO:0003669.name: photoreceptor inner segment layer thickness
CMO:0003669.def: This is a measurement of the inner segment of the retinal photoreceptor layer. The inner segment of the photoreceptor connects the outer segment and synapse and is filled with organelles such as the ER, Golgi, and mitochondria, where much of metabolism and regulation of membrane potential takes place.

CMO:0003670.name: renal cortex thickness
CMO:0003670.def: A linear measurement of the outer part of the kidney made from the outer edge of the renal medulla to the capsule of the kidney. The cortex is composed mainly of glomeruli and convoluted tubules.

CMO:0003671.name: Bowman's capsule diameter
CMO:0003671.def: A linear measurement made from one edge to the other edge across the widest portion of a single Bowman's capsule. Bowman's capsule is the expanded portion of the nephron encircling the glomerulus.

CMO:0003672.name: calculated nephron measurement
CMO:0003672.def: Any measurement that has been normalized, adjusted or derived by a mathematical process or computation, of the nephrons of one or both kidneys, the paired organ which functions to maintain proper water and electrolyte balance, regulate acid-base concentration, and filter the blood of metabolic wastes.

CMO:0003673.name: Bowman's capsule volume
CMO:0003673.def: A calculated estimate of the size of the three dimensional space occupied by a single Bowman's capsule in the kidney. Bowman's capsule is the expanded portion of the nephron encircling the glomerulus.

CMO:0003674.name: kidney glomerular density
CMO:0003674.def: The number of glomeruli per unit area of kidney. Based on stereological principles, the number of glomeruli per unit area of kidney equals the number of glomeruli per unit volume of kidney. Glomeruli are the tufts of capillaries each situated within a Bowman's capsule at the end of a renal tubule in the vertebrate kidney that filter waste products from the blood and thus initiate urine formation.

CMO:0003675.name: norepinephrine response/sensitivity measurement
CMO:0003675.def: Measurement of an organism's, organ's, tissue's or cell's capacity to respond, such as by a change in activity, state or condition, to norepinephrine, a catecholamine which can act as a neurotransmitter, a stress hormone and a vasoconstrictor.

CMO:0003676.name: norepinephrine-induced blood vessel contractile force expressed as percent of force at baseline
CMO:0003676.def: A calculated measurement in which the difference between the contractile force of a blood vessel in response to a specified dosage of norepinephrine and the baseline contractile force exerted by that vessel in the absence of any external stimuli, is divided by the baseline contractile force measurement and the result expressed as a percentage. Norepinephrine is a catecholamine which can act as a neurotransmitter, a stress hormone and a vasoconstrictor.
synonyms: noradrenaline-induced blood vessel contractile force expressed as percent of force at baseline

CMO:0003677.name: logarithm of the concentration of norepinephrine at which the force of blood vessel contraction is half the maximum value
CMO:0003677.def: A calculated value for logarithm of the concentration of norepinephrine at which the energy produced by the active reduction in the diameter of a blood vessel in response to the application of norepinephrine is halfway between the baseline value and the highest achievable value of such norepinephrine-induced contractile energy. The logarithm of the concentration is the exponent indicating the power to which 10 must be raised to obtain that concentration value.
synonyms: logarithm of the concentration of noradrenaline at which the force of blood vessel contraction is half the maximum value

CMO:0003678.name: ventricular late potential
CMO:0003678.def: The VLP is a high-frequency and very-low-intensity signal that is localized at the end of QRS duration, and on the beginning part of a ST segment.

CMO:0003679.name: calculated measurement of mechanical stimulus needed to elicit evasive reaction
CMO:0003679.def: A measurement of the pressure of liquid, gas, or solid stimulus which causes the subject to take evasive action to avoid further stimulation when that measurement has been normalized, adjusted or derived by a mathematical process or computation.

CMO:0003680.name: measurement of the 50% threshold of mechanical stimulus needed to elicit evasive reaction
CMO:0003680.def: A nociception assay is used to determine the mechanical force required to elicit a paw withdrawal response in 50% of subjects. The calculation is based on the statistical formula used to determine LD50s.

CMO:0003681.name: calculated platelet aggregation measurement
CMO:0003681.def: Measurement of the ability of platelets to aggregate in response to a known platelet aggregating factor such as collagen, ADP or thrombin which has been normalized, adjusted or derived by a mathematical process or computation.

CMO:0003682.name: percentage of full platelet aggregation generated by thrombin
CMO:0003682.def: This value is calculated from an aggregometry assay curve by measuring the distance between the baseline and maximal aggregation caused by thrombin and dividing by the distance between the baseline [0% aggregation - platelet rich plasma] and 100% aggregation [platelet poor plasma].

CMO:0003683.name: renal plasma flow (inulin)
CMO:0003683.def: A measurement of the amount of plasma that perfuses the renal tubules per unit time, derived by measurement of the clearance rate of the indigestible polysaccharide inulin.

CMO:0003684.name: renal plasma flow (PAH)
CMO:0003684.def: A measurement of the amount of plasma that perfuses the renal tubules per unit time, derived by measurement of the clearance rate of the non-metabolizable solute para-aminohippurate (PAH).

CMO:0003685.name: ratio of renal plasma flow to kidney weight (inulin)
CMO:0003685.def: A calculated measurement in which the renal plasma flow rate (RPF) is divided by weight (i.e. the heaviness or the degree to which an object is drawn toward the earth by gravity) of one kidney and presented as a ratio, fraction, quotient or percentage. The RPF is the amount of plasma that perfuses the renal tubules per unit time, derived by measurement of the clearance rate of the indigestible polysaccharide inulin.
synonyms: ratio of RPF to kidney weight (inulin)

CMO:0003686.name: ratio of renal plasma flow to kidney weight (PAH)
CMO:0003686.def: A calculated measurement in which the renal plasma flow rate (RPF) is divided by weight (i.e. the heaviness or the degree to which an object is drawn toward the earth by gravity) of one kidney and presented as a ratio, fraction, quotient or percentage. The RPF is the amount of plasma that perfuses the renal tubules per unit time, derived by measurement of the clearance rate of the non-metabolizable solute para-aminohippurate (PAH).
synonyms: ratio of RPF to kidney weight (PAH)

CMO:0003687.name: percentage of study population developing ventral prostate tumorous lesions with a solid structure during a period of time
CMO:0003687.def: The number of individuals in a study population which develop new instances of ventral prostate tumorous lesions with a solid structure during a certain period of time compared to the total number of individuals in the study population, expressed as a percentage. Tumorous lesions include tumors, preneoplastic lesions, and hyperplastic lesions composed of histollogicaly normal cells.
synonyms: solid ventral prostate tumorous lesion incidence

CMO:0003688.name: percentage of study population developing ventral prostate tumorous lesions with round, irregular size nuclei during a period of time
CMO:0003688.def: The number of individuals in a study population which develop new instances of ventral prostate tumorous lesions with round, irregular size nuclei during a certain period of time compared to the total number of individuals in the study population, expressed as a percentage. Tumorous lesions include tumors, preneoplastic lesions, and hyperplastic lesions composed of histollogicaly normal cells.
synonyms: incidence of ventral prostate tumorous lesions with ACI-type nuclei

CMO:0003689.name: area of individual ventral prostate tumorous lesion with a solid structure
CMO:0003689.def: A measurement of the extent of a two-dimensional surface of or plane through an individual tumorous lesion with a solid structure in the ventral prostate. A tumorous lesion is one which is or has the potential to become a tumor, that is, a neoplasm or new growth of tissue in which cell multiplication is more or less uncontrolled and progressive. Tumorous lesions include tumors and preneoplastic lesions, as well as hyperplastic lesions composed of histologically normal cells.

CMO:0003690.name: area of individual ventral prostate tumorous lesion with round, irregular size nuclei
CMO:0003690.def: A measurement of the extent of a two-dimensional surface of or plane through an individual tumorous lesion with round, irregular size nuclei in the ventral prostate. A tumorous lesion is one which is or has the potential to become a tumor, that is, a neoplasm or new growth of tissue in which cell multiplication is more or less uncontrolled and progressive. Tumorous lesions include tumors and preneoplastic lesions, as well as hyperplastic lesions composed of histologically normal cells.
synonyms: area of individual ventral prostate tumorous lesion with ACI-type nuclei

CMO:0003691.name: area of ventral prostate occupied by tumorous lesions with solid structure to total ventral prostate area ratio
CMO:0003691.def: A calculated measurement in which the area of the ventral prostate gland occupied by tumorous lesions with solid structure is divided by the total area of the ventral prostate gland, and the result presented as a ratio, fraction, quotient or percentage. A tumorous lesion is one which is or has the potential to become a tumor, that is, a neoplasm or new growth of tissue in which cell multiplication is more or less uncontrolled and progressive. Tumorous lesions include tumors and preneoplastic lesions, as well as hyperplastic lesions composed of histologically normal cells.

CMO:0003692.name: area of ventral prostate occupied by tumorous lesions with round, irregular size nuclei to total ventral prostate area ratio
CMO:0003692.def: A calculated measurement in which the area of the ventral prostate gland occupied by tumorous lesions with round, irregular size nuclei is divided by the total area of the ventral prostate gland, and the result presented as a ratio, fraction, quotient or percentage. A tumorous lesion is one which is or has the potential to become a tumor, that is, a neoplasm or new growth of tissue in which cell multiplication is more or less uncontrolled and progressive. Tumorous lesions include tumors and preneoplastic lesions, as well as hyperplastic lesions composed of histologically normal cells.

CMO:0003693.name: number of ventral prostate tumorous lesions with solid structure
CMO:0003693.def: The number of tumorous lesions with solid structure in the ventral lobe of the prostate gland. A tumorous lesion is one which is or has the potential to become a tumor, that is, a neoplasm or new growth of tissue in which cell multiplication is more or less uncontrolled and progressive. Tumorous lesions include tumors, preneoplastic lesions, and hyperplastic lesions composed of histologically normal cells.

CMO:0003694.name: number of ventral prostate tumorous lesions with round, irregular size nuclei
CMO:0003694.def: The number of tumorous lesions with round, irregular size nuclei in the ventral lobe of the prostate gland. A tumorous lesion is one which is or has the potential to become a tumor, that is, a neoplasm or new growth of tissue in which cell multiplication is more or less uncontrolled and progressive. Tumorous lesions include tumors, preneoplastic lesions, and hyperplastic lesions composed of histologically normal cells.
synonyms: number of ventral prostate tumorous lesions with ACI-type nuclei

CMO:0003695.name: plasma plasminogen activator inhibitor 1 level
CMO:0003695.def: Measurement of the amount of plasminogen activator inhibitor 1 (PAI-1) in a specified sample of plasma, the fibrinogen-containing fluid portion of the blood in which the particulate components are suspended. PAI-1 is a serine protease inhibitor protein that functions as the principal inhibitor of tissue plasminogen activator (tPA) and urokinase (uPA), the activators of plasminogen and hence fibrinolysis (the physiological breakdown of blood clots).
synonyms: plasma serpin family E member 1 level

CMO:0003696.name: plasma Complement C3a des Arg  level
CMO:0003696.def: This is a measurement of the amount of C3a des Arg in a specified sample of plasma, the fibrinogen-containing fluid portion of the blood in which the particulate components are suspended. C3a des Arg is formed from C3a via carboxypeptidase cleavage of the C-terminal arginine group.

CMO:0003697.name: efferent arteriolar plasma flow rate
CMO:0003697.def: Volume of blood plasma delivered by a single glomerulus per unit time.

CMO:0003698.name: blood vitamin level
CMO:0003698.def: The amount of a vitamin in a specified volume of blood. A vitamin is any of various organic substances that are essential in minute quantities to the nutrition of most animals and some plants, act especially as coenzymes and precursors of coenzymes in the regulation of metabolic processes, but do not provide energy or serve as building units, and are present in natural foodstuffs or sometimes produced within the body.

CMO:0003699.name: blood metabolite measurement
CMO:0003699.def: A quantification of a parameter of a substance in the blood essential to the metabolism of a particular organism or to a particular metabolic process. In biochemistry, a metabolite is an intermediate or end product of metabolism. The term metabolite is usually used for small molecules.

CMO:0003700.name: subcutaneous tumor diameter measurement
CMO:0003700.def: The distance between two specified opposite points on the periphery of a tumor found immediately below the dermis. A tumor is an abnormal growth of tissue resulting from uncontrolled, progressive multiplication of cells and serving no physiological function.

CMO:0003701.name: subcutaneous tumor size measurement
CMO:0003701.def: Any measurement of the size of an individual tumor of the hypodermis, or of the amount of the hypodermis occupied by tumor. A tumor is an abnormal growth of tissue resulting from uncontrolled, progressive multiplication of cells and serving no physiological function.

CMO:0003702.name: photopic B wave amplitude of ERG waveform
CMO:0003702.def: Electroretinographic photopic measurement targets cone-pathway function made from the light-adapted eye. The amplitude of the b-wave is measured from the trough of the a-wave to the following peak of the b-wave. The b-wave is generated by a combination of ON- and OFF-type bipolar cells in photopic measurement.

CMO:0003703.name: ERG oscillatory potential
CMO:0003703.def: Oscillatory potentials (OPs) (four to six wavelets) can be seen on the ascending limb of most b-waves in both scotopic and photopic bright flash ERG recording. Oscillatory potentials are thought to reflect activity initiated by amacrine cells in the inner retina.

CMO:0003704.name: dose of whole thorax lung irradiation at which breathing rate increases for 50% of the total study population
CMO:0003704.def: The amount of x-radiation that is sufficient to cause lung injury (measurable as increased breathing rate) to 50 percent of a population within a certain time frame.

CMO:0003705.name: scotopic B wave amplitude of ERG waveform
CMO:0003705.def: Electroretinographic scotopic measurement targets rod-pathway function made from the dark-adapted eye. The amplitude of the b-wave is measured from the trough of the a-wave to the following peak of the b-wave.

CMO:0003706.name: scotopic A wave amplitude of ERG waveform
CMO:0003706.def: Electroretinographic scotopic measurement targets rod-pathway function made from the dark-adapted eye. The a-wave is the first large negative component of the electrical wave generated by the retina in response to light. The amplitude of the a-wave is measured from the baseline to the negative trough of the a-wave. If the stimulus light is weak, no scotopic A wave can be measured.

CMO:0003707.name: photopic A wave amplitude of ERG waveform
CMO:0003707.def: Electroretinographic photopic measurement targets cone-pathway function made from the light-adapted eye. The amplitude of the a-wave is typically measured from the pre-stimulus baseline (0 µV) to the trough of the a-wave. Under photopic (light-adapted) conditions, the a-wave is generated by cone photoreceptors, with additional contributions from OFF-type bipolar cells.

CMO:0003708.name: mean length density of glomerular capillaries
CMO:0003708.def: This is a calculated value based on the number of capillary profiles counted in microscopic images of glomerular tufts. The total calculated length of capillaries is expressed per glomerulus.
synonyms: average total length of capillaries per glomerulus

CMO:0003709.name: glomerular filtering surface area to glomerular volume ratio
CMO:0003709.def: This is a calculated value estimated from the glomerular filtering surface area of the peripheral capillary wall per unit glomerular volume. It is based on the proportion of the peripheral capillary basement membrane in contact with epithelial podocytes, as determined by microscopic measurements.
synonyms: ratio of glomerular filtering surface area to glomerular volume
surface density of the filtering surface area

CMO:0003710.name: total filtering surface area per glomerulus
CMO:0003710.def: This is a calculated value estimated from the average total glomerular filtering surface area of the peripheral capillary wall per glomerulus. It is based on the proportion of the peripheral capillary basement membrane in contact with epithelial podocytes, as determined by microscopic measurements.

CMO:0003711.name: calculated kidney glomerular podocyte measurement
CMO:0003711.def: Any measurement that has been normalized, adjusted or derived by a mathematical process or computation, of the glomerular podocytes of one or both kidneys, the paired organ which functions to maintain proper water and electrolyte balance, regulate acid-base concentration, and filter the blood of metabolic wastes.
synonyms: calculated kidney glomerular visceral epithelial cell measurement

CMO:0003712.name: total pericapillary slit length
CMO:0003712.def: This is a calculated value estimated from the glomerular filtering surface area of the peripheral capillary wall and the epithelial filtration slit frequency. The measurements for the calculations are from computerized analysis of electron micrographs.
synonyms: total glomerular visceral epithelial cell slit length

CMO:0003713.name: podocyte slit width
CMO:0003713.def: This is an average value for the gap distance between interdigitating foot processes of podocytes in kidney glomeruli. The value is derived from the measurements of podocytes during computerized analysis of electron micrographs.
synonyms: glomerular visceral epithelial cell slit width

CMO:0003714.name: podocyte foot process width
CMO:0003714.def: This is a calculated value estimated from the measurement of foot processes and an equation adjusting for ambiguity of electron microscopic images of podocyte foot process boundaries.
synonyms: glomerular visceral epithelial cell foot process width

CMO:0003715.name: podocyte foot process height
CMO:0003715.def: This is an average value of the distance between the basal side of the podocyte contacting the basement membrane and the apical side of the podocyte projecting into the urinary space. The value is derived from the measurements of podocytes during computerized analysis of electron micrographs.
synonyms: glomerular visceral epithelial cell foot process height

CMO:0003716.name: mesangium volume per glomerulus
CMO:0003716.def: This is a calculated value made by dividing the total mesangial volume measurement by the total number of glomeruli measured, both values having been determined from measurements of microscopic images. Alternately, the fractional mesangial volume (FMV) may be multiplied by the mean glomerular volume (GV) to get the total mesangial volume (TMV).

CMO:0003717.name: pulse wave velocity
CMO:0003717.def: Pulse wave velocity (PWV) is a measurement of arterial stiffness that is an independent predictor of cardiovascular risk. It can be measured simply and noninvasively by measuring the carotid and femoral pulse pressures and the time delay between the two or by other methods relying on pulse-wave analysis.

CMO:0003718.name: calculated pulse pressure measurement
CMO:0003718.def: A measurement which has been normalized, adjusted or derived by a mathematical process or computation, of pulse pressure, the difference between systolic and diastolic blood pressures.

CMO:0003719.name: mesenteric artery wall thickness
CMO:0003719.def: A measurement of the depth of the wall of a mesenteric artery, either of two arteries arising from the aorta and passing between the two layers of the mesentery to the intestine.

CMO:0003720.name: mesenteric artery media thickness
CMO:0003720.def: A measurement of the depth of the tunica media of a mesenteric artery. The tunica media is the middle layer of the mesenteric arterial wall, containing smooth muscle and elastic tissue.

CMO:0003721.name: mesenteric artery adventitial thickness
CMO:0003721.def: A measurement of the depth of the tunica adventitia of a mesenteric artery. The tunica adventitia is the outermost layer of the mesenteric arterial wall, composed mainly of fibrous tissue.

CMO:0003722.name: percentage of study population developing radiation pneumonitis during a period of time
CMO:0003722.def: The total number of subjects within a study population which develop radiation pneumonitis during a specified period of time divided by the total number of individuals in the study population, expressed as a percentage. Radiation pneumonitis is inflammation of the lung due to harmful effects of ionizing or non-ionizing radiation.

CMO:0003723.name: percentage of study population developing radiation-induced bone marrow disease during a period of time
CMO:0003723.def: The total number of subjects within a study population which develop radiation-induced bone marrow dysfunction during a specified period of time divided by the total number of individuals in the study population, expressed as a percentage. Radiation-induced bone marrow dysfunction is hematopoietic toxicity due to the harmful effects of radiation.
synonyms: incidence of radiation-induced bone marrow disease
percentage of study population developing radiation-induced bone marrow failure during a period of time

CMO:0003724.name: arteriole diameter
CMO:0003724.def: The length of a line which crosses a transverse view of an arteriole, passing through its center and ending on either side at the outer surface of the arteriole wall. An arteriole is the smallest division of the artery located between the muscular arteries and capillaries.

CMO:0003725.name: renal afferent arteriole diameter
CMO:0003725.def: The length of a line which crosses a transverse view of a renal afferent arteriole, passing through its center and ending on either side at the outer surface of the arteriole wall. A renal afferent arteriole is one of the blood vessels that branch from the kidney interlobular artery and conveys blood to the glomerular capillaries.

CMO:0003726.name: norepinephrine-induced blood vessel contractile force expressed as percent of force of contraction to KCL
CMO:0003726.def: A calculated measurement in which the difference between the contractile force of a blood vessel in response to a specified dosage of norepinephrine and the contractile force exerted by that vessel in response to a given concentration of potassium chloride, is divided by the potassium chloride contractile force measurement and the result expressed as a percentage. Norepinephrine is a catecholamine which can act as a neurotransmitter, a stress hormone and a vasoconstrictor.
synonyms: noradrenaline-induced blood vessel contractile force expressed as percent of force of contraction to KCL

CMO:0003727.name: negative logarithm of the molar concentration of norepinephrine at which the force of blood vessel contraction is half the maximum value
CMO:0003727.def: A calculated value for the negative logarithm of the concentration of norepinephrine at which the energy produced by the active reduction in the diameter of a blood vessel in response to the application of norepinephrine is half of the value of the highest achievable value of such norepinephrine-induced contractile energy. The logarithm of the concentration is the exponent indicating the power to which 10 must be raised to obtain that concentration value.
synonyms: negative logarithm of the molar concentration of noradrenaline at which the force of blood vessel contraction is half the maximum value

CMO:0003728.name: negative logarithm of the molar concentration of acetylcholine at which the reduction in force during dilation of a blood vessel is half the maximum value
CMO:0003728.def: A calculated value for the negative logarithm of the molar concentration of acetylcholine (ACh), which acts as a neurotransmitter, at which the dilation of a blood vessel in response to the application of ACh is half maximal. The logarithm of the concentration is the exponent indicating the power to which 10 must be raised to obtain that concentration value.
synonyms: acetylcholine -Log half maximal effective concentration (-Log EC50)

CMO:0003729.name: optokinetic reflex
CMO:0003729.def: This eye movement consists of two components that serve to stabilize images on the retina: a slow, pursuit phase and a fast reflex or refixation phase. Measurement of the cumulative time spent visually tracking a moving object determines the extent of the reflex. The reflex is seen when an individual follows a moving object with their eyes, which then moves out of the field of vision at which point their eye moves back to the position it was in when it first saw the object.

CMO:0003730.name: blood amino acid measurement
CMO:0003730.def: Any measurement involving the amount, composition or type of amino acid, a carboxylic acid containing one or more amino groups, in blood. Twenty alpha-amino acids are the subunits which are encoded directly by triplet codons in the genetic code and polymerized to form proteins.

CMO:0003731.name: blood arginine level
CMO:0003731.def: Measurement of the amount of arginine, an alpha-amino acid that is glycine in which the side chain (R group) is a 3-guanidinopropyl group, in blood.

CMO:0003732.name: blood asymmetric dimethylarginine level
CMO:0003732.def: Measurement of the amount of asymmetric dimethylarginine, an arginine derivative that is arginine substituted by two methyl groups, in blood. Asymmetric dimethylarginine (ADMA) is a toxic, non-proteinogenic amino acid formed by post-translational modification and is a uremic toxin that inhibits nitric oxide (NO) production. ADMA has two methyl groups bound to one nitrogen of the parental arginine molecule.

CMO:0003733.name: blood symmetric dimethylarginine level
CMO:0003733.def: Measurement of the amount of symmetric dimethylarginine, an arginine derivative that is arginine substituted by two methyl groups, in blood. Symmetric dimethylarginine (SDMA) is a toxic, non-proteinogenic amino acid formed by post-translational modification and is a uremic toxin that inhibits nitric oxide (NO) production. SDMA has two methyl groups each bound to different nitrogens of the parental arginine molecule.

CMO:0003734.name: plasma arginine level
CMO:0003734.def: Measurement of the amount of arginine, an alpha-amino acid that is glycine in which the side chain (R group) is a 3-guanidinopropyl group, in blood plasma.

CMO:0003735.name: plasma asymmetric dimethylarginine level
CMO:0003735.def: Measurement of the amount of asymmetric dimethylarginine, an arginine derivative that is arginine substituted by two methyl groups, in blood plasma.

CMO:0003736.name: plasma symmetric dimethylarginine level
CMO:0003736.def: Measurement of the amount of symmetric dimethylarginine, an arginine derivative that is arginine substituted by two methyl groups, in blood plasma.

CMO:0003737.name: calculated plasma arginine level
CMO:0003737.def: A measurement which has been normalized, adjusted or derived by a mathematical process or computation, of the amount of arginine, an alpha-amino acid that is glycine in which the side chain (R group) is a 3-guanidinopropyl group, in blood plasma, in a specified sample of plasma, the fibrinogen-containing fluid portion of the blood in which the particulate components are suspended.

CMO:0003738.name: calculated plasma asymmetric dimethylarginine level
CMO:0003738.def: A measurement which has been normalized, adjusted or derived by a mathematical process or computation, of the amount of asymmetric dimethylarginine, an arginine derivative that is arginine substituted by two methyl groups, in a specified sample of plasma, the fibrinogen-containing fluid portion of the blood in which the particulate components are suspended.

CMO:0003739.name: plasma arginine level to asymmetric dimethylarginine level ratio
CMO:0003739.def: A calculated measurement in which the value for the amount of arginine in a specified sample of plasma is divided by the value for the level of asymmetric dimethylarginine in the same sample of plasma, and the result is presented as a ratio, fraction, quotient or percentage.
synonyms: plasma arginine level to ADMA level ratio

CMO:0003740.name: heart fibrotic lesion measurement
CMO:0003740.def: Any measurement of a lesion in the heart characterized by an abnormal proliferation of fibrous connective tissue. A lesion is a localized pathological change in structure of an organ or tissue due to injury or disease; especially one that is circumscribed and well defined.

CMO:0003741.name: heart left ventricle fibrotic lesion measurement
CMO:0003741.def: Any measurement of a lesion in the left ventricle of the heart characterized by an abnormal proliferation of fibrous connective tissue. A lesion is a localized pathological change in structure of an organ or tissue due to injury or disease; especially one that is circumscribed and well defined.

CMO:0003742.name: heart left ventricle fibrotic lesion size measurement
CMO:0003742.def: This is any measurement of the physical dimensions, proportions, magnitude, or extent of a lesion in the left ventricle of the heart characterized by an abnormal proliferation of fibrous connective tissue. A lesion is a localized pathological change in structure of an organ or tissue due to injury or disease; especially one that is circumscribed and well defined.

CMO:0003743.name: heart left ventricle fibrotic lesion area measurement
CMO:0003743.def: This is a measurement of the extent of a two-dimensional surface of or plane through a single heart left ventricle fibrotic lesion, or a measurement of the total area occupied by fibrotic lesions in a cross-section of the heart left ventricle.

CMO:0003744.name: calculated heart left ventricle fibrotic lesion area measurement
CMO:0003744.def: This is a measurement of the extent of a two-dimensional surface of or plane through a single heart left ventricle fibrotic lesion, or a measurement of the total area occupied by fibrotic lesions in a cross-section of the heart left ventricle, when that value has been normalized, adjusted or derived by a mathematical process or computation.

CMO:0003745.name: heart left ventricle interstitial fibrotic lesion area to total heart left ventricule area ratio
CMO:0003745.def: This is a calculated value in which the extent of the two-dimensional surface occupied by interstitial fibrotic lesions is divided by the total extent of the two-dimensional surface of the heart left ventricle and presented as a ratio, fraction, quotient or percentage, thus normalizing it to the size of the heart left ventricle.

CMO:0003746.name: heart left ventricle perivascular fibrotic lesion area to total heart left ventricule area ratio
CMO:0003746.def: This is calculated value in which the extent of the two-dimensional surface occupied by perivascular fibrotic lesions is divided by the total extent of the two-dimensional surface of the heart left ventricle and presented as a ratio, fraction, quotient or percentage, thus normalizing it to the size of the heart left ventricle.

CMO:0003747.name: kidney interstitial fibrotic lesion area to total kidney area ratio
CMO:0003747.def: This measurement is a calculated value in which the extent of the two-dimensional area occupied by fibrotic lesions is divided by the total extent of the two-dimensional area of the kidney and presented as a ratio, fraction, quotient or percentage, thus normalizing it to the size of the kidney. The two-dimensional measurements are made on microscopic images.
synonyms: kidney fibrotic lesion cross-sectional area to total kidney cross-sectional area ratio

CMO:0003748.name: glomerular volume per podocyte
CMO:0003748.def: A calculated measurement in which the average volume of kidney glomeruli is divided by the average number of podocytes in a glomerulus. It represents the reciprocal value of 'number of podocytes to glomerular volume ratio (CMO:0002955).

CMO:0003749.name: Darcy permeability
CMO:0003749.def: This measurement defines the capacity of a porous material to transmit fluids. Darcy's law is an equation that describes the flow of a fluid through a porous medium. The calculation in biological systems relies on a pressure gradient, the thickness of the material through which the fluid is proceeding, and the dynamic viscosity of the filtration solution.

CMO:0003750.name: volume of glomerular capillary tuft not affected by sclerosis
CMO:0003750.def: Calculated value for average volume of glomerular capillary tuft not affected by sclerotic changes in sampled subjects.
synonyms: volume of normal glomerular capillary tuft

CMO:0003751.name: volume of glomerular capillary tuft occupied by sclerosis
CMO:0003751.def: Calculated value for average volume of glomerular capillary tuft occupied by sclerotic changes in sampled subjects.

CMO:0003752.name: volume of kidney cortical interstitium to total volume of kidney cortex ratio
CMO:0003752.def: A calculated measurement in which the average volume of interstitial space in the renal cortex is divided by the average total volume of the renal cortex and the result presented as a ratio, fraction, quotient or percentage, thus normalizing it to kidney cortical volume and, by extension, to the size of the kidney.
synonyms: volume of interstitial kidney cortex to total volume of kidney cortex ratio

CMO:0003753.name: blood lipase activity level
CMO:0003753.def: Any quantitation of the catalytic effect exerted by lipase in a specified sample of blood. Lipase, is an enzyme that catalyzes the hydrolysis of lipids. It's normal to have a small amount of lipase in blood, but a high level of lipase can mean the subject has some type of pancreatic disease.

CMO:0003754.name: serum lipase activity level
CMO:0003754.def: Any quantitation of the catalytic effect exerted by lipase in a specified sample of blood serum. Lipase, is an enzyme that catalyzes the hydrolysis of lipids. It's normal to have a small amount of lipase in blood, but a high level of lipase can mean the subject has some type of pancreatic disease.

CMO:0003755.name: plasma lipase activity level
CMO:0003755.def: Any quantitation of the catalytic effect exerted by lipase in a specified sample of blood plasma. Lipase, is an enzyme that catalyzes the hydrolysis of lipids. It's normal to have a small amount of lipase in blood, but a high level of lipase can mean the subject has some type of pancreatic disease.

CMO:0003756.name: heart left ventricle infarction area to total heart left ventricle area ratio
CMO:0003756.def: A calculated measurement in which the area of a heart left ventricle infarction is divided by the total area of the heart left ventricle, and the result presented as a ratio, fraction, quotient or percentage, thus normalizing it to heart left ventricle size and, by extension, to the size of the heart.

CMO:0003757.name: increase in liver tumorous lesion volume between two points in time
CMO:0003757.def: A calculated value in which the volume of the liver occupied by tumorous lesions at a point in time is subtracted from the volume of the liver occupied by tumorous lesions at a later point in time.
synonyms: effective tumor growth between two points in time

CMO:0003758.name: subsequent liver tumorous lesion volume to precedent liver tumorous lesion volume ratio
CMO:0003758.def: A calculated value in which the volume of the liver occupied by tumorous lesions at a second point in time is divided by the volume of the liver occupied by tumorous lesions at previous point in time and presented as a ratio, fraction or quotient, thus standardizing the growth of the tumorous lesions.

CMO:0003759.name: liver volume after excision and regeneration
CMO:0003759.def: Measurement of the size of the three dimensional space occupied by one or more lobes of the liver after removal and subsequent regrowth. The liver is the large abdominal organ/gland which functions in the storage and filtration of blood, secretion of bile, and other processes.
synonyms: liver volume after partial excision and regeneration

CMO:0003760.name: post excision/regeneration liver volume to original liver volume ratio
CMO:0003760.def: A calculated measurement in which the size of the three dimensional space (volume) occupied by one or more lobes of the liver after excision and subsequent regeneration is divided by the original, preoperative volume and presented as a ratio, fraction, quotient or percentage.

CMO:0003761.name: number of contractions above 10 mmHg of anorectal pressure during a specified time
CMO:0003761.def: Measurement of cyclical rising of pressure in the anorectum as a result of anal sphincter action over a designated period of time.

CMO:0003762.name: intestine physiological measurement
CMO:0003762.def: Any quantification of a function or process of intestine, that is, a parameter related to the way the intestine operates and/or the chemical or physical functions that exist in the intestine, the portion of the alimentary canal extending from the pyloric opening of the stomach to the anus.

CMO:0003763.name: duration of contractions above 10 mmHg of anorectal pressure
CMO:0003763.def: Measurement of the time from start to finish of a sphincter contraction causing anorectal pressure above 10 mmHg, calculated from a set of measurements taken from multiple contractions during a designated period of time.

CMO:0003764.name: frequency of contractions above 10 mmHg of anorectal pressure
CMO:0003764.def: Measurement of the number of instances of pressure in the anorectum going over a designated level, as a result of anal sphincter action, per unit of time.
synonyms: ratio of contractions per unit time

CMO:0003765.name: time to peak anorectal sphincter contraction
CMO:0003765.def: Measurement of the time from the beginning of anorectal sphincter contraction to the maximum achieved pressure.

CMO:0003766.name: number of peaks in pressure per anorectal sphincter contraction
CMO:0003766.def: Measurement of the count of fasciculation-producing peaks in pressure generated during an anorectal sphincter contraction.
synonyms: number of twitchesks in per anorectal sphincter contraction

CMO:0003767.name: calculated anorectal physiological measurement
CMO:0003767.def: A measurement which has been normalized, adjusted or derived by a mathematical process or computation, of some parameter of anorectal physiology.

CMO:0003768.name: range of pressure generated by anorectal contractions
CMO:0003768.def: A calculated value in which the lowest measured pressure is subtracted from the highest measured pressure from stabilized anorectal contractions in the same subject.

CMO:0003769.name: area under the anorectal pressure curve
CMO:0003769.def: This measurement involves calculation of the the area under the plotted curve for pressure generated by anorectal contractions.

CMO:0003770.name: red blood cell sodium level
CMO:0003770.def: The intracellular concentration of sodium ions measured in a specific sample of red blood cells.

CMO:0003771.name: red blood cell potassium level
CMO:0003771.def: The intracellular concentration of potassium ions measured in a specific sample of red blood cells

CMO:0003772.name: red blood cell ATP level
CMO:0003772.def: The intracellular concentration of adenosine-5'- triphosphate measured in a specific sample of red blood cells.

CMO:0003773.name: red blood cell Na-K-Cl cotransport activity
CMO:0003773.def: Measurement of the level of activity of the erythrocyte membrane transport protein that transports sodium (Na), potassium (K), and chloride (Cl) ions across the cell membrane into erythrocytes. For every sodium and potassium ion transported, this symporter transports two chloride ions, thus maintaining electroneutrality.

CMO:0003774.name: red blood cell sodium/potassium passive permeability
CMO:0003774.def: This is a measurement of sodium and/or potassium ion efflux from erythrocytes in the presence of a sodium-potassium pump inhibitor (ouabain) and a sodium-potassium-chloride cotransporter inhibitor (furosemide or bumetamide).

CMO:0003775.name: number of small metastatic liver tumors in the right liver
CMO:0003775.def: A value or quantity determined by count of small (< 1 mm) metastatic tumors in the right lobes (right lobes and caudate lobes) of the liver. A metastatic tumor in the liver is a secondary, abnormal growth of tissue resulting from the spread of cancer cells to the liver from the place where they first formed.
synonyms: count of micrometastases in the right liver
count of micrometastases in the right liver < 1 mm
number of micrometastases in the right liver

CMO:0003776.name: number of small metastatic liver tumors in the left liver
CMO:0003776.def: A value or quantity determined by count of small (< 1 mm) metastatic tumors in the left lobes (left lateral lobe and median lobes in rat) of the liver. A metastatic tumor in the liver is a secondary, abnormal growth of tissue resulting from the spread of cancer cells to the liver from the place where they first formed.
synonyms: count of metastases in the left liver < 1 mm
count of micrometastases in the left liver
number of micrometastases in the left liver

CMO:0003777.name: small liver metastatic tumorous lesion diameter measurement
CMO:0003777.def: The distance (< 1 mm) between two specified opposite points on the periphery of a micrometastatic tumorous lesion found on or in the liver. A micrometastatic tumorous lesion is one that is or has the potential to become a tumor, that is, a neoplasm or new growth of tissue in which cell multiplication is more or less uncontrolled and progressive. Tumorous lesions include tumors, preneoplastic lesions, and hyperplastic lesions composed of histologically normal cells.
synonyms: liver micrometastatic tumorous lesion diameter measurement

CMO:0003778.name: large liver metastatic tumorous lesion diameter measurement
CMO:0003778.def: The distance (> 3 mm) between two specified opposite points on the periphery of a macrometastatic tumorous lesion found on or in the liver. A macrometastatic tumorous lesion is one that is or has the potential to become a tumor, that is, a neoplasm or new growth of tissue in which cell multiplication is more or less uncontrolled and progressive. Tumorous lesions include tumors, preneoplastic lesions, and hyperplastic lesions composed of histologically normal cells.
synonyms: liver macrometastatic tumorous lesion diameter measurement

CMO:0003779.name: medium-sized liver metastatic tumorous lesion diameter measurement
CMO:0003779.def: The distance ( 1-3 mm) between two specified opposite points on the periphery of a micrometastatic tumorous lesion found on or in the liver. A micrometastatic tumorous lesion is one that is or has the potential to become a tumor, that is, a neoplasm or new growth of tissue in which cell multiplication is more or less uncontrolled and progressive. Tumorous lesions include tumors, preneoplastic lesions, and hyperplastic lesions composed of histologically normal cell
synonyms: liver micrometastatic tumorous lesion diameter measurement

CMO:0003780.name: percentage of study population developing peritoneal carcinomatosis during a period of time
CMO:0003780.def: The total number of subjects within a study population which develop peritoneal carcinomatosis during a specified period of time divided by the total number of individuals in the study population, expressed as a percentage. Peritoneal carcinomatosis is multiple tumorsusually metastatic, growing in or on the peritoneum, a serous membrane that lines the peritoneal cavity .

CMO:0003781.name: number of large metastatic liver tumors in the left liver
CMO:0003781.def: A value or quantity determined by count of large ( > 3 mm) metastatic tumors in the left lobes (left lateral lobe and median lobes in rat) of the liver. A metastatic tumor in the liver is a secondary, abnormal growth of tissue resulting from the spread of cancer cells to the liver from the place where they first formed.
synonyms: count of macrometastases in the left liver
count of metastases in the left liver > 3 mm
number of macrometastases in the left liver

CMO:0003782.name: number of large metastatic liver tumors in the right liver
CMO:0003782.def: A value or quantity determined by count of large (> 3 mm) metastatic tumors in the right lobes (right lobes and caudate lobes) of the liver. A metastatic tumor in the liver is a secondary, abnormal growth of tissue resulting from the spread of cancer cells to the liver from the place where they first formed.
synonyms: count of macrometastases in the right liver
count of metastases in the right liver > 3 mm
number of macrometastases in the right liver

CMO:0003783.name: pancreatic islet insulin output
CMO:0003783.def: A calculated measure of the amount of insulin secretion from a single pancreatic islet per unit of time.
synonyms: pancreatic islet insulin output per unit time

CMO:0003784.name: percentage of study population developing ascites during a period of time
CMO:0003784.def: The total number of subjects within a study population which develop ascites during a specified period of time divided by the total number of individuals in the study population, expressed as a percentage. Ascites is the pathological accumulation or retention of free fluid within the peritoneal cavity.
synonyms: percentage of study population developing abdominal dropsy during a period of time
percentage of study population developing excess abdominal fluid during a period of time
percentage of study population developing hydroperitoneum during a period of time
percentage of study population developing hydroperitonia during a period of time

CMO:0003785.name: percentage of study population developing extra-hepatic metastases during a period of time
CMO:0003785.def: The number of subjects developing extra-hepatic metastases in a study population during a certain period compared to the total number of subjects in the study population, expressed as a percentage. An extra-hepatic metastasis is a neoplasm transferred from one organ or part of the body to another (not liver) remote from the primary site.

CMO:0003786.name: calculated blood CD25 cell count
CMO:0003786.def: A measurement which has been normalized, adjusted or derived by a mathematical process or computation, of the number of lymphocytes expressing the CD25 antigen on their surface in a specified sample of blood.

CMO:0003787.name: debris zone thickness
CMO:0003787.def: Measurement of the thickness of a buildup of an autofluorescent layer containing the nonphagocytosed photoreceptor outer segment (POS) debris in the subretinal space of subjects with retinal disease. The debris zone is located between the outer nuclear layer (ONL) and the retinal pigmented epithelium (RPE).

CMO:0003788.name: amount of time spent making head dipping movements during experiment in an elevated plus maze
CMO:0003788.def: This is a measure of the total amount of time during an experiment in an elevated plus maze that a subject spends making intentional downward movements of its head.
synonyms: amount of time spent making head dipping movements during experiment in an EPM
total amount of time spent making head dipping movements during experiment in an elevated plus maze
total amount of time spent making head dipping movements during experiment in an EPM

CMO:0003789.name: time to first grooming within an experimental apparatus
CMO:0003789.def: A measurement of the latency period spent by an organism or experimental subject in an experimental apparatus before starting any activity of self-cleaning or cleaning another subject.
synonyms: grooming latency within an experimental apparatus

CMO:0003790.name: amount of time spent making rearing movements in an experimental apparatus
CMO:0003790.def: The total amount of time in an experiment that a quadrupedal subject spends in a distinct and specified area of a piece of technical equipment or machinery, an appliance, or a device designed for a particular purpose, rising up on its back legs.

CMO:0003791.name: time to first rearing within an experimental apparatus
CMO:0003791.def: This is a measurement of the latency period spent by an experimental, quadrupedal subject in an experimental apparatus before rising up on its back legs.

CMO:0003792.name: head movement measurement
CMO:0003792.def: Any measurable or observable characteristic related to the motion of the head which originated, or was undertaken, controlled, or accomplished as a result of an organism's free will or choice.

CMO:0003793.name: head dip measurement
CMO:0003793.def: Any measurable or observable characteristic related to a downward motion of the head which originated, or was undertaken, controlled, or accomplished as a result of an organism's free will or choice.

CMO:0003794.name: number of head dipping movements in an experimental apparatus
CMO:0003794.def: A value or quantity determined by count of how many times a quadrupedal subject in a piece of technical equipment or machinery, an appliance, or a device designed for a particular purpose moves its head purposefully in a downward motion.

CMO:0003795.name: time to first head dip within an experimental apparatus
CMO:0003795.def: This is a measurement of the latency period spent by an subject in an experimental apparatus before starting any intentional downward motion of the head.
synonyms: time to first head dips within an experimental apparatus

CMO:0003796.name: amount of time spent making head dipping movements in an experimental apparatus
CMO:0003796.def: The total amount of time in an experiment that a subject spends in a distinct and specified area of a piece of technical equipment or machinery, an appliance, or a device designed for a particular purpose, making intentional downward movements of its head.

CMO:0003797.name: number of glomeruli per kidney
CMO:0003797.def: The number of glomeruli calculated to be in one kidney from a measured sample of that kidney. Glomeruli are the tufts of capillaries each situated within a Bowman's capsule at the end of a renal tubule in the vertebrate kidney that filter waste products from the blood and thus initiate urine formation.

CMO:0003798.name: calculated kidney glomerulus count
CMO:0003798.def: Any count that has been normalized, adjusted or derived by a mathematical process or computation, of the glomeruli of one or both kidneys, the paired organ which functions to maintain proper water and electrolyte balance, regulate acid-base concentration, and filter the blood of metabolic wastes.

CMO:0003799.name: number of glomeruli per volume of kidney
CMO:0003799.def: A count that has been normalized, adjusted or derived by a mathematical process or computation, of the glomeruli in a given volume of kidney tissue.
synonyms: number of kidney glomeruli per volume of tissue

CMO:0003800.name: ratio of deaths related to chronic hypertension to total study population during a period of time
CMO:0003800.def: A measure of the total number of deaths related to chronic hypertension occurring during a specified period of time within a study population divided by the total number of individuals in the study population and presented as a ratio, fraction, quotient or percentage.
synonyms: incidence of deaths related to chronic hypertension

CMO:0003801.name: ratio of deaths related to mammary cancer to total study population during a period of time
CMO:0003801.def: A measure of the total number of deaths related to mammary cancer occurring during a specified period of time within a study population divided by the total number of individuals in the study population and presented as a ratio, fraction, quotient or percentage.
synonyms: incidence of deaths related to mammary cancer

CMO:0003802.name: ratio of deaths related to experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis to total study population during a period of time
CMO:0003802.def: A measure of the total number of deaths related to experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis occurring during a specified period of time within a study population divided by the total number of individuals in the study population and presented as a ratio, fraction, quotient or percentage.
synonyms: incidence of deaths related to experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis

CMO:0003803.name: ratio of survivors of metabolic syndrome to total study population during a period of time
CMO:0003803.def: This is a measure of the total number of metabolic syndrome subjects within a study population which remain alive during a specified period of time divided by the total number of individuals in the study population, presented as a ratio, fraction, quotient or percentage.
synonyms: percentage of metabolic syndrome survivors in a study population during a period of time

CMO:0003804.name: amount of time spent making stretched attend posture movements in an experimental apparatus
CMO:0003804.def: This is a measurement of the total amount of time in an experiment that a quadrupedal subject spends in a piece of technical equipment or machinery, an appliance, or a device designed for a particular purpose, making stretched attend posture movements, in which the hind legs remain stationary while the body is stretched forward with head raised.
synonyms: amount of time spent making stretch attend posture movements in an experimental apparatus

CMO:0003805.name: time to first stretched attend posture movement in an experimental apparatus
CMO:0003805.def: This is a measurement of the latency period spent by an subject in an experimental apparatus before starting any stretched-attend posture movement.
synonyms: time to first stretched attend posture movement within an experimental apparatus

CMO:0003806.name: exploratory movement measurement
CMO:0003806.def: A measurement of time, movement type, or location of a subject's exploration of an object, location, or other entity.

CMO:0003807.name: amount of time spent exploring a novel object in an experimental apparatus
CMO:0003807.def: The total amount of time in an experiment that a subject spends in a piece of technical equipment or machinery, an appliance, or a device designed for a particular purpose, exploring a novel object.

CMO:0003808.name: amount of time spent exploring a familiar object in an experimental apparatus
CMO:0003808.def: The total amount of time in an experiment that a subject spends in a piece of technical equipment or machinery, an appliance, or a device designed for a particular purpose, exploring a familiar object.

CMO:0003809.name: ratio of deaths related to DMBA toxicity to total study population during a period of time
CMO:0003809.def: A measure of the total number of deaths related to 7,12-Dimethylbenz(a)anthracene (DMBA) toxicity occurring during a specified period of time within a study population divided by the total number of individuals in the study population and presented as a ratio, fraction, quotient or percentage.
synonyms: ratio of deaths related to 7,12-Dimethylbenz(a)anthracene toxicity to total study population during a period of time

CMO:0003810.name: ratio of deaths related to left ventricular hypertrophy to total study population during a period of time
CMO:0003810.def: A measure of the total number of deaths related to left ventricular hypertrophy occurring during a specified period of time within a study population divided by the total number of individuals in the study population and presented as a ratio, fraction, quotient or percentage.
synonyms: incidence of deaths related to left ventricular hypertrophy

CMO:0003811.name: renal cortex morphological measurement
CMO:0003811.def: Measurement of the physical form or structure of the renal cortex, the outer part of the kidney, composed mainly of glomeruli and convoluted tubules.

CMO:0003812.name: renal cortex cross-sectional area
CMO:0003812.def: A measurement of the outer extent of a plane perpendicular through the hilum, the opening on the medial margin of the kidney leading into the renal sinus. Its value may be calculated from or measured via a microscopic image.

CMO:0003813.name: carotid artery blood flow velocity
CMO:0003813.def: Measurement of average carotid artery blood flow velocity, the speed with which blood moves along the circulation in any particular segment of carotid artery. Blood flow velocity is related directly to blood flow and inversely to cross-sectional area. Blood flow velocity can be measured indirectly by Doppler ultrasound
synonyms: mean carotid artery blood flow velocity

CMO:0003814.name: peak carotid artery blood flow velocity
CMO:0003814.def: Measurement of peak carotid artery blood flow velocity, the top speed (systolic) with which blood moves along the circulation in any particular segment of carotid artery. Blood flow velocity is related directly to blood flow and inversely to cross-sectional area. Blood flow velocity can be measured indirectly by Doppler ultrasound

CMO:0003815.name: cerebral blood flow rate
CMO:0003815.def: Cerebral blood flow (CBF) rate is the volume of blood delivered to or exiting the brain, through a network of cerebral arteries and veins, per unit time

CMO:0003816.name: number of blastocysts implanted per litter
CMO:0003816.def: This is the number, i.e., the quantity determined by count, of implanted blastocysts, products of one gestation produced during one pregnancy in a multiparous mammal.

CMO:0003817.name: number of fetuses with external malformations to total number of live fetuses ratio
CMO:0003817.def: A calculated measurement in which the number of fetuses with external malformations is divided by the total number of live fetuses in the prospective litter, and the result presented as a ratio, fraction, quotient or percentage.
synonyms: percent of fetuses with external malformations

CMO:0003818.name: calculated offspring mortality measurement
CMO:0003818.def: Any measurement which has been normalized, adjusted or derived by a mathematical process or computation, of the number of dead offspring in a litter or prospective litter. A litter or prospective litter refers to the products of one gestation produced by a multiparous mammal.

CMO:0003819.name: number of fetuses with exencephaly to total number of live fetuses ratio
CMO:0003819.def: A calculated measurement in which the number of fetuses with exencephaly is divided by the total number of live fetuses in the prospective litter, and the result presented as a ratio, fraction, quotient or percentage. Exencephaly is a rare malformation of the neural tube with a large amount of protruding brain tissue and absence of calvarium.
synonyms: percent of fetuses with protruding brain tissue and absence of calvarium

CMO:0003820.name: number of fetuses with brain hernia to total number of live fetuses ratio
CMO:0003820.def: A calculated measurement in which the number of fetuses with brain hernia is divided by the total number of live fetuses in the prospective litter, and the result presented as a ratio, fraction, quotient or percentage. Fetal brain tissue herniation occurs through a congenital defect in the skull.

CMO:0003821.name: number of fetuses with eye malformations to total number of live fetuses ratio
CMO:0003821.def: A calculated measurement in which the number of fetuses with eye malformations is divided by the total number of live fetuses in the prospective litter, and the result presented as a ratio, fraction, quotient or percentage. The eye malformations may include anophthalmia, microphthalmia, etc.

CMO:0003822.name: number of fetuses with visceral malformations to total number of fetuses ratio
CMO:0003822.def: A calculated measurement in which the number of fetuses with visceral malformations is divided by the total number of fetuses in the prospective litter, and the result presented as a ratio, fraction, quotient or percentage.
synonyms: percent of fetuses with internal malformations
percent of fetuses with visceral malformations

CMO:0003823.name: number of fetuses with hydrocephaly to total number of fetuses ratio
CMO:0003823.def: A calculated measurement in which the number of fetuses with hydrocephaly is divided by the total number of fetuses in the prospective litter, and the result presented as a ratio, fraction, quotient or percentage. Hydrocephaly is characterized by an abnormal accumulation of cerebrospinal fluid in the ventricles of the brain.

CMO:0003824.name: number of fetuses with cardiovascular malformations to total number of fetuses ratio
CMO:0003824.def: A calculated measurement in which the number of fetuses with cardiovascular malformations is divided by the total number of fetuses in the prospective litter, and the result presented as a ratio, fraction, quotient or percentage. Cardiovascular malformations include conditions such as ventricular septal defect, common atrioventricular canal, transposition of great arteries, and right aortic arch.
synonyms: percent of fetuses with cardiovascular malformations

CMO:0003825.name: number of fetuses with renal malformations to total number of fetuses ratio
CMO:0003825.def: A calculated measurement in which the number of fetuses with renal malformations is divided by the total number of fetuses in the prospective litter, and the result presented as a ratio, fraction, quotient or percentage.
synonyms: number of fetuses with malformation of kidneys to total number of fetuses ratio
percent of fetuses with renal malformations

CMO:0003826.name: number of fetuses with left umbilical artery to total number of fetuses ratio
CMO:0003826.def: A calculated measurement in which the number of fetuses with left umbilical artery is divided by the total number of fetuses in the prospective litter, and the result presented as a ratio, fraction, quotient or percentage. In a rat fetus the right umbilical artery tends to remain patent while the left becomes closed near the end of gestation.
synonyms: percent of fetuses with left umbilical artery

CMO:0003827.name: number of fetuses with skeletal malformations to total number of fetuses ratio
CMO:0003827.def: A calculated measurement in which the number of fetuses with skeletal malformations is divided by the total number of fetuses in the prospective litter, and the result presented as a ratio, fraction, quotient or percentage.
synonyms: percent of fetuses with malformations of the skeleton
percent of fetuses with skeletal malformations

CMO:0003828.name: number of fetuses with cranial malformations to total number of fetuses ratio
CMO:0003828.def: A calculated measurement in which the number of fetuses with cranial malformations is divided by the total number of fetuses in the prospective litter, and the result presented as a ratio, fraction, quotient or percentage.
synonyms: percent of fetuses with cranial malformations
percent of fetuses with malformations of the cranium

CMO:0003829.name: number of fetuses with vertebral malformations to total number of fetuses ratio
CMO:0003829.def: A calculated measurement in which the number of fetuses with one or more vertebral malformations is divided by the total number of fetuses in the prospective litter, and the result presented as a ratio, fraction, quotient or percentage.
synonyms: percent of fetuses with malformations of the vertebrae
percent of fetuses with vertebral malformations

CMO:0003830.name: number of fetuses with skeletal variations to total number of fetuses ratio
CMO:0003830.def: This is a calculated measurement in which the number of fetuses with skeletal variations is divided by the total number of fetuses in the prospective litter, and the result presented as a ratio, fraction, quotient or percentage.
synonyms: percent of fetuses with skeletal variations
percent of fetuses with variations of the skeleton

CMO:0003831.name: number of fetuses with sternum variations to total number of fetuses ratio
CMO:0003831.def: This is a calculated measurement in which the number of fetuses with sternum variations is divided by the total number of fetuses in the prospective litter, and the result presented as a ratio, fraction, quotient or percentage.
synonyms: percent of fetuses with sternum variations
percent of fetuses with variations of the sternum

CMO:0003832.name: number of fetuses with cervical rib variations to total number of fetuses ratio
CMO:0003832.def: This is a calculated measurement in which the number of fetuses with cervical rib variations is divided by the total number of fetuses in the prospective litter, and the result presented as a ratio, fraction, quotient or percentage.
synonyms: percent of fetuses with cervical rib variations
percent of fetuses with variations of the cervical ribs

CMO:0003833.name: number of fetuses with lumbar rib variations to total number of fetuses ratio
CMO:0003833.def: This is a calculated measurement in which the number of fetuses with lumbar rib variations is divided by the total number of fetuses in the prospective litter, and the result presented as a ratio, fraction, quotient or percentage.
synonyms: percent of fetuses with lumbar rib variations
percent of fetuses with variations of the lumbar ribs

CMO:0003834.name: number of fetuses with an ossified anterior arch of atlas to total number of fetuses ratio
CMO:0003834.def: This is a calculated measurement in which the number of fetuses with an ossified anterior arch of atlas is divided by the total number of fetuses in the prospective litter, and the result presented as a ratio, fraction, quotient or percentage.
synonyms: percent of fetuses with an ossified anterior arch of atlas
percent of fetuses with ossification of the anterior arch of atlas

CMO:0003835.name: number of fetuses without an ossified first cervical vertebral body to total number of fetuses ratio
CMO:0003835.def: This is a calculated measurement in which the number of fetuses without an ossified first cervical vertebral body is divided by the total number of fetuses in the prospective litter, and the result presented as a ratio, fraction, quotient or percentage.
synonyms: percent of fetuses without an ossified first cervical vertebral body
percent of fetuses without ossification of the first cervical vertebral body

CMO:0003836.name: post-insult time of death from IgM immunocytoma
CMO:0003836.def: This is a measurement of the length of time between introduction of an IgM immunocytoma and the death of the subject, i.e. the cessation of all vital functions of the body including the heartbeat, brain activity (including the brain stem), and breathing.
synonyms: post-insult time of death from IgM lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma

CMO:0003837.name: calculated capillary measurement
CMO:0003837.def: Any measurement which has been normalized or adjusted by a mathematical process or computation of the minute vessels connecting arterioles and venules, the walls of which act as a semipermeable membrane for interchange of various substances between the blood and tissue fluid.

CMO:0003838.name: number of capillaries per cross-sectional area of left ventricular myocardium
CMO:0003838.def: A calculated number of capillaries associated with a sampled cross-sectional area of left ventricular myocardium, the muscular layer of the ventricle. Capillaries are the minute vessels connecting arterioles and venules, the walls of which act as a semipermeable membrane for interchange of various substances between the blood and tissue fluid.

CMO:0003839.name: total horizontal distance resulting from voluntary locomotion in pursuit of a target in an experimental apparatus
CMO:0003839.def: Measurement of the linear equivalent of the extent of forward progress attained via the movement of an individual along a plane parallel to the plane of the horizon in pursuit of a target in a piece of technical equipment or machinery, or in an appliance or device designed for a particular purpose originated, undertaken, controlled, or accomplished as a result of free will or choice.
synonyms: total horizontal distance resulting from voluntary locomotion in pursuit of a platform in a Morris water maze

CMO:0003840.name: cardiac myocyte cross-sectional area
CMO:0003840.def: A measurement of the extent of a plane through, that is, perpendicular to the axis of, a cardiac myocyte, striated muscle cells that are responsible for heart contraction. In mammals, the contractile fiber resembles those of skeletal muscle but are only one third as large in diameter, are richer in sarcoplasm, and contain centrally located instead of peripheral nuclei.
synonyms: striated cardiac muscle cell cross-sectional area

CMO:0003841.name: serum non-high density lipoprotein cholesterol level
CMO:0003841.def: This is a calculated measurement in which the value for high density lipoprotein (HDL) cholesterol in a specified sample of serum is subtracted from the value for total cholesterol in that same sample. HDL is the smallest of the major lipoprotein particles, complex molecules that consist of a protein membrane surrounding a core of lipids

CMO:0003842.name: hepatic extraction fraction
CMO:0003842.def: This is the fraction of a drug entering the liver in the blood which is irreversibly removed (extracted) during one pass of the blood through the liver. The hepatic extraction fraction (HEF) depends on the hepatic blood flow, uptake into hepatocytes, and enzyme metabolism. HEF can be calculated using deconvolution analysis of the liver using scintigraphic data.

CMO:0003843.name: liver physiological measurement
CMO:0003843.def: Any measurement relating to the function of the liver or any part thereof. The liver functions in the detoxification of xenobiotics, synthesis and storage of glycogen, synthesis and breakdown of fats and temporary storage of fatty acids, and synthesis of serum proteins.

CMO:0003844.name: calculated liver physiological measurement
CMO:0003844.def: A measurement of any functional parameter in a specified sample of liver, when that measurement has been normalized, adjusted or derived by a mathematical process or computation.

CMO:0003845.name: urine 8-hydroxy-2'-deoxyguanosine level
CMO:0003845.def: This is a common oxidized form of deoxyguanosine in which the C-8 position of the guanine base has a carbonyl group. It is used as a biomarker of oxidative DNA damage.

CMO:0003846.name: hepatic extraction fraction
CMO:0003846.def: This is the fraction of a drug entering the liver from the blood which is irreversibly removed (extracted) during one pass of the blood through the liver. The hepatic extraction fraction (HEF) depends on the hepatic blood flow, uptake into hepatocytes, and enzyme metabolism.
